record-handling-hoare-1965.name: Record Handling (Hoare)
record-handling-hoare-1965.definition: Hoare's 1965 proposal for representing complex structured objects in an ALGOL 60 extension: dynamically created records belonging to declared record classes, fields declared in the class, class-qualified references, and subclasses - the record-class half of what Simula 67 fused with the ALGOL block.
record-handling-hoare-1965.bottleneck: Before Hoare's proposal, structured data in a general-purpose language was ad-hoc: arrays and pointer conventions with no declared kind of object, no fields fixed by a class declaration, and no reference qualified by the class it may point to.
record-handling-hoare-1965.leap: Hoare's Record Handling (WG 2.1 Working Paper, Oct 1965; ALGOL Bulletin 21.3.6) proposes record classes: declare a kind of object once, create and destroy its records dynamically, access fields by dot notation, and qualify references by class - with subclasses as specializations.
record-handling-hoare-1965.prior_state: ALGOL 60's scalars and arrays; application-specific record layouts in assembly and FORTRAN.

list-structured-free-store-for-block-ins.name: List-structured free store for block instances (Dahl)
list-structured-free-store-for-block-ins.definition: Dahl's storage management package (completed by May 1963) allocating block instances from a two-dimensional free area list, with reference counts and a last-resort garbage collector, freeing block instances from ALGOL's stack discipline.
list-structured-free-store-for-block-ins.bottleneck: Before Dahl's free store, an ALGOL block instance could not outlive its caller: the stack discipline made persistent, independently referenced program components impossible.
list-structured-free-store-for-block-ins.leap: A storage regime in which block instances have independent existence - allocated from a free store, referenced explicitly, reclaimed by reference counts and garbage collection - the mechanism Simula's processes and later objects stand on.
list-structured-free-store-for-block-ins.prior_state: Strict LIFO stack allocation of block instances in ALGOL implementations.

logo-1967.name: Logo
logo-1967.definition: Feurzeig, Papert & Solomon's language for children (BBN, 1967): an interactive, radically simple language (turtle geometry) proving children could program and think with computers.
logo-1967.bottleneck: Before Logo, programming was held to be an adult professional skill; no working language existed that a child could use to think with.
logo-1967.leap: Logo proves the demand and the possibility: children programming as a medium for learning - the audience and the standard of simplicity every later children's language is measured against.
logo-1967.prior_state: Drill-and-practice computer-aided instruction; BASIC in a few schools.

flex-language-and-machine-kay-1969.name: FLEX language and machine (Kay)
flex-language-and-machine-kay-1969.definition: Kay's extensible kernel language and personal machine (notes 1967; MSc 1968; PhD thesis 'The Reactive Engine', Utah, 1969): an Euler-like, interactive, self-extending language with object-oriented aspects, designed to be executed directly by a small personal computer; compiled by others for the Univac 1108 and the SDS 940.
flex-language-and-machine-kay-1969.bottleneck: Before FLEX, no design joined a small extensible interactive language to a personal machine that executes it directly: languages belonged to institutions' batch and timesharing systems.
flex-language-and-machine-kay-1969.leap: FLEX: a language as the kernel of a personal computer - interactive, extensible by its users, with objects avant la lettre; the design stock (and the research programme) Kay carried to PARC.
flex-language-and-machine-kay-1969.prior_state: JOSS-style timesharing interactivity without extensibility; Euler without a machine; batch personal computing nonexistent.

gsm8k-benchmark-of-math-word-problems-co.name: GSM8K benchmark of math word problems (Cobbe et al., 2021)

gsm8k-benchmark-of-math-word-problems-co.prior_state: MAWPS/ASDiv-era sets: small, templated, and (per Patel et al. 2021) substantially solvable by heuristics.

coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure-res.name: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure (responsible disclosure practice in computer security)

namespaces-in-xml-w3c-recommendation-199.name: Namespaces in XML (W3C Recommendation, 1999)
namespaces-in-xml-w3c-recommendation-199.definition: The W3C Recommendation of January 1999 defining namespaces in XML - the mechanism by which element and attribute names are partitioned among vocabularies.
namespaces-in-xml-w3c-recommendation-199.bottleneck: Before Namespaces in XML, names from different vocabularies collided in one flat space, because XML 1.0 had no partitioning mechanism - the absence DTDs could not repair.
namespaces-in-xml-w3c-recommendation-199.leap: Namespaces in XML (January 1999) supplied the name-partitioning mechanism that XSD's namespace-aware declarations (targetNamespace, qualified names) consume as a given.
namespaces-in-xml-w3c-recommendation-199.prior_state: Flat name space; vocabulary mixing handled by naming conventions.

thurstone-s-law-of-comparative-judgment-.name: Thurstone's law of comparative judgment
thurstone-s-law-of-comparative-judgment-.definition: Thurstone's 1927 model of paired comparison: each item evokes a normal 'discriminal process' on a psychological continuum, and the probability one item is judged above another is the normal ogive of the difference of their scale values (Case V).
thurstone-s-law-of-comparative-judgment-.bottleneck: Before Thurstone's law, paired judgments could not be converted into measurements on a scale, because no probabilistic model connected choice frequencies to latent magnitudes.
thurstone-s-law-of-comparative-judgment-.leap: Thurstone (1927) made paired comparisons a measurement instrument: latent scale values recoverable from observed preference proportions, founding psychometric scaling.
thurstone-s-law-of-comparative-judgment-.prior_state: Judgments recorded as raw counts and orderings, with no model linking them to an underlying continuum.

yates-incomplete-randomised-blocks-1936.name: Yates, Incomplete randomised blocks
yates-incomplete-randomised-blocks-1936.definition: Yates's 1936 Rothamsted paper founding incomplete block designs: layouts in which each block holds only a subset of treatments, with recovery of inter-block information, for experiments where complete blocks are infeasible.
yates-incomplete-randomised-blocks-1936.bottleneck: Before Yates (1936), an experiment with more treatments than any block could hold could not be run with block-level error control, because design theory assumed every block contained every treatment.
yates-incomplete-randomised-blocks-1936.leap: Yates (1936) created the incomplete block design: treatments compared through blocks that hold only some of them, with inter-block information recovered in the analysis.
yates-incomplete-randomised-blocks-1936.prior_state: Complete blocks and Latin squares as the only design forms; large treatment sets forced either huge blocks or no blocking.

fechner-elemente-der-psychophysik-1860-1.name: Fechner, Elemente der Psychophysik (1860)

fechner-elemente-der-psychophysik-1860-1.bottleneck: Before Fechner's Elemente, sensation had no measurement procedure at all, because no unit or law connected physical stimulus magnitudes to experienced magnitudes.
fechner-elemente-der-psychophysik-1860-1.leap: Fechner (1860) made sensation measurable: the just noticeable difference became a unit to be counted, and Fechner's law gave the first quantitative function relating stimulus to sensation.
fechner-elemente-der-psychophysik-1860-1.prior_state: Qualitative introspective psychology; Weber's isolated JND proportionality without a measurement programme.

urban-s-psychometric-function-and-phi-ga.name: Urban's psychometric function and phi-gamma hypothesis (1908)

urban-s-psychometric-function-and-phi-ga.leap: Urban (1908) fitted the psychometric function: proportions of comparative judgments became the cumulative normal ogive of stimulus difference, the first statistical model of judgment proportions.

galton-co-relations-and-their-measuremen.name: Galton, Co-relations and their measurement, chiefly from anthropometric data (1888)
galton-co-relations-and-their-measuremen.definition: Galton's 1888 Proceedings of the Royal Society paper (45: 135-145) defining co-relation and its measure from paired anthropometric measures — the first general measure of the degree of resemblance between two varying quantities.
galton-co-relations-and-their-measuremen.bottleneck: Before the 1888 paper, how strongly two varying quantities are related could not be expressed as a number, because co-relation had never been defined or measured.
galton-co-relations-and-their-measuremen.leap: Galton (1888) defined co-relation and measured it: from the paired deviations of two organs or measures he extracted a single index — resemblance between any two variables became a quantity, and degrees of kinship became measurable in the same currency.
galton-co-relations-and-their-measuremen.prior_state: Association between measures judged by eye from tables and diagrams; regression available only between parent and offspring measures of the same trait.

A component that verifies is not a mediator that carries. Attack recorded; edge stands. Outcome provisional.

galton-regression-towards-mediocrity-in-.name: Galton, Regression towards mediocrity in hereditary stature (1886)
galton-regression-towards-mediocrity-in-.definition: Galton's 1886 Journal of the Anthropological Institute paper (read at Aberdeen, 1885): filial regression measured on family stature records — offspring deviate on average two-thirds as much as their mid-parents.
galton-regression-towards-mediocrity-in-.bottleneck: Before the 1886 paper, that the children of exceptional parents are on average less exceptional could not be stated as a measured law of heredity, because no family data had ever been tabulated against parental measures.
galton-regression-towards-mediocrity-in-.leap: Galton (1886) measured regression towards mediocrity in hereditary stature: the offspring of mid-parents deviate two-thirds as much as their parents — filial resemblance became a ratio, and its explanation (inheritance partly from ancestry) pointed straight at the ancestral law.
galton-regression-towards-mediocrity-in-.prior_state: Regression glimpsed only in sweet-pea seed weights (1877); human filial resemblance a matter of anecdote and breeder's impression.

quetelet-sur-l-homme-and-the-application.name: Quetelet, Sur l'homme and the application of the law of error to human measures (1835)
quetelet-sur-l-homme-and-the-application.definition: Quetelet's Sur l'homme (1835) first fitted the astronomers' law of error to human measurements (the chests of Scottish soldiers, the heights of French conscripts) and made the 'average man' the object of a science of man.
quetelet-sur-l-homme-and-the-application.bottleneck: Before Quetelet, the law of error belonged to the observatory, because no one had shown that the measures of men — chests, heights — obey it as the measures of stars do.
quetelet-sur-l-homme-and-the-application.leap: Quetelet (1835) carried the astronomers' law of error into the science of man: human measurements distribute about the 'average man' as observations about a true value, making population variation a lawful, measurable object.
quetelet-sur-l-homme-and-the-application.prior_state: The error law confined to astronomy and geodesy; human variation described anecdotally, without distribution or constants.

kleene-introduction-to-metamathematics-t.name: Kleene, Introduction to Metamathematics — the theory of partial recursive functions (1952)
kleene-introduction-to-metamathematics-t.definition: Kleene's codification (1952) of the theory of (partial) recursive functions: functions defined from elementary functions by composition, recursion and minimisation — the definitional scheme of computability McCarthy's formalism re-targets.
kleene-introduction-to-metamathematics-t.bottleneck: Before Kleene's codification, what it means for a function to be effectively calculable had no single standard definitional scheme a new formalism could take as its basis.
kleene-introduction-to-metamathematics-t.leap: Kleene's theory of partial recursive functions (1952) gave computability its canonical definitional scheme — functions built from elementary functions by composition, primitive recursion and minimisation — the scheme the parent re-targets from numbers to symbolic expressions.
kleene-introduction-to-metamathematics-t.prior_state: Competing accounts of effective calculability (Church's thesis, Turing's machines) without one standard reference treatment of recursive definition.

ipl-information-processing-language-newe.name: IPL — Information Processing Language (Newell, Shaw & Simon, 1956)

galton-family-likeness-in-stature-1886-1.name: Galton, Family likeness in stature (1886)

galton-s-sweet-pea-experiments-and-typic.name: Galton's sweet-pea experiments and 'Typical laws of heredity' (1877)
galton-s-sweet-pea-experiments-and-typic.definition: Galton's 1877 Royal Institution lecture and paper reporting the sweet-pea experiments: filial seeds regress towards mediocrity in direct proportion to the parental deviation — the first statement of the regression law.

galton-s-sweet-pea-experiments-and-typic.prior_state: Filial resemblance a matter of breeder's impression; offspring assumed to inherit the parental deviation whole.

laplace-theorie-analytique-des-probabili.name: Laplace, Théorie analytique des probabilités (1812)
laplace-theorie-analytique-des-probabili.definition: Laplace's treatise giving the error law its limit-theorem warrant: the sum of many small independent accidental causes distributes by the curve of frequency of error.
laplace-theorie-analytique-des-probabili.bottleneck: Before Laplace's Théorie analytique (1812), the error curve was an empirical rule of the observatory, because no theorem showed why accumulated accidental causes must produce it.
laplace-theorie-analytique-des-probabili.leap: Laplace (1810-12) proved that the aggregate of many small independent causes follows the error curve — the curve became a theorem about causes, the warrant on which its transfer to new domains rests.
laplace-theorie-analytique-des-probabili.prior_state: The error curve used empirically by astronomers; De Moivre's approximation confined to games of chance.

de-moivre-the-doctrine-of-chances-1738-1.name: De Moivre, The Doctrine of Chances (1738)
