Outcome provisional per standing practice and the partial Q3.

rfc-2396-uniform-resource-identifiers-ge.name: RFC 2396, Uniform Resource Identifiers: Generic Syntax (Berners-Lee, Fielding & Masinter, 1998)
rfc-2396-uniform-resource-identifiers-ge.definition: The IETF standards-track generic syntax for URIs: 'A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a compact string of characters for identifying an abstract or physical resource' - defining absolute and relative URI references (including fragment identifiers) as one scheme-independent grammar that 'revises and replaces the generic definitions in RFC 1738 and RFC 1808'. The parent Recommendation's core definition reads: 'An XML namespace is a collection of names, identified by a URI reference [RFC2396]' - the parent normatively cites this document for the form of its namespace names, and its uniqueness argument is 'the combination of the universally-managed URI namespace and the document's own namespace produces identifiers that are universally unique'.
rfc-2396-uniform-resource-identifiers-ge.bottleneck: Before a generic URI syntax, identifying a resource across schemes was impractical to standardise, because locators (URLs) and persistent names (URNs) had separate grammars and no common reference form existed that a specification could cite once for all of them.
rfc-2396-uniform-resource-identifiers-ge.leap: RFC 2396 (Aug 1998) unified URL and URN under one generic syntax for URI references - absolute and relative, with fragment identifiers - giving any specification a single citable form for 'a compact string of characters for identifying an abstract or physical resource', backed by scheme registration and DNS delegation, the management that makes the identifier space universal.
rfc-2396-uniform-resource-identifiers-ge.prior_state: RFC 1738 URLs (1994) and RFC 1808 relative URLs defined locator forms piecemeal; URNs were standardised separately (RFC 2141, 1997); no unified reference grammar existed.

verification.notes: Attacks run. (1) Multiples test on Q3: the URI idea had earlier carriers (RFC 1630's informal 1994 account; RFC 1738's URL grammar), which is why Q3 was scored partial in evaluation - but the artifact the parent normatively cites, and the only one supplying the unified 'URI reference' form, is RFC 2396; the multiples cap the necessity claim, they do not move the channel. (2) Mediation attack via RFC 1738: tried and answered - RFC 1738 specifies locators for concrete resources; the parent's definition needs an identifier for an abstract collection of names, and its citation is to 2396's generic syntax, which by its own abstract 'revises and replaces' 1738's generic definitions. RFC 1738's rejection at this parent is recorded as mediated via RFC 2396. (3) Date/direction: RFC 2396 (Aug 1998) precedes the Recommendation (Jan 1999); the parent's own Jan 1998 Note already used URIs loosely, and the REC tightened the reference to [RFC2396] - direction and citation both direct. Outcome provisional per standing practice and the partial Q3.

colloidal-silica-chemical-mechanical-pol.name: Colloidal-silica chemical-mechanical polishing of silicon wafers (Walsh & Herzog, Monsanto, 1965)
colloidal-silica-chemical-mechanical-pol.definition: Monsanto's chemical-mechanical polishing process for bare silicon wafers (Walsh & Herzog, patented 1965; polished wafers sold from late 1962): submicron silicon-dioxide abrasive in an alkaline slurry, cutting wafer finishing time from about 1.5 hours to about 5 minutes while leaving a damage-free, scratch-free surface.
colloidal-silica-chemical-mechanical-pol.bottleneck: Before colloidal-silica chem-mech polishing, production silicon wafers could not be finished flat and damage-free at manufacturing speed, because purely mechanical polishing left a damaged, scratched surface layer and took on the order of an hour and a half per batch.
colloidal-silica-chemical-mechanical-pol.leap: Walsh & Herzog's Monsanto process (patented 1965; polished wafers sold from late 1962) finished silicon wafers with submicron silica abrasive in an alkaline slurry: finishing time fell from about 1.5 hours to about 5 minutes and the surface came out flat, scratch-free and damage-free - the production practice that semiconductor CMP later morphed from.
colloidal-silica-chemical-mechanical-pol.prior_state: Wafer finishing was mechanical polishing with classified alumina or zirconia abrasives, followed by chemical etching to remove the mechanically damaged layer.

sources.title: Fury, Milestones in a Quarter Century of CMP, ECS Trans. 19(7) (2009); Lai, Mechanics, Mechanisms, and Modeling of the Chemical Mechanical Polishing Process, MIT PhD thesis (2001), sec. 1.3

verification.notes: All four attacks run. (1) Q1 attack: etch-and-polish sequences did produce usable wafers before 1965, so 'impossible' is too strong in the abstract - but they were slow, two-step, and left the finishing bottleneck the candidate removed in a single 5-minute step; the flip survives as scored for production practice (speed plus damage-free surface jointly), and Q3 was already capped at partial for exactly this reason. (2) Multiples test on Q3: near-simultaneous chem-mech work exists - Fuller & Allison's III-V polishing etchant (1962) and Schmidt's 1962 report - but both are a compound-semiconductor niche method and a report respectively; for silicon wafer production the Monsanto practice is the documented commercial carrier (polished wafers sold from late 1962). Multiples recorded; the node is not verified on necessity grounds. (3) Date/direction: patent dated 1965 with commercial sale from late 1962 (Lai 2001) - the 1965 year is the defensible documentary date; direction (bare-wafer practice -> device-wafer planarization) is Fury's own morphing sentence. (4) Mediation attack: two intermediates tried. Blake & Mendel (1970) - answered: a cupric-salt slurry variant inside the same IBM production practice, not a separable carrier; Fury's channel sentence names the wafer-polishing practice itself. Schmidt (1962) - answered: a report of the practice is not its carrier (document-about-advance discrimination). No mediation object recorded. Outcome provisional per standing practice and the partial Q3.

self-aligned-double-gate-finfet-device-f.name: Self-aligned double-gate FinFET device formulation (Hu et al., IEEE Trans. Electron Devices, 2000)
self-aligned-double-gate-finfet-device-f.definition: The Berkeley group's canonical FinFET paper: self-aligned double-gate MOSFET with ultrathin body, gate length scalable to 20 nm.
self-aligned-double-gate-finfet-device-f.bottleneck: By the late 1990s planar MOSFET electrostatics set a hard floor under gate length: below ~50 nm the gate lost control of the channel, because the scale length was set by junction depth and oxide thickness.
self-aligned-double-gate-finfet-device-f.leap: The Berkeley group's FinFET formulation (IEDM 1998; Huang et al. 1999; Hu et al., IEEE TED 2000) made the thin vertical fin the channel and wrapped the gate on both sides, self-aligned: the scale length is set by fin thickness, and the published device was shown scalable to 20 nm gate length.
self-aligned-double-gate-finfet-device-f.prior_state: Planar bulk MOSFETs at the electrostatic wall; double-gate devices existed as theory (and as Hisamoto's DELTA pillar) without a manufacturable self-aligned formulation.

tsmc-20nm-soc-process-20soc-2014-2014.name: TSMC 20nm SoC process (20SoC, 2014)
tsmc-20nm-soc-process-20soc-2014-2014.definition: TSMC's 20 nm planar SoC process, in production 2014.

delta-fully-depleted-lean-channel-transi.name: DELTA fully-depleted lean-channel transistor (Hisamoto et al., Hitachi CRL, 1989)
delta-fully-depleted-lean-channel-transi.definition: Hitachi's vertical ultrathin SOI MOSFET (IEDM 1989; EDL 1990): a fully depleted lean channel formed on the side surface of a vertical silicon pillar - the first fabricated fin-type double-gate device.
delta-fully-depleted-lean-channel-transi.bottleneck: Late-1990s planar MOSFET electrostatics set a hard floor under gate length: below ~50 nm the gate lost control of the channel (scale length set by junction depth and oxide thickness), and channel doping could not be raised further without destroying mobility and Vt control.
delta-fully-depleted-lean-channel-transi.leap: The first fabricated fin-type transistor: a fully depleted lean channel formed on the side surface of a vertical ultrathin SOI pillar - gate control from geometry, not doping.
delta-fully-depleted-lean-channel-transi.prior_state: 1989 state of the art: planar bulk MOSFETs; double-gate devices existed only as calculations (XMOS 1984) and simulation; no fabricated thin-body vertical device.

selective-oxidation-soi-cmos-process-kub.name: Selective-oxidation SOI CMOS process (Kubota et al., IEDM 1986)
selective-oxidation-soi-cmos-process-kub.definition: Hitachi process forming bulk single-crystal silicon-on-insulator by selective (LOCOS-type) oxidation of patterned silicon islands - an SOI CMOS process with no implanted or recrystallized layer.
selective-oxidation-soi-cmos-process-kub.bottleneck: Before Kubota's selective-oxidation SOI process, a silicon-on-insulator layer could only be had as implanted or recrystallized material, because no process formed SOI out of bulk single-crystal silicon itself.
selective-oxidation-soi-cmos-process-kub.leap: The first SOI CMOS process whose isolated device layer is bulk single-crystal silicon, formed by selective (LOCOS-type) oxidation of patterned silicon islands - no implanted or recrystallized film anywhere in the flow.

bernoulli-ars-conjectandi-1713-1713.name: Bernoulli, Ars Conjectandi (1713)
bernoulli-ars-conjectandi-1713-1713.definition: Jacob Bernoulli's posthumous treatise: Part I a commentary on Huygens, Part IV the 'golden theorem' - for a binomial experiment the observed frequency can be made to fall within any given limits of the true ratio with moral certainty, by taking trials enough; it fixes the binomial distribution as the object and poses the deviation problem.

bernoulli-ars-conjectandi-1713-1713.leap: Bernoulli (1713) proved the first limit theorem of probability: frequency converges to chance, with explicit (if impractically wide) bounds on the number of trials required.
bernoulli-ars-conjectandi-1713-1713.prior_state: Exact enumeration for small cases (Huygens, Montmort); the stability of frequency an empirical observation (Graunt, Arbuthnot) without proof.

stirling-methodus-differentialis-1730-17.name: Stirling, Methodus Differentialis (1730)
stirling-methodus-differentialis-1730-17.definition: Stirling's treatise on finite differences whose corollary gives the asymptotic series for log n! with the constant determined as sqrt(2 pi) (via Wallis's product) - the factorial asymptotic De Moivre's 1733 derivation consumes at its load-bearing point.

stirling-methodus-differentialis-1730-17.prior_state: De Moivre's own series for log(n!) with the constant only approximated numerically (c ~ 2.5); exact factorials computable only for small n.

rfc-1738-uniform-resource-locators-url-b.name: RFC 1738, Uniform Resource Locators (URL) (Berners-Lee, Masinter & McCahill, 1994)

pascal-fermat-correspondence-on-the-prob.name: Pascal-Fermat correspondence on the problem of points (1654)
pascal-fermat-correspondence-on-the-prob.definition: The 1654 exchange in which Pascal and Fermat solved the problem of points by enumerating the fictitious completion of the game - the founding documents of mathematical probability.

rfc-1737-functional-requirements-for-uni.leap: RFC 1737 (1994) fixed the requirement set for URNs - global scope and uniqueness, persistence, legacy-scheme embedding, delegated naming authorities under central registration, a single encoding with simple comparison - the charter against which a URN syntax could be specified and judged.

nowlan-maximum-likelihood-competitive-le.prior_state: Winner-take-all competitive learning: the winning unit alone adapts, with dead units and no likelihood semantics.

ibm-solder-bump-flip-chip-joining-with-c.name: IBM solder-bump flip-chip joining with copper-ball standoff (1962)

ibm-solder-bump-flip-chip-joining-with-c.leap: The 1962 practice joined glass-passivated chips face-down by reflowing solder bumps - each stiffened by an embedded copper ball acting as standoff - onto solder-coated electrodes of a ceramic carrier: every terminal joined in a single reflow.
ibm-solder-bump-flip-chip-joining-with-c.prior_state: Chips connected one terminal at a time by wires around the periphery, or mounted by brazing into packages.

godel-on-formally-undecidable-propositio.bottleneck: Before Godel (1931), statements of a formal system could not themselves be treated as numbers, so no theorem could speak about provability or about a system's own formulas, and no property of formulas could be defined arithmetically.
godel-on-formally-undecidable-propositio.leap: Godel's arithmetization assigned every formula a number (the Godel representation) and defined (primitive) recursive functions and relations, making a formal system's syntax an object of arithmetic - the device Church's 1936 paper uses throughout Secs. 4-6 to define recursive properties of formulas, and cites at footnote 14.
godel-on-formally-undecidable-propositio.prior_state: Hilbert's programme, in which metamathematics was conducted informally, outside and about the formal system, without a numerical encoding of its syntax.

leap.prior_state: State-of-the-art neural MT in mid-2014 was the fixed-vector encoder-decoder (Cho et al.; Sutskever et al.): the whole source sentence compressed into one vector, with translation quality collapsing on long sentences, while phrase-based SMT (Moses) still set the BLEU standard (35.63 on WMT'14 En-Fr).
leap.jump: Bahdanau et al. (posted 1 Sep 2014) let the decoder soft-search all encoder annotations at every step: RNNsearch scored 26.75 BLEU against the equivalent encoder-decoder's 17.82 (50-word training), quality no longer deteriorated on 50+-word sentences, and a longer-trained model reached 36.15 on no-unknown-word sentences, matching the phrase-based incumbent; attention became a reusable mechanism separable from recurrence.

directness.counterfactual: Remove the bidirectional RNN and RNNsearch as published does not exist: every annotation the soft search scores is the concatenation of forward and backward encoder states (paper section 3.1); a unidirectional encoder strips the right-context from every annotation, degrading exactly the objects the alignment model exists to search over.

leap.prior_state: Plain RNNs trained by backpropagation through time, with the vanishing/exploding gradient problem formally characterized (Hochreiter 1991; Bengio et al. 1994) and no trainable long-memory cell.
leap.jump: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997) showed a gated memory cell with a constant error carousel could learn dependencies over very long lags that gradient descent on plain RNNs provably could not.

directness.counterfactual: Remove the 1991 analysis and the 1997 paper loses its design derivation: Sec. 3's exponential error-flow result is what specifies the remedy (enforce constant error flow), and the gated cell is engineered point-by-point against the failure modes the analysis names. No intermediate work sits between the thesis and the paper's derivation.
directness.evidence: LSTM paper (1997), abstract and Sec. 1-3; IDSIA page on Hochreiter's 1991 fundamental deep learning problem.

Q1.evidence: It showed pairwise comparisons between trajectory segments suffice to learn a reward model that trains agents on objectives humans can judge but not formalize (MuJoCo, Atari).

Q2.falsification: this pass dies if preference-based reward learning is shown to have remained confined to control tasks.

Q3.evidence: For this parent the channel also ran through Ziegler et al.'s LM port, and alternative feedback routes (TAMER, IRL) existed; the framework's necessity is shared, not sole.

Q4.evidence: Comparisons are far cheaper than demonstrations or reward engineering, but the method still consumed hundreds to thousands of human judgments per task.

Q5.evidence: It turned unobservable human preference into a trainable scalar signal - the reward model - measurable and optimizable.

Q5.falsification: this pass dies if the reward model is shown not to track human preference better than chance; the paper's evaluations show the opposite.

leap.prior_state: Gradient learning used the ordinary (Euclidean) gradient of the loss on arbitrarily parameterized models, so the direction of 'steepest descent' depended on the arbitrary coordinate choice; Fisher information existed as a static estimation quantity, its metric role confined to estimation theory; and what asymptotic efficiency an online (stochastic) learning rule could attain was an open question being probed by the statistical-physics literature (Heskes & Kappen 1991; Opper 1996).
leap.jump: Amari (1998) defines the natural gradient - steepest descent under the Fisher-information Riemannian metric on the model's statistical manifold (Theorem 1) - proves natural gradient online learning is Fisher efficient, attaining the Cramer-Rao bound (Theorem 2), and computes the metric and its inverse explicitly for perceptrons, for the matrix manifold of blind source separation, and for linear dynamical systems.

leap.prior_state: Few-shot prompting in its standard form (Brown et al., 2020) mapped questions directly to answers in one forward pass, and on multi-step reasoning tasks its scaling curve was flat (Rae et al., 2021). leap.prior_state: Conventional networks trained by minimizing sum-of-squares or cross-entropy error output the conditional averages of the target data. For multi-valued inverse problems - robot inverse kinematics, reconstruction - the average of several correct target values is not itself a correct value, so least-squares networks give completely erroneous results there. The era's density alternatives were nonparametric kernel estimators that store the data, or mixture models with input-independent parameters fitted by EM.
leap.jump: Bishop (1994) made a conventional feedforward network output the mixing coefficients, means and variances of a Gaussian mixture, trained by maximum likelihood through the network - a single model representing arbitrary conditional densities p(t|x). On the two-link robot inverse kinematics problem the MDN reduced end-effector positioning RMS error by an order of magnitude versus the least-squares network, with small errors even in the region where the inverse mapping is double-valued.

directness.counterfactual: Remove adaptive mixtures of local experts and the parent loses its architectural template and its error function's precedent: the MDN is the experts construction with each expert replaced by a density kernel and the gating posterior reinterpreted as mixing coefficients. Without the 1991 form in the literature the parent would have had to invent input-dependent mixture weighting and its likelihood training from the statistics side alone - a different and later paper.
directness.evidence: Citation + instantiation at three points of the parent's own text: the softmax choice for mixing coefficients is cited '(Bridle, 1990; Jacobs et al., 1991)'; the mixture representation's variance benefit is cited '(Jacobs et al., 1991; Nowlan and Hinton, 1992)'; and the error-function section states the formal equivalence with Jacobs et al.'s competing-experts error function while discriminating the interpretation (a full conditional density, not a posterior over experts). Ancestor-modified consumption, documented by the parent itself.

leap.prior_state: Conventional networks trained by minimizing sum-of-squares or cross-entropy error output the conditional averages of the target data. For multi-valued inverse problems - robot inverse kinematics, reconstruction - the average of several correct target values is not itself a correct value, so least-squares networks give completely erroneous results there. The era's density alternatives were nonparametric kernel estimators that store the data, or mixture models with input-independent parameters fitted by EM.
leap.jump: Bishop (1994) made a conventional feedforward network output the mixing coefficients, means and variances of a Gaussian mixture, trained by maximum likelihood through the network - a single model representing arbitrary conditional densities p(t|x). On the two-link robot inverse kinematics problem the MDN reduced end-effector positioning RMS error by an order of magnitude versus the least-squares network, with small errors even in the region where the inverse mapping is double-valued.

Q1.evidence: Before this memoir, the degree of resemblance between kinsmen in any given degree could not be computed at all — there were no constants of kinship. Q2.evidence: The memoir's formulae are stated for stature but claimed for 'every one-dimensioned faculty that all men possess in some degree', and its surface machinery applies to any pair of variables — the 1888 paper is itself the first generalisation it unblocked.

Q2.falsification: This pass dies if the memoir's machinery is shown to be specific to stature with no general form.

Q3.evidence: Necessity is capped at ripe: the author's JAI memoir covers part of the same ground, and Edgeworth's error-theory line was developing the multivariate law in parallel. As written, however, the parent cites and re-works this memoir, not the alternatives.

Q4.falsification: This partial dies if the formulae are shown to have required fresh data for each application.

leap.prior_state: Association between measures judged by eye from tables and diagrams; regression available only between parent and offspring measures of the same trait.
leap.jump: Galton (1888) defined co-relation and measured it: from the paired deviations of two organs or measures he extracted a single index r — resemblance between any two variables became a quantity, and degrees of kinship became measurable in the same currency.

directness.counterfactual: Remove the memoir and the 1888 paper loses all three of its load-bearing parts: the kinship results it generalises (it cites this memoir by volume and page for them), its one worked case where the two Q-scales differ (the mid-parent case, re-derived in the paper from this memoir's numbers), and the surface mathematics it expressly declines to repeat because the memoir's appendix contains it. The paper would shrink to the organ tables with no rationale and no warrant.
directness.evidence: The 1888 paper: 'analogous to what was observed in kinship, as I showed in my paper read before this Society on Hereditary Stature (Roy. Soc. Proc., vol. 40, 1886, p. 42)'; the mid-parent recomputation (2/3 and 1/3 in inches becoming 0.47 and 0.44 in Q units) is worked from that memoir's case; 'The rationale of all this will be found discussed in the paper on Hereditary Stature... and in the appendix to it by Mr. J. D. Hamilton Dickson... therefore I need not repeat them here.' Citation plus instantiation, the strong channel.

Q1.evidence: Before 1877, proportional filial regression had never been observed or stated: offspring were assumed to take the parental deviation whole. The lecture made the shortfall itself the phenomenon — 'the mean filial regression towards mediocrity was directly proportional to the parental deviation' — a fact about heredity that had been invisible inside the assumption it replaced.

Q1.falsification: This pass dies if a pre-1877 publication is shown to state proportional regression of offspring towards the mean.

Q2.evidence: The seed law opened the space the memoir works in — a law of heredity statable as a ratio — but the generalisation to kinship in every degree and to correlation waited for the 1886-88 memoirs.

Q2.falsification: This partial rises if the 1877 lecture is shown to state the law for kinship degrees beyond parent-offspring.

Q3.evidence: Necessity is capped at ripe: the phenomenon is a fact of nature that careful family data might in principle have revealed directly; but as the record stands, the memoir's inquiry was undertaken to test the seed law in man, and its author states that motive in its first pages.

Q3.falsification: This partial rises to pass if the memoir is shown to have been conceived independently of the seed result.

Q4.evidence: The seeds collapsed the cost of a heredity experiment: a generation in a season, complete pedigrees, thousands of cases for the price of a bag of peas — against human generations of twenty-five years. Q4.source: Stanton, Galton, Pearson, and the Peas (J. Statistics Education 9(3), 2001)
Q4.falsification: This partial dies if the seed experiments are shown to have been slower or costlier per datum than the family-record route.

Q6.evidence: It supplied the phenomenon's first explanatory frame — reversion towards the ancestral type, restated by the memoir as inheritance partly from parents, partly from ancestry — which the memoir's Appendix II turns into the ancestral law's arithmetic (1/2, 1/4, 1/16...).

Q8.falsification: This partial rises if a pre-1886 application outside the author's programme is shown.

Q9.evidence: Annual generations collapsed the feedback loop of heredity research from decades to seasons: the experiments ran through one, two, and three generations of plants while a single human generation was still growing up.

Q9.falsification: This pass dies if the experiments are shown to have taken comparable calendar time to human pedigree work.

leap.jump: Galton (1886) measured regression towards mediocrity in hereditary stature: the offspring of mid-parents deviate two-thirds as much as their parents — filial resemblance became a ratio, and its explanation (inheritance partly from ancestry) pointed straight at the ancestral law.

directness.counterfactual: Remove the 1877 lecture and the memoir loses its stated reason for existing: it opens by restating the seed result, republishes the seed averages in Appendix I as the law's first evidence, and declares its motive — 'It was anthropological evidence that I desired, caring only for the seeds as means of throwing light on heredity in man.' Without the seed law there is no hypothesis for the family records to test and no two-thirds ratio to find.
directness.evidence: The memoir's opening: 'I then found that the mean filial regression towards mediocrity was directly proportional to the parental deviation from it... The experiments... showed a mean regression... of one-third'; Appendix I republishes the seed data in full ('the diameters of parent seeds and of their offspring... first observed in the diameters of seeds'). Own-version exception argued explicitly: a separable published artifact (Royal Institution lecture, 9 Feb 1877; Proc. Roy. Inst. 9) whose mechanism — proportional regression — is consumed and reworked: the memoir re-derives it in man, explains it (ancestry dilution), and generalises it (Appendix II's ancestral contributions). The mechanism-consumption clause is met.

edges.leap: Before RAG, answering knowledge-intensive questions with a language model was impractical in a specific way: everything the model knew had to be stored in its parameters at training time, so its knowledge could not be updated, inspected or attributed, and generation drifted into hallucination - while the retrieval-augmented models that existed (ORQA, REALM) put the retriever behind an extractive or masked-LM reader, not a generator. RAG's discontinuous step was the general-purpose formulation: a pretrained seq2seq generator coupled to a pretrained dense retriever over a 21M-passage Wikipedia index, the retrieved documents treated as latent variables and marginalized (per-sequence or per-token), the pair fine-tuned end-to-end - parametric and non-parametric memory as one trainable object, demonstrated across open-domain QA, fact verification and generation tasks at once.

directness.counterfactual: Remove ORQA and the parent loses both its stated corpus convention (the parent adopts Lee et al.'s dump and passage form verbatim, by citation) and the formulation it transforms: latent retrieval over Wikipedia, marginalized, trained end-to-end. DPR supplies better retriever weights, but the object being trained - and the corpus it runs on - is ORQA's construction.
directness.evidence: Two documented channels in the parent's own text: the methods section follows Lee et al. [31] for the non-parametric memory's construction, and the introduction names ORQA as one of the two retrieval-augmented models whose formulation the parent generalizes (reader made generative, retriever initialized from DPR instead of ICT). Ancestor-modified with the mechanism retained (latent-variable marginalization over retrieved passages IS the parent's training object) - the Rumelhart & Norman successor shape, not a component: ORQA is not inside the parent's runs, it is the design the parent's runs instantiate.

Q1.evidence: Impossibility flip, pass: before the Bosch cycle, a vertical-walled hole tens of microns deep in silicon was not a manufacturable object - wet etch follows crystal planes, single-step plasma etch undercuts or stalls. The alternating cycle made the geometry routine: etch rates >2 um/min, mask selectivity >100:1, vertical sidewalls (Laermer & Urban's own process summary). The parent's vias are etched holes of exactly this class.
Q1.source: Laermer & Urban, 'Bosch-DRIE Shaping MEMS', Hilton Head 2010; Laermer & Schilp, US 5,501,893 (1996)
Q1.falsification: This pass dies if a pre-1994 production etch process with comparable rate, selectivity and sidewall verticality is documented.

Q2.evidence: Generativity, pass: the process unblocked two industries - MEMS (accelerometers, gyroscopes, microphones, micromirrors, all built on it from 1995) and 3D integration (the etched TSV). Bosch alone reported 50 million inertial sensors a year on it by 2007.
Q2.source: Laermer & Urban, 'Bosch-DRIE Shaping MEMS', Hilton Head 2010; Laermer & Schilp, US 5,501,893 (1996)
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if the MEMS device record is shown to rest on a different etch process.

Q3.evidence: Necessity, partial - capped by multiples inside etch technology: cryogenic single-step etching (Jansen et al.) was a parallel route to deep silicon structures, and laser drilling (Samsung WSP) formed vias by another mechanism entirely. Q3.source: Laermer & Urban, 'Bosch-DRIE Shaping MEMS', Hilton Head 2010; Laermer & Schilp, US 5,501,893 (1996)
Q3.falsification: This partial rises only if the cryogenic and laser routes are shown to have been non-viable at production scale in 2007; it falls if either is shown to have carried a comparable TSV productization.

Q1.evidence: Before the memo's idea was implemented, composing programs meant writing intermediate results to files and invoking the next program by hand; the memo proposed coupling as a system primitive - 'coupling programs like garden hose... Q3.falsification: A document showing Thompson took pipes from a source other than McIlroy's advocacy.

leap.prior_state: Fixed supervisor command sets of the CTSS kind; on the brand-new UNIX (1969-71) users typed one built-in command at a time, with no redirection, no pipes and no scripts.
leap.jump: The command interpreter became an ordinary program composing commands as text: per-command redirection (<, >), simultaneous/background execution (&), command files executed by the shell itself, and (1972-73) pipes connecting one command's output to another's input.

directness.counterfactual: Remove the memo and its author's decade of advocacy, and pipes do not enter UNIX when they did: Ritchie's account has the idea 'fail to ignite any immediate action' until 'McIlroy's persistence' got it installed - the parent's pipes component is this document's delayed implementation.
directness.evidence: Ritchie: pipes appeared 'at the suggestion (or perhaps insistence) of M. D. McIlroy, a long-time advocate'; 'thanks to McIlroy's persistence, pipes were finally installed'. The memo (11 Oct 1964) is the concept's founding document, written by the head of Thompson's own department in the Multics design context both men worked in.

The flip is real at the component scope; the parent's contribution on this component is compactness and per-command form, which is why Q3 stays partial and the score stays low. Q1.evidence: Before this practice, no chip could be joined face-down with all terminals made in a single operation - every connection was a separate serial act (a wire, a braze). The 1962 reduction to practice made gang reflow joining of a whole chip real: solder bumps on a glass-passivated device, reflowed onto a circuitized ceramic carrier.
Q1.source: Totta, Forty Years of Flip Chips with Solder Bumps
Q1.falsification: Evidence of a working solder-bump flip-chip joint before summer 1962.

Q2.evidence: Generative: this practice is the seed of the entire flip-chip line - C4 itself, the area array, and four decades of bump-count growth (Totta: from 3 bumps to 7018) all descend from it.
Q2.source: Totta, Forty Years of Flip Chips with Solder Bumps
Q2.falsification: Evidence the flip-chip line descends from a different founding practice.

Q3.evidence: Multiples cap necessity: Miller's introduction attests that 'the component industry has developed a number of processes for joining semiconductor devices face down' (his refs 1-3) - face-down joining was in the era's air. But the parent's descent is specifically from THIS practice: same firm, same line, same equipment, and the programme historian narrates the modification directly. Necessity holds for the path that happened, not for the concept in the abstract.
Q3.source: Miller, Controlled Collapse Reflow Chip Joining, IBM J. Res. Dev. 13(3):239 (1969)
Q3.falsification: A document showing Miller's controlled collapse derived from a non-IBM face-down process.

Q4.evidence: Gang joining collapsed per-terminal labour inside IBM's module production (the practice was built for automated SLT lines), but no period cost accounting survives to grade the collapse as orders of magnitude.
Q4.source: Miller, Controlled Collapse Reflow Chip Joining, IBM J. Res. Dev. 13(3):239 (1969)
Q4.falsification: Period cost data showing hand joining remained cheaper on the SLT line.

Q5.evidence: No metric registered this practice's step in its own moment (the L17 dry-with-finding for this parent).

Q5.falsification: A period benchmark of chip joining naming the 1962 practice.

Q6.source: Davis et al., Solid Logic Technology, IBM JRD 8:102 (1964)
Q6.falsification: Evidence the practice was understood at the time as a one-off expedient with no general model.

Q7.evidence: Composability: the bump terminal is an interface - any device carrying the Cr-Cu-Au terminal joins any circuitized carrier in one reflow, without the device or carrier knowing each other's internals. That interface is exactly what the parent inherits and keeps.

Q7.falsification: Evidence each 1962 joint was a bespoke, device-specific construction.

Q9.falsification: Evidence joining remained the SLT line's bottleneck unchanged by the practice.

Q10.falsification: Evidence IBM itself kept wire-bonding its SLT devices after 1962.

Q11.evidence: Lineage centrality: both lineage accounts available (Totta's history; the IMAPS origins review) root the C4 line here - 'In 1969 controlled collapse chip connection (C-4) replaced copper balls with solder balls' presupposes this practice as the thing replaced and continued.

leap.prior_state: Peripheral wire bonding and beam leads: serial, pitch-bound, inductance-heavy interconnection, one wire at a time.
leap.jump: Controlled-collapse chip connection put solder bumps over the whole face of the chip, their collapse governed by surface tension against glass-dam-defined pads, joining every I/O in a single reflow - the area array, which let interconnection scale with die area instead of die perimeter.

directness.counterfactual: Remove the 1962 practice and the parent has nothing to modify: no bumped devices, no Cr-Cu-Au terminals in production, no SLT reflow line or equipment, and no collapse problem to control - the parent's problem (soft pads collapsing and shorting) exists only because this practice put solder bumps on chips. The descent is documented in the child's own paper (SLT fabrication as the named wet-process exemplar; SLT tiles; 'the same automated equipment used for processing SLT modules') and in the programme historian's narration of the exact modification.
directness.evidence: Miller (1969), Introduction and Process sections; Totta's history: the 1962 reduction to practice, then 'glass dams were created to interrupt the solder coating on the electrodes which prevented the chip solder from wetting out and collapsing the chip without the need for copper ball standoffs. The name given to the development was controlled collapse chip connection or C4.' The intra-firm-formation attack is answered by these documents: the child's paper itself names the ancestor practice's fabrication line as its process home - documented consumption, not silent craft inheritance (the damascene-at-0.18um discipline).

Q1.evidence: Before this paper, extending a compiler's language by defining new constructs was not a designed capability: macros were assembler shorthand. The paper showed a compiler built from a small function set with conditional assembly and nested definitions could accept 'very general extensions to its ground language' - and its author later graded the deeper flip: macro processing is switching among data streams, the operation the memo proposes between programs.
Q1.source: McIlroy, CACM 3(4), 1960 (abstract); McIlroy interview (Mahoney), in Spinellis (ed.), The Oral History of Unix
Q1.falsification: Evidence that a general macro-extension mechanism, or the stream-switching view of it, was in print from another hand before April 1960.

Q2.evidence: Generative in both its own frame and the parent's: the paper founded the extensible-languages line, and the stream-switchyard model it gave its author is the seed of the whole composition space the memo opens - coupling arbitrary programs, IO included.
Q2.source: McIlroy interview (Mahoney), in Spinellis (ed.), The Oral History of Unix
Q2.falsification: A showing that the memo's coupling idea appears in McIlroy's record with no antecedent in his macro work.

Q3.evidence: Necessity is shared, and the sharing is documented by the author himself: his oral history names two ingredients - his macro work ('starting back in '59 or '60') and Conway's coroutines article. On the path that happened, the macro experience is the one he describes in mechanism detail ('Stop taking input from here, go take it from the definition'); but the memo might conceivably have been written from the coroutine ingredient alone, so necessity is partial, not sole.
Q3.source: McIlroy interview (Mahoney), in Spinellis (ed.), The Oral History of Unix
Q3.falsification: A document in which McIlroy attributes the coupling idea to a source other than his macro experience and Conway's article.

Q4.evidence: Macro extension collapsed the effort of growing a language (define, don't rebuild), but no period accounting grades the collapse as orders of magnitude, and for the parent's step the candidate is a concept source, not a cost event.
Q4.source: McIlroy, CACM 3(4), 1960
Q4.falsification: Period cost evidence for macro-compiler construction versus hand-built compilers.

Q5.falsification: A period measurement of macro processing.

Q6.falsification: Evidence the switchyard characterization is a later commentator's gloss, not McIlroy's own account of his macro work.

Q7.falsification: Evidence the 1960 macros could not be nested or composed.

Q8.falsification: Evidence of the stream-switching model at work in a second field before 1964.

Q9.falsification: Evidence macro-compiler users did not iterate by redefinition.

leap.prior_state: Programs ran one at a time on prepared files; composition meant writing intermediate results to files and running the next program by hand.
leap.jump: The memo proposed coupling programs like garden hose segments - screwing in another segment when data must be massaged another way - the founding statement of stream composition, IO included.

directness.counterfactual: Remove the author's macro work and its 1960 paper, and the memo loses the source experience its author himself names first: 'I had been doing macros, starting back in '59 or '60... macros mainly involve switching data streams... a macro processor as a switchyard for data streams.' The garden hose is that switchyard proposed between programs; without the decade of stream switching inside compilations, the 1964 proposal has no documented origin in its author's record.
directness.evidence: The channel is the author's own retrospective grading, twice stated (oral-history precis and the Tool Box chapter): the pipes idea 'sprang from the earlier use of macros', and macros 'mainly involve switching data streams'. Mediation check: no M sits between the paper and the memo - Conway's article (1963) is a parallel ingredient the author names alongside, not a carrier of the paper (the paper predates it by three years). Own-version discipline: this is a separable published artifact (CACM 3(4), 214-220) whose mechanism - stream switching - is consumed and reworked at a new scope (text streams within a compilation -> data streams between programs), the Ney-Essen-Kneser / Nowlan own-version exception shape, not Stirling-1719 identity.

Q1.evidence: Before Conway's paper, cooperating program parts could not suspend and resume each other symmetrically: control flow was hierarchical call-and-return. leap.prior_state: Estimation by least squares and moments, justified case by case; no measure of a sample's information content and no criterion for an estimate's efficiency.
leap.jump: Fisher's 1922 paper founds estimation theory: consistency, efficiency and sufficiency defined as criteria; maximum likelihood re-founded on the new concept of likelihood, extracted from inverse probability with its postulate removed; the information in a sample quantified, with an 'intrinsic accuracy' limiting any estimate.

directness.counterfactual: Remove Bayes's essay and the parent's sec. 6 loses its stated object: the paper defines likelihood AS the reinterpretation of 'BAYES' problem' - the binomial ratio p^x(1-p)^y retained, the postulate that made it a probability deleted. Fisher's confession (his 1912 statement 'based... upon the principle of inverse probability') routes the method's ancestry through the tradition this essay founded, and the apparatus cites the essay itself (ref. (10)), not a survey of it.
directness.evidence: Fisher (1922) sec. 6, pp. 326-327: 'Our interpretation of BAYES' problem, then, is that the likelihood of any value of p is proportional to p^x(1-p)^y, and is therefore a maximum when p = x/n, which is the best value obtainable from the sample'; reference list (10): 'BAYES (1763), An Essay towards Solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances, Phil. Trans. liii, p. 370.'

raw_candidates.name: Task-oriented dialogue systems
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Task-oriented dialogue systems directly framed the gap the agent leapt over: slot-filling bots were the incumbent the agent was compared against and displaced.
raw_candidates.source_title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Weng, 2023)
raw_candidates.definition: Pipeline or end-to-end neural dialogue systems that complete narrow tasks (booking, FAQ) by tracking dialogue state and filling slots.

raw_candidates.name: Robotic process automation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RPA directly enabled the agent's leap by defining the automation demand it displaced: brittle scripted UI automation was the prior state for 'software that does tasks'.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Birth of Agentic AI: A Convergence of Powers (Bornet et al.)
raw_candidates.definition: Software bots that automate repetitive desktop/web workflows by replaying recorded UI actions and rules.

raw_candidates.name: Deep Q-Networks (DQN)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DQN directly enabled the agent's leap as the prior paradigm of loop-based machine agency: agents that perceive, act, and learn from reward in an environment.
raw_candidates.source_title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Weng, 2023)
raw_candidates.definition: Deep reinforcement learning agents that learn action policies from raw pixel input and reward, demonstrating the perceive-act loop in games.

raw_candidates.name: Watson question answering
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Watson directly enabled the agent's leap as the prior state of machine question-answering over unstructured text that LLM agents were measured against.
raw_candidates.source_title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Weng, 2023)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's DeepQA system that won Jeopardy! by retrieving and ranking evidence-based answers over large text corpora.

raw_candidates.name: Siri voice assistant
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Siri directly enabled the agent's leap as the incumbent consumer assistant whose intent-slot limits defined what 'agent' had to surpass.
raw_candidates.source_title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Weng, 2023)
raw_candidates.definition: Apple's voice assistant that maps speech to a fixed set of intents and services on a phone.

raw_candidates.name: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RLHF directly enabled the agent's leap by making the underlying model steerable to human intent, so its reasoning could be trusted inside an action loop.
raw_candidates.source_title: Why is ChatGPT so good? (Scale AI)
raw_candidates.definition: Training recipe that fine-tunes a language model with a reward model learned from human preference rankings, aligning outputs with judged helpfulness.

raw_candidates.name: InstructGPT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: InstructGPT directly enabled the agent's leap by demonstrating that an RLHF-tuned model follows instructions reliably enough to be directed at open-ended tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: AI Paper Review: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
raw_candidates.definition: OpenAI's GPT-3 fine-tuned with supervised demonstrations plus RLHF; labelers preferred its outputs to a 100x larger base model.

raw_candidates.name: Instruction tuning (FLAN)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Instruction tuning directly enabled the agent's leap by converting a text completer into a model that follows natural-language task specifications, the control surface agents issue commands through.
raw_candidates.source_title: Why is ChatGPT so good? (Scale AI)
raw_candidates.definition: Fine-tuning language models on mixtures of tasks phrased as instructions, yielding zero-shot task following (FLAN, T0).

raw_candidates.name: Supervised fine-tuning on human demonstrations
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SFT on human demonstrations directly enabled the agent's leap by giving the base model the assistant behavior format that RLHF then refined and agents then drove.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Day We Stopped Predicting the Next Word: How ChatGPT Was Actually Built

candidate.causal_claim: WebArena directly enabled the agent's leap by grading agents on functional task completion in realistic self-hosted websites.
candidate.source_title: What is WebArena? The web-agent benchmark explained
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Zhou et al., CMU, 2023): 812 tasks on self-hosted e-commerce, forum, GitLab and CMS sites; best GPT-4 agent scored 14.41% vs 78.24% human.

candidate.name: Tree of Thoughts
candidate.causal_claim: Tree of Thoughts directly enabled the agent's leap by generalizing the reasoning step into search over thought branches with self-evaluation, the planning upgrade of 2023 agents.
candidate.source_title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Weng, 2023)
candidate.definition: Framework (Yao et al., 2023) for deliberate search over branching reasoning paths with LLM self-evaluation.

candidate.name: Direct preference optimization
candidate.causal_claim: DPO directly enabled the agent's leap by simplifying preference alignment into a single supervised objective agent builders could apply cheaply.
candidate.source_title: Classic Papers, Deep-Dived (agent papers database)
candidate.definition: Method (Rafailov et al., 2023) deriving preference fine-tuning directly from preference pairs without an explicit reward model or RL loop.

candidate.name: Reflexion
candidate.causal_claim: Reflexion directly enabled the agent's leap by giving agents verbal self-reflection stored in memory, measurably improving retry success (91% pass@1 on HumanEval).
candidate.source_title: Self-Improving AI Agents Explained: Reflection, Skills and Memory
candidate.definition: Framework (Shinn et al., Mar 2023): agents store natural-language reflections on failures in episodic memory and improve on retry.

candidate.name: Generative Agents
candidate.causal_claim: Generative Agents directly enabled the agent's leap by demonstrating the memory-stream + reflection + planning architecture for persistent agents.
candidate.source_title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior (arXiv:2304.03442)
candidate.definition: Stanford/Google system (Park et al., Apr 2023): 25 agents in a sandbox town with natural-language memory streams and periodic reflection.

candidate.name: HuggingGPT
candidate.causal_claim: HuggingGPT directly enabled the agent's leap by showing an LLM controller planning and delegating subtasks to a zoo of specialist models.
candidate.source_title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Weng, 2023)
candidate.definition: System (Shen et al., 2023) using ChatGPT as controller: task planning, model selection, execution, response generation over Hugging Face models.

candidate.name: Voyager
candidate.causal_claim: Voyager directly enabled the agent's leap by demonstrating lifelong learning in Minecraft via an ever-growing library of code skills.
candidate.source_title: Self-Improving AI Agents Explained: Reflection, Skills and Memory
candidate.definition: NVIDIA/Caltech agent (Wang et al., 2023) with automatic curriculum and a reusable skill library of executable code.

candidate.name: AutoGPT
candidate.causal_claim: AutoGPT directly enabled the agent's leap by popularizing the fully autonomous goal-loop agent in open source, defining the category the modern agent names.
candidate.source_title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Weng, 2023)
candidate.definition: Open-source project (Mar 2023) chaining GPT-4 calls in a self-directed loop toward a user-given goal.

candidate.name: ChatGPT plugins

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: 103M tokens from 28k verified-good Wikipedia articles.
raw_candidates.name: WikiText-103
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Gave language modeling a long-context Wikipedia benchmark corpus.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: ULMFiT's pretraining corpus and a standard LM benchmark.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: One billion words of news text with a fixed train/test split.
raw_candidates.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Standardized large-scale statistical language modeling evaluation.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: The benchmark of the large-LSTM LM era.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: One million words of Wall Street Journal text with POS tags and parse trees.
raw_candidates.name: Penn Treebank
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Provided parsed, tagged text that anchored LM and parsing research.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Standard LM testbed for two decades.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: A C-based platform exposing GPU thread hierarchies to developers.
raw_candidates.lineage: Infrastructure under all large LM training.
raw_candidates.name: CUDA
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Made GPUs programmable for general-purpose parallel computing.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: The compute substrate of the deep-learning era.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Dataflow graphs executed on CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs with automatic differentiation.
raw_candidates.lineage: Framework substrate of the pretraining era.
raw_candidates.name: TensorFlow
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Standardized building and training large neural networks across hardware.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Dominant research framework of the late 2010s.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Dynamic computation graphs with autograd over GPU tensors.
raw_candidates.lineage: Framework substrate of the pretraining era.
raw_candidates.name: PyTorch
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Made neural-network research programmable in imperative Python with GPU tensors.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Became the dominant research framework by 2019.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Hebbian traces modulated by learned coefficients, trained by gradient descent.
raw_candidates.name: Differentiable plasticity
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Learned per-connection plasticity rules for fast within-lifetime adaptation.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Fast-adaptation mechanism research line.

raw_candidates.key_mechanism: Per-parameter learned step sizes applied in inner-loop updates across tasks.
raw_candidates.name: Meta-SGD
raw_candidates.problem_solved: Meta-learned learning rates and update directions, not just initializations.
raw_candidates.scale_or_impact: Optimization-based meta-learning variant.

raw_candidates.name: Chain-of-thought prompting
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoT showed elicited reasoning traces dramatically raise LLM task accuracy; ReAct's thought actions are CoT traces interleaved with environment actions.
raw_candidates.definition: Prompting technique (Wei et al., 2022) in which few-shot exemplars contain step-by-step reasoning, eliciting intermediate reasoning from an LLM before its answer.
raw_candidates.source_title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: In-context learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct is delivered entirely as few-shot in-context exemplars: the thought-action-observation format exists only as prompt conditioning, the capability ICL established.
raw_candidates.definition: The ability of a pretrained LM (demonstrated at scale by GPT-3, 2020) to perform a new task from examples and instructions in its prompt, with no parameter updates.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

raw_candidates.name: Scratchpads
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Scratchpads showed models compute better when allowed to emit intermediate steps into a buffer; ReAct's thought stream is a scratchpad interleaved with actions.
raw_candidates.definition: Technique (Nye et al., 2021) training/prompting models to write intermediate computation into a 'scratchpad' before answering, improving multi-step arithmetic and code execution prediction.
raw_candidates.source_title: Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation with Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Least-to-most prompting
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Least-to-most decomposed hard problems into sequenced subproblems shortly before ReAct; a sibling prompting strategy for multi-step reasoning.
raw_candidates.definition: Prompting strategy (Zhou et al., 2022) that decomposes a problem into subproblems solved in sequence, each answer feeding the next prompt.
raw_candidates.source_title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Self-consistency
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Self-consistency improved CoT by sampling and marginalizing over reasoning paths; a decoding-side sibling of ReAct's single-trajectory loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Decoding strategy (Wang et al., 2022) sampling multiple CoT reasoning paths and taking the majority answer, substantially raising reasoning benchmark scores.
raw_candidates.source_title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models

raw_candidates.name: STaR: Self-Taught Reasoner
raw_candidates.causal_claim: STaR bootstrapped rationale generation from few exemplars, showing reasoning traces could be elicited and improved without large rationale datasets.
raw_candidates.definition: Bootstrapping method (Zelikman et al., 2022) in which a model generates rationales for problems, keeps those reaching correct answers, and fine-tunes on them.
raw_candidates.source_title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

raw_candidates.name: Zero-shot chain-of-thought
raw_candidates.causal_claim: 'Let's think step by step' showed reasoning traces could be elicited with no exemplars at all, sharpening the reasoning/acting contrast ReAct built on.
raw_candidates.definition: Finding (Kojima et al., 2022) that appending 'Let's think step by step' elicits reasoning traces from LLMs zero-shot, large gains on reasoning tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners

raw_candidates.name: Selection-inference
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Selection-inference decomposed reasoning into LLM selection and inference steps over facts, a modular sibling of ReAct's interleaving.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Creswell et al., 2022) alternating an LLM selection module (pick relevant facts) and inference module (derive one step), for faithful multi-step reasoning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Selection-Inference: Exploiting Large Language Models for Interpretable Logical Reasoning

raw_candidates.name: Decomposed prompting
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Decomposed prompting split complex tasks into sub-tasks routed to specialized LLM calls, a modular sibling architecture to ReAct's loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Approach (Khot et al., 2022) decomposing a complex task into sub-tasks, each handled by an LLM prompt or handler, composed by a controller.
raw_candidates.source_title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks

raw_candidates.name: Automatic prompt engineering
raw_candidates.causal_claim: APE automated the search for effective instructions, part of the 2022 prompting-methods wave surrounding ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Zhou et al., 2022) using an LLM to propose and select natural-language instructions automatically, matching human prompt engineering.
raw_candidates.source_title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers

raw_candidates.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct's experiments prompt GPT-3 and PaLM; the pretrained model is the substrate whose in-context behavior the ReAct format steers.
raw_candidates.definition: 175B-parameter autoregressive LM (Brown et al., 2020) whose few-shot in-context performance made prompt-based task specification practical at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

raw_candidates.name: PaLM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PaLM-540B was ReAct's strongest base model; its scale supplied the emergent reasoning ReAct's exemplars elicited.
raw_candidates.definition: 540B dense decoder LM (Chowdhery et al., 2022) trained with Pathways, showing strong emergent reasoning and few-shot performance.
raw_candidates.source_title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways

raw_candidates.name: Codex code generation model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct's GPT-3 experiments used the davinci-series API models descended from the GPT-3/Codex line; Codex showed prompted models executing structured action-like outputs.
raw_candidates.definition: GPT-3 fine-tuned on public code (Chen et al., 2021); powered GitHub Copilot and scored 28.8% on HumanEval, showing prompted models producing executable structured output.
raw_candidates.source_title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code

raw_candidates.name: Instruction tuning (FLAN)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: FLAN showed instruction-formatted multitask tuning unlocks zero-shot task following; ReAct instead used base models, but FLAN defined the instruction-following contrast class.
raw_candidates.definition: Fine-tuning a 137B LM on 60+ datasets phrased as instructions (Wei et al., 2021), yielding large zero-shot gains on unseen task types.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners

raw_candidates.name: Hosted LLM APIs (OpenAI API)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ReAct was run through hosted API access to GPT-3-class models; API serving made prompt-loop experiments a commodity.
raw_candidates.definition: Commercial API access to GPT-3 (June 2020), which turned large-model prompting into an on-demand service any researcher could loop over.
raw_candidates.source_title: OpenAI API announcement

raw_candidates.name: LaMDA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LaMDA demonstrated dialog-tuned LLMs at scale in early 2022, part of the model wave ReAct drew on; not used in ReAct's experiments.
raw_candidates.definition: Dialog-specialized LLM family (Thoppilan et al., 2022) fine-tuned for grounded, sensible conversation.
raw_candidates.source_title: LaMDA: Language Models for Dialog Applications

raw_candidates.name: Chinchilla
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Chinchilla reset the compute-optimal scaling recipe in 2022; a scaling-law sibling result, not an input to ReAct's method.
raw_candidates.definition: 70B LM (Hoffmann et al., 2022) establishing compute-optimal parameter/token balance, outperforming much larger models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Gopher
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Gopher was a 280B contemporary of the models ReAct used, documenting emergent few-shot abilities at scale.
raw_candidates.definition: 280B LM (Rae et al., 2021) from DeepMind with extensive analysis of scale-driven capability gains and risks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Language Models: Methods, Analysis & Insights from Training Gopher

raw_candidates.name: T5 text-to-text framework
raw_candidates.causal_claim: T5 unified tasks as text-to-text, an ancestor of the prompt-as-interface idea ReAct exploits; ReAct used decoder LMs, not T5.
raw_candidates.definition: Transfer-learning framework (Raffel et al., 2019) casting every NLP task as text-in/text-out, with an 11B encoder-decoder model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT established the pretrain-then-adapt paradigm ReAct inherited, but ReAct's generative prompting bypassed encoder fine-tuning entirely.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: GPT-2
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 first showed conditioning alone elicits tasks zero-shot, the direct empirical precedent for the prompting substrate ReAct builds on.
raw_candidates.definition: 1.5B LM (Radford et al., 2019) demonstrating zero-shot task transfer by text conditioning, improving log-linearly with scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

raw_candidates.name: SayCan
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SayCan grounded LLM plans in robot affordances months before ReAct; the leading sibling approach to LLM acting, compared against ReAct's setting.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Ahn et al., 2022) pairing an LLM's task knowledge ('Say') with learned affordance values ('Can') to ground plans for a mobile manipulator.
raw_candidates.source_title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

raw_candidates.name: Inner Monologue
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Inner Monologue fed environment feedback back into an LLM planner in text form, the closest contemporaneous sibling to ReAct's observation loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Huang et al., 2022) giving an LLM planner textual environment feedback (success detection, scene description) for closed-loop robotic planning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models

raw_candidates.name: MRKL systems
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MRKL routed LLM calls to external tools and knowledge sources months before ReAct; the verifier already flagged it as ReAct's near-simultaneous multiple.
raw_candidates.definition: Neuro-symbolic architecture (Karpas et al., 2022) in which an LLM router dispatches to expert modules: calculators, APIs, knowledge bases.
raw_candidates.source_title: MRKL Systems: A modular, neuro-symbolic architecture that combines large language models, external knowledge sources and discrete reasoning

raw_candidates.name: Language models as zero-shot planners
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Huang et al. showed LLMs could decompose embodied tasks into executable steps zero-shot, defining the act-only baseline ReAct's reasoning was measured against.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Huang et al., 2022) translating LLM-generated high-level plans into admissible embodied actions via sentence-embedding matching.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents

raw_candidates.name: WebGPT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WebGPT fine-tuned GPT-3 to browse the web with search and citation actions, an early demonstration of an LLM operating a tool interface in a loop.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Nakano et al., 2021) fine-tuning GPT-3 to use a text-based browser (search, click, scroll) and answer questions with citations, preferred over humans on ELI5.
raw_candidates.source_title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

raw_candidates.name: ProgPrompt
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ProgPrompt generated program-like robot plans with assertion-based recovery, a code-as-policy sibling of ReAct's loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Singh et al., 2022) prompting LLMs to emit Pythonic robot action programs with assertions enabling environment feedback and recovery.
raw_candidates.source_title: ProgPrompt: Generating Situated Robot Task Plans using Large Language Models

raw_candidates.name: Gato
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Gato showed a single transformer acting across embodiments and modalities in 2022; a generalist-agent sibling, not an input to ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Multi-modal, multi-task agent (Reed et al., 2022): one 1.2B transformer playing Atari, captioning images, and controlling a robot arm.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Generalist Agent

raw_candidates.name: Decision Transformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Decision Transformer reframed RL as sequence modeling over trajectories, part of the transformer-meets-acting wave; ReAct's acting is prompt-based, not return-conditioned.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Chen et al., 2021) casting offline RL as conditional sequence modeling, generating actions from desired returns and past trajectories.
raw_candidates.source_title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Trajectory Transformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Trajectory Transformer modeled offline RL trajectories for planning by beam search; a sequence-modeling sibling with no channel into ReAct.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Janner et al., 2021) modeling distributions over trajectories with a transformer and planning via beam search.
raw_candidates.source_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning as One Big Sequence Modeling Problem

raw_candidates.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: RAG coupled an LM to a retriever for knowledge tasks; ReAct's Wikipedia actions generalize that retrieve-then-reason pattern into an interactive loop.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Lewis et al., 2020) combining a pretrained retriever with a generator, state of the art on open-domain QA at introduction.
raw_candidates.source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

raw_candidates.name: Dense passage retrieval
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DPR made neural retrieval the default knowledge-access layer for QA systems of ReAct's era; ReAct used the Wikipedia API's own search instead.
raw_candidates.definition: Dual-encoder retriever (Karpukhin et al., 2020) outperforming BM25 by wide margins on open-domain QA retrieval.
raw_candidates.source_title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

raw_candidates.name: REALM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: REALM pretrained with retrieval in the loop, an ancestor of retrieve-while-reasoning; ReAct's retrieval happens at inference via actions, not in pretraining.
raw_candidates.definition: Pretraining framework (Guu et al., 2020) augmenting an LM with a neural retriever trained end-to-end on a Wikipedia corpus.
raw_candidates.source_title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training

raw_candidates.name: ALFWorld
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ALFWorld was one of ReAct's two headline testbeds (+34 over baselines); its text-game alignment of embodied tasks made the acting loop measurable.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Shridhar et al., 2020) aligning the ALFRED embodied instruction dataset with interactive text games, enabling text-agent evaluation of embodied tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning

raw_candidates.name: WebShop
raw_candidates.causal_claim: WebShop was ReAct's second headline testbed (+10); a coeval benchmark, built independently of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Simulated e-commerce environment (Yao et al., 2022) with 1.18M products and 12k instructions for evaluating web-shopping agents.
raw_candidates.source_title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents

raw_candidates.name: HotpotQA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: HotpotQA was ReAct's multi-hop QA testbed, where its Wikipedia search actions were exercised; the benchmark predates and did not shape the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Yang et al., 2018) of 113k multi-hop questions requiring reasoning over multiple Wikipedia paragraphs, with supporting-fact annotations.
raw_candidates.source_title: HotpotQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering

raw_candidates.name: FEVER
raw_candidates.causal_claim: FEVER was ReAct's fact-verification testbed; its retrieve-and-verify task shape matches ReAct's action set but predates the method by four years.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Thorne et al., 2018) of 185k claims labeled Supported/Refuted/NotEnoughInfo against Wikipedia evidence.
raw_candidates.source_title: FEVER: a large-scale dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification

raw_candidates.name: TextWorld
raw_candidates.causal_claim: TextWorld made text-game agent research a commodity platform; ALFWorld's design descends from it, so its channel to ReAct runs through ALFWorld.
raw_candidates.definition: Microsoft learning environment (Cote et al., 2018) for generating and solving text-based games, used to train and evaluate RL language agents.
raw_candidates.source_title: TextWorld: A Learning Environment for Training Reinforcement Learning Agents, Inspired by Text-based Games

raw_candidates.name: BabyAI

candidate.name: Gato
