raw_candidates.name: Generative pretraining (GPT-1)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1 is GPT-2's literal predecessor in the same lab: the Transformer-decoder generative-pretraining recipe GPT-2 scaled 10x and pushed from fine-tuning to zero-shot conditioning.
raw_candidates.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2018): a 117M Transformer decoder pretrained on BooksCorpus, then fine-tuned per task, beating purpose-built models on 9 of 12 language-understanding tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

raw_candidates.name: ULMFiT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

raw_candidates.name: ELMo
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
raw_candidates.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

raw_candidates.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
raw_candidates.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

raw_candidates.name: Layer normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Layer Normalization

raw_candidates.name: Adam optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.name: GELU activation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
raw_candidates.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

raw_candidates.name: BooksCorpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

raw_candidates.name: Common Crawl
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
raw_candidates.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Common Crawl

raw_candidates.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

raw_candidates.name: AlexNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
raw_candidates.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
raw_candidates.source_title: CUDA

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation

raw_candidates.name: LSTM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Bahdanau attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
raw_candidates.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

raw_candidates.name: MAML meta-learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
raw_candidates.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
raw_candidates.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

raw_candidates.name: Matching Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Prototypical Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

raw_candidates.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
raw_candidates.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

raw_candidates.name: Perplexity as LM metric
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
raw_candidates.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Perplexity

raw_candidates.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
raw_candidates.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Penn Treebank

raw_candidates.name: TensorFlow
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
raw_candidates.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
raw_candidates.source_title: TensorFlow

raw_candidates.name: PyTorch
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.
raw_candidates.definition: Facebook's open-source deep-learning framework (2016) with dynamic computation graphs.
raw_candidates.source_title: PyTorch

raw_candidates.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture pattern (Li et al., 2014) scaling ML training across clusters via parameter servers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

raw_candidates.name: Curriculum learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Strategy (Bengio et al., 2009) presenting training examples in a meaningful order to improve generalization and speed.
raw_candidates.source_title: Curriculum Learning

raw_candidates.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Work (Graves, 2013) using LSTMs with mixture-density outputs to generate handwriting and text sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CoVe contextual vectors
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
raw_candidates.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

raw_candidates.name: GloVe
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GloVe was the other embedding standard of the word2vec era; the embedding premise reaches GPT-2 through the pretraining tradition, and GPT-2 learns its embeddings end-to-end regardless.
raw_candidates.definition: Embedding method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factorizing global co-occurrence statistics.
raw_candidates.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

raw_candidates.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
raw_candidates.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

raw_candidates.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.
raw_candidates.definition: Research programme (Thrun & Pratt, eds., 1998) on learning inductive bias from task families.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Learn

raw_candidates.name: Neural Turing Machines
raw_candidates.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.name: Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
raw_candidates.source_title: Memory Networks

card.name: CUDA GPU computing
card.definition: Software platform (NVIDIA, 2007): the parallel programming model and runtime that made NVIDIA GPUs programmable for general-purpose computation - the layer every deep-learning training stack of the 2010s executed on.

card.name: cuDNN
card.definition: Library (NVIDIA, 2014): GPU-accelerated primitives for deep neural networks (convolutions, RNNs, normalization, attention helpers), implemented as CUDA kernels and called by training frameworks.

judge_queue.note: gray-zone band 0.80-0.92; adjudicate SAME / DIFFERENT / SUBTYPE

raw_candidates.name: Generative pretraining (GPT-1)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1 is GPT-2's literal predecessor in the same lab: the Transformer-decoder generative-pretraining recipe GPT-2 scaled 10x and pushed from fine-tuning to zero-shot conditioning.
raw_candidates.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2018): a 117M Transformer decoder pretrained on BooksCorpus, then fine-tuned per task, beating purpose-built models on 9 of 12 language-understanding tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

raw_candidates.name: ULMFiT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

raw_candidates.name: ELMo
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
raw_candidates.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

raw_candidates.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
raw_candidates.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

raw_candidates.name: Layer normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Layer Normalization

raw_candidates.name: Adam optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.name: GELU activation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
raw_candidates.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

raw_candidates.name: BooksCorpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

raw_candidates.name: Common Crawl
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
raw_candidates.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Common Crawl

raw_candidates.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

raw_candidates.name: AlexNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
raw_candidates.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
raw_candidates.source_title: CUDA

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation

raw_candidates.name: LSTM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning

raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Child et al., 2019, OpenAI): factorized strided+local attention patterns reducing self-attention complexity for long sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sparse attention - LLM Wiki

raw_candidates.name: Megatron-LM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3 required model parallelism at 175B; Megatron-LM is the prominent 2019 demonstration of tensor parallelism - but no record shows GPT-3's training consumed NVIDIA's implementation rather than OpenAI's own.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA framework (Shoeybi et al., 2019): intra-layer tensor model parallelism for training multi-billion-parameter Transformers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism

raw_candidates.name: Scaling laws for neural language models (Kaplan et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3's 175B size choice follows the Kaplan scaling-law analysis from the same lab months earlier - coeval at year granularity.
raw_candidates.definition: Empirical study (Kaplan et al., Jan 2020, OpenAI): loss follows power laws in model size, data, and compute, prescribing much larger models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

raw_candidates.name: CTRL conditional language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A parallel demonstration of steerable large LMs; not part of GPT-3's lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Keskar et al., 2019, Salesforce): 1.6B LM steered by control codes.
raw_candidates.source_title: CTRL: A Conditional Transformer Language Model for Controllable Generation

raw_candidates.name: T5 text-to-text transfer Transformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A parallel pretraining paradigm (fine-tune per task); GPT-3's paper contrasts its in-context approach rather than consuming T5.
raw_candidates.definition: Model/framework (Raffel et al., 2019, Google): unified text-to-text format with encoder-decoder Transformer pretrained on C4.
raw_candidates.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

raw_candidates.name: SuperGLUE benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3 was evaluated on SuperGLUE few-shot; an evaluation target, not an enabler of the leap.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark suite (Wang et al., 2019) of hard language-understanding tasks.
raw_candidates.source_title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems

raw_candidates.name: Natural Questions dataset
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A GPT-3 few-shot evaluation set, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019, Google): real search queries with Wikipedia answers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research

raw_candidates.name: Winogrande dataset
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A GPT-3 evaluation set, not an enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Sakaguchi et al., 2019): large-scale Winograd-style commonsense benchmark.
raw_candidates.source_title: Winogrande: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale

raw_candidates.name: WebText corpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3 trained on WebText2, an expanded version of GPT-2's WebText - the channel runs through GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (OpenAI, 2019): web pages from outbound Reddit links, built for GPT-2.
raw_candidates.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

raw_candidates.name: Microsoft-OpenAI Azure supercomputing partnership
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3's training run executed on the Microsoft-built cluster - an institutional/compute precondition rather than a technical milestone in the lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Partnership (announced Jul 2019): Microsoft invested $1B in OpenAI to build Azure AI supercomputing for large-model training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Microsoft invests in OpenAI (2019 announcement)

raw_candidates.name: DeepSpeed ZeRO optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not part of GPT-3's training stack on the record.
raw_candidates.definition: Library (Rajbhandari et al., 2020, Microsoft): memory-optimization for distributed training.
raw_candidates.source_title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models

raw_candidates.name: ELECTRA
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020) and a parallel paradigm.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Clark et al., 2020, Google): replaced-token-detection pretraining.
raw_candidates.source_title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators

raw_candidates.name: Reformer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not consumed by it.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Kitaev et al., 2020): LSH attention and reversible layers for efficient Transformers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer

raw_candidates.name: Deep RL from human preferences (Christiano et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Christiano-style preference learning directly enabled the agent's leap as the first demonstration that human comparisons could train a reward model guiding behavior — the seed of RLHF.
raw_candidates.source_title: Why is ChatGPT so good? (Scale AI)
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Christiano et al., 2017) learning a reward model from human preferences over trajectory segments and optimizing it with RL.

raw_candidates.name: PPO (proximal policy optimization)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PPO directly enabled the agent's leap as the optimization algorithm that ran the RLHF stage aligning the agent's engine.
raw_candidates.source_title: The Day We Stopped Predicting the Next Word: How ChatGPT Was Actually Built
raw_candidates.definition: Policy-gradient RL algorithm (Schulman et al., 2017) with clipped surrogate objective; the standard optimizer for RLHF.

raw_candidates.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-3-scale pretraining directly enabled the agent's leap by producing a single model with enough world knowledge and few-shot adaptability to serve as a general task engine.
raw_candidates.source_title: AI Paper Review: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
raw_candidates.definition: Training very large autoregressive language models on web-scale text; GPT-3 (175B) showed few-shot in-context task performance without fine-tuning.

raw_candidates.name: Fine-tuning language models from human preferences (Ziegler et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The first application of preference-based reward learning to language models - the direct methodological bridge between Christiano et al. 2017 and Stiennon et al. 2020 / InstructGPT.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Ziegler et al., 2019, OpenAI): train a reward model from human comparisons and fine-tune a pretrained LM (GPT-2) with PPO under a KL penalty.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences - ADS

raw_candidates.name: Learning to summarize from human feedback (Stiennon et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The immediate predecessor of InstructGPT: same recipe, same lab, six shared authors; proved RLHF beats supervised baselines and human reference summaries.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Stiennon et al., 2020, OpenAI): full RLHF recipe - human comparisons, Bradley-Terry reward model, PPO with reference-KL penalty - applied to summarization at 1.3B-6.7B scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to summarize from human feedback

raw_candidates.name: TRPO (trust region policy optimization)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PPO's direct predecessor; the RLHF lineage consumed the simplified PPO, not TRPO itself.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Schulman et al., 2015): policy updates constrained to a trust region via KL bound, with monotonic-improvement guarantees.
raw_candidates.source_title: Trust Region Policy Optimization

raw_candidates.name: Bradley-Terry model of paired comparisons
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The preference-model form inside every RLHF reward model - but it reached RLHF packaged inside Christiano et al.'s reward-learning method.
raw_candidates.definition: Statistical model (Bradley & Terry, 1952): probability that one item beats another is a logistic function of latent scores.
raw_candidates.source_title: Rank Analysis of Incomplete Block Designs

raw_candidates.name: Inverse reinforcement learning (Ng & Russell)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The intellectual ancestor of reward learning; RLHF's channel runs through preference-based reward learning (Christiano), not demonstration-based IRL.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Ng & Russell, 2000): recover a reward function from an expert's observed behavior.
raw_candidates.source_title: Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: Apprenticeship learning via inverse RL (Abbeel & Ng)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A demonstration-based precursor; not the channel into preference-based RLHF.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Abbeel & Ng, 2004): match an expert's feature expectations to learn near-expert policies without a reward function.
raw_candidates.source_title: Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning

raw_candidates.name: TAMER framework (Knox & Stone)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: An early human-feedback RL channel, but evaluative rather than preference-comparison based; the InstructGPT lineage runs through Christiano/Ziegler/Stiennon.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Knox & Stone, 2009): agents learn from human evaluative feedback (+/-) treated as reward.
raw_candidates.source_title: Interactively Shaping Agents via Human Reinforcement

raw_candidates.name: Preference-based reinforcement learning (Wirth et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The formal backdrop Christiano et al. operationalized at deep-RL scale in the same year; the consumed artifact in the lineage is Christiano's method.
raw_candidates.definition: Survey/formalization (Wirth et al., 2017) of RL from trajectory preferences rather than numeric rewards.
raw_candidates.source_title: Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning: A Formal Framework and a Survey

raw_candidates.name: WebGPT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: A sibling application of human-feedback fine-tuning, not an enabler of the RLHF recipe itself.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Nakano et al., 2021, OpenAI): GPT-3 fine-tuned with human feedback to answer questions using a text browser.
raw_candidates.source_title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

raw_candidates.name: InstructGPT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with the RLHF node itself (same year, same work) - cannot be its predecessor at year granularity.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Ouyang et al., 2022, OpenAI): SFT + RLHF on GPT-3 - the very system this graph's RLHF node is drawn from.
raw_candidates.source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

raw_candidates.name: Constitutional AI
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022) and a parallel branch, not a predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Bai et al., 2022, Anthropic): RL from AI feedback (RLAIF) using a written constitution.
raw_candidates.source_title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

raw_candidates.name: Sparrow dialogue agent
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022); a parallel application.
raw_candidates.definition: System (Glaese et al., 2022, DeepMind): dialogue agent trained with human judgements and rule-based rewards.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements

raw_candidates.name: Direct preference optimization (DPO)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Postdates the RLHF node (2022) - a successor/simplification, not a predecessor.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Rafailov et al., 2023): optimize policies directly on preference data, bypassing an explicit reward model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Direct Preference Optimization

raw_candidates.name: TL;DR summarization dataset
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The task substrate for Stiennon et al.'s demonstration - its channel into RLHF runs through that paper.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Reddit TL;DR posts with author-written summaries), used by Ziegler and Stiennon for RLHF summarization experiments.
raw_candidates.source_title: TL;DR dataset (Reddit summarization corpus)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Amodei et al. directly enabled RLHF's leap by posing, in 2016, the two problems the recipe is built to answer: reward hacking (a learned proxy gets gamed) and scalable supervision (the true objective is too expensive to evaluate often).
raw_candidates.definition: Amodei, Olah, Steinhardt, Christiano, Schulman & Mane's 2016 agenda paper naming five concrete accident problems in ML systems: side effects, reward hacking, scalable supervision, safe exploration, distributional shift.
raw_candidates.name: Concrete problems in AI safety (Amodei et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety (arXiv:1606.06565)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Leike et al. directly enabled RLHF's leap by posing the alignment problem in exactly the form RLHF answers for language models: separate learning what to achieve (a reward model from human feedback) from learning how (RL optimization).
raw_candidates.definition: Leike, Krueger, Everitt, Martic, Maini & Legg's 2018 research-direction paper (DeepMind) defining the agent alignment problem and proposing reward modeling - learn the reward from user feedback, optimize it with RL - as the scalable route.
raw_candidates.name: Scalable agent alignment via reward modeling (Leike et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Scalable agent alignment via reward modeling: a research direction (arXiv:1811.07871)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: CIRL directly enabled RLHF's leap by giving the value alignment problem its formal statement - behavior aligned to a human reward function the machine does not start out knowing - which RLHF operationalizes with rankings instead of demonstrations.
raw_candidates.definition: Hadfield-Menell, Dragan, Abbeel & Russell's NIPS 2016 formal definition of the value alignment problem as a cooperative partial-information game in which the robot must infer the human's unknown reward function.
raw_candidates.name: Cooperative inverse reinforcement learning (Hadfield-Menell et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning (NIPS 2016, arXiv:1606.03137)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The specification gaming catalogue directly enabled RLHF's leap by documenting the obstruction its design defends against - optimizers exploiting gaps between the stated objective and the intent - which is why the recipe keeps the policy on a KL leash to the reference model and iterates the reward model.
raw_candidates.definition: Krakovna and colleagues' catalogue (maintained since 2018; DeepMind synthesis 'Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity', April 2020) of ~60 documented cases of agents satisfying the literal specification of an objective without achieving the intended outcome.
raw_candidates.name: Specification gaming catalogue (Krakovna et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: Specification gaming (glossary synthesis of Krakovna et al.'s DeepMind catalogue)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: RealToxicityPrompts directly enabled RLHF's leap by measuring the deployment obstruction - raw pretrained models reliably produce toxic, unhelpful text - that RLHF's judged-helpfulness training was built to remove, and on whose terms (reduced toxicity) InstructGPT reports gains.
raw_candidates.definition: Gehman, Gururangan, Sap, Choi & Smith's EMNLP 2020 Findings testbed: 100K naturally occurring prompts showing pretrained LMs degenerate into toxic text even from innocuous prompts, with no failsafe mitigation available at the time.
raw_candidates.name: RealToxicityPrompts (Gehman et al.)
raw_candidates.source_title: RealToxicityPrompts: Evaluating Neural Toxic Degeneration in Language Models (Findings of EMNLP 2020)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Iterated amplification directly enabled RLHF's leap by diagnosing, inside OpenAI itself, the obstruction RLHF answers differently: the training signal for capable systems cannot come from direct human demonstration or evaluation alone.
raw_candidates.definition: Christiano, Shlegeris & Amodei's 2018 paper (OpenAI) posing the scalable-oversight obstruction - how to train systems on tasks too complex for humans to evaluate directly - and proposing iterated amplification as one answer.
raw_candidates.name: Supervising strong learners by amplifying weak experts (Christiano, Shlegeris & Amodei)
raw_candidates.source_title: Supervising strong learners by amplifying weak experts (arXiv:1810.08575)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The InstructGPT preference dataset directly enabled RLHF's leap by being the consumed training signal - the rankings the reward model was fit to and the demonstrations the SFT stage cloned.
raw_candidates.definition: The data collected for the InstructGPT paper: prompts drawn from real OpenAI API traffic plus labeler-written prompts, with demonstrations and K-way rankings of model outputs produced by about 40 screened labelers (roughly 33k training prompts for the reward model).
raw_candidates.name: InstructGPT human preference dataset
raw_candidates.source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT, arXiv:2203.02155)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Azure supercomputer directly enabled RLHF's leap by being the machine GPT-3 was trained on and within whose fleet the RLHF fine-tuning runs executed - the physical plant of the 2022 recipe.
raw_candidates.definition: The Azure-hosted supercomputer built with and exclusively for OpenAI, announced at Build in May 2020: a single system of over 285,000 CPU cores and 10,000 GPUs with 400 Gb/s networking per GPU server, ranked top-five on the TOP500; GPT-3 was trained on it.
raw_candidates.name: Microsoft Azure AI supercomputer for OpenAI
raw_candidates.source_title: Microsoft announces new supercomputer, lays out vision for future AI work (Microsoft, May 2020)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The V100 directly enabled RLHF's leap by being the accelerator the base model's training - and the fine-tuning compute of the RLHF era at OpenAI - actually ran on.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's Volta-generation datacenter GPU (2017), the cluster unit of GPT-3's paper-documented training hardware and of the Azure supercomputer's 10,000-GPU fleet (assumed V100s in contemporary reporting).
raw_candidates.name: NVIDIA V100 GPU
raw_candidates.source_title: Microsoft's Massive AI Supercomputer on Azure: 285k CPU Cores, 10k GPUs (HPCwire, May 2020)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA directly enabled RLHF's leap by being the programmability layer the entire training stack - base model and fine-tuning alike - was programmed through on NVIDIA hardware.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's parallel computing platform and programming model (2007) that made GPUs programmable for general computation - the layer through which the RLHF training stack's kernels execute.
raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.source_title: Microsoft's Massive AI Supercomputer on Azure (HPCwire, May 2020)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: cuDNN directly enabled RLHF's leap by supplying the tuned GPU kernels the RLHF training runs executed on the Azure fleet.
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated library of deep-neural-network primitives (2014), the kernel layer frameworks dispatch to on NVIDIA hardware.
raw_candidates.name: cuDNN
raw_candidates.source_title: Microsoft's Massive AI Supercomputer on Azure (HPCwire, May 2020)

raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

raw_candidates.name: ULMFiT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
raw_candidates.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

raw_candidates.name: ELMo
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
raw_candidates.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
raw_candidates.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bengio's NPLM founded neural language modeling - distributed word representations learned jointly with the LM; the deep ancestor of the pretraining lineage, reaching GPT-2 through GPT-1 and the Transformer succession.
raw_candidates.definition: Model (Bengio et al., 2003) learning distributed word embeddings jointly with a neural LM, beating n-gram models on perplexity.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

raw_candidates.name: Word2vec
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Mikolov et al., 2013) learning word embeddings from co-occurrence prediction at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

raw_candidates.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent neural LM (Mikolov et al., 2010) reducing perplexity and WER substantially over backoff n-gram models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

raw_candidates.name: Byte-pair encoding for NMT
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BPE subword segmentation is GPT-2's tokenization family (byte-level BPE); the segmentation scheme was inherited as part of the GPT-1 recipe and tooling.
raw_candidates.definition: Segmentation method (Sennrich et al., 2016) applying byte-pair encoding to learn subword units, fixing rare-word handling in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

raw_candidates.name: Layer normalization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
raw_candidates.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
raw_candidates.source_title: Layer Normalization

raw_candidates.name: Adam optimizer
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
raw_candidates.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
raw_candidates.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

raw_candidates.name: GELU activation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
raw_candidates.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

raw_candidates.name: BooksCorpus
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
raw_candidates.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

raw_candidates.name: Common Crawl
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
raw_candidates.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
raw_candidates.source_title: Common Crawl

raw_candidates.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
raw_candidates.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
raw_candidates.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

raw_candidates.name: AlexNet
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
raw_candidates.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
raw_candidates.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CUDA GPU computing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
raw_candidates.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
raw_candidates.source_title: CUDA

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
raw_candidates.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation

raw_candidates.name: LSTM
raw_candidates.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
raw_candidates.source_title: Long short-term memory

raw_candidates.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
raw_candidates.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
raw_candidates.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: Bahdanau attention
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
raw_candidates.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

raw_candidates.name: MAML meta-learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
raw_candidates.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
raw_candidates.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

raw_candidates.name: Matching Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Prototypical Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

raw_candidates.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

raw_candidates.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
raw_candidates.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
raw_candidates.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

raw_candidates.name: Perplexity as LM metric
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
raw_candidates.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
raw_candidates.source_title: Perplexity

raw_candidates.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

raw_candidates.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
raw_candidates.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
raw_candidates.source_title: Penn Treebank

raw_candidates.name: TensorFlow
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
raw_candidates.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
raw_candidates.source_title: TensorFlow

raw_candidates.name: PyTorch
raw_candidates.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.
raw_candidates.definition: Facebook's open-source deep-learning framework (2016) with dynamic computation graphs.
raw_candidates.source_title: PyTorch

raw_candidates.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture pattern (Li et al., 2014) scaling ML training across clusters via parameter servers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

raw_candidates.name: Curriculum learning
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.
raw_candidates.definition: Strategy (Bengio et al., 2009) presenting training examples in a meaningful order to improve generalization and speed.
raw_candidates.source_title: Curriculum Learning

raw_candidates.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.
raw_candidates.definition: Work (Graves, 2013) using LSTMs with mixture-density outputs to generate handwriting and text sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

raw_candidates.name: CoVe contextual vectors
raw_candidates.lens: immediate prior state of the art
raw_candidates.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
raw_candidates.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

raw_candidates.name: GloVe
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GloVe was the other embedding standard of the word2vec era; the embedding premise reaches GPT-2 through the pretraining tradition, and GPT-2 learns its embeddings end-to-end regardless.
raw_candidates.definition: Embedding method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factorizing global co-occurrence statistics.
raw_candidates.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

raw_candidates.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
raw_candidates.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

raw_candidates.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.
raw_candidates.definition: Research programme (Thrun & Pratt, eds., 1998) on learning inductive bias from task families.
raw_candidates.source_title: Learning to Learn

raw_candidates.name: Neural Turing Machines
raw_candidates.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

raw_candidates.name: Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
raw_candidates.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
raw_candidates.source_title: Memory Networks

raw_candidates.name: End-to-End Memory Networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.

candidate.name: Neural probabilistic language model

candidate.name: Word2vec
candidate.causal_claim: Word2vec industrialized learned embeddings, the representation premise pretraining scaled; it reaches GPT-2 through the whole pretraining tradition.

candidate.source_title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

candidate.name: RNN language modeling (Mikolov)
candidate.causal_claim: Mikolov's RNNLM showed neural LMs decisively beating n-gram baselines, restarting LM research as a neural discipline; an ancestor at several removes.

candidate.source_title: Recurrent neural network based language model

candidate.name: Layer normalization
candidate.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
candidate.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.

candidate.name: Adam optimizer

candidate.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

candidate.name: GELU activation
candidate.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
candidate.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
candidate.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

candidate.name: BooksCorpus
candidate.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.

candidate.name: Common Crawl

candidate.source_title: Common Crawl

candidate.name: AlexNet

candidate.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
candidate.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

candidate.name: CUDA GPU computing
candidate.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.

candidate.source_title: CUDA

candidate.name: Backpropagation
candidate.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
candidate.source_title: Backpropagation

candidate.name: LSTM
candidate.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.

candidate.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
candidate.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
candidate.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
candidate.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

candidate.name: Bahdanau attention
candidate.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
candidate.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
candidate.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

candidate.name: Matching Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.

candidate.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

candidate.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
candidate.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
candidate.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

candidate.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
candidate.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
candidate.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
candidate.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

candidate.name: Perplexity as LM metric
candidate.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
candidate.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
candidate.source_title: Perplexity

candidate.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.

candidate.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

candidate.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.

candidate.source_title: Penn Treebank

candidate.name: TensorFlow

candidate.name: PyTorch

candidate.name: Curriculum learning
candidate.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.

candidate.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.

candidate.name: cuDNN

candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard LM technology for three decades.

candidate.name: TRPO (trust region policy optimization)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO's direct predecessor - PPO is explicitly 'a first-order approximation of TRPO' that keeps its stability without second-order machinery.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Schulman et al., 2015): policy updates constrained to a trust region via a KL bound, with monotonic-improvement guarantees.
candidate.source_title: Trust Region Policy Optimization

candidate.name: REINFORCE (Williams)
candidate.causal_claim: The founding policy-gradient method; the entire lineage PPO belongs to descends from it.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Williams, 1992): gradient ascent on expected reward using sampled returns - the original policy-gradient estimator.
candidate.source_title: Simple statistical gradient-following algorithms for connectionist reinforcement learning

candidate.name: Policy gradient theorem (Sutton et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The mathematical foundation that makes policy-gradient methods (REINFORCE, actor-critic, TRPO, PPO) well-defined.
candidate.definition: Theorem (Sutton, McAllester, Singh & Mansour, 2000): the gradient of expected return can be written without differentiating the state distribution.
candidate.source_title: Policy Gradient Methods for Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation

candidate.name: Actor-critic methods (Konda & Tsitsiklis)
candidate.causal_claim: The variance-reduction architecture inside TRPO/PPO practice - but consumed packaged in those methods, not directly.
candidate.definition: Framework (Konda & Tsitsiklis, 2000-2003): a critic estimates values to reduce the variance of an actor's policy-gradient updates.
candidate.source_title: Actor-Critic Algorithms

candidate.name: Natural policy gradient (Kakade)
candidate.causal_claim: The intellectual parent of trust-region methods; its channel into PPO runs through TRPO.
candidate.definition: Method (Kakade, 2002): follow the gradient in the Fisher-information metric rather than raw parameter space.
candidate.source_title: A Natural Policy Gradient

candidate.name: Conservative policy iteration (Kakade & Langford)
candidate.causal_claim: An early improvement-guarantee method whose lineage runs into TRPO.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Kakade & Langford, 2002): conservative mixture updates with approximate monotonic improvement guarantees.
candidate.source_title: Approximately Optimal Approximate Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: Generalized advantage estimation (GAE)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO's companion estimator - the advantage signal PPO's clipped objective consumes in standard implementations (and in all RLHF codebases).
candidate.definition: Estimator (Schulman et al., 2016): exponentially-weighted advantage estimates trading bias against variance via a lambda parameter.
candidate.source_title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation

candidate.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN)
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel value-based lineage; PPO's policy-gradient family does not consume it.
candidate.definition: System (Mnih et al., 2015): value-based deep RL with experience replay and target networks, reaching human-level Atari play.
candidate.source_title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning

candidate.name: A3C asynchronous actor-critic
candidate.causal_claim: A contemporary baseline PPO was compared against, not an input to it.
candidate.definition: Method (Mnih et al., 2016): asynchronous parallel actor-learners for actor-critic RL.
candidate.source_title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: OpenAI Gym
candidate.causal_claim: Infrastructure the RL community used, but not a causal input to PPO's algorithm.
candidate.definition: Toolkit (Brockman et al., 2016): standardized RL environments and evaluation protocol.
candidate.source_title: OpenAI Gym

candidate.name: Importance sampling for off-policy evaluation (Precup et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO's probability-ratio objective is importance-sampling-flavored, but the consumed formulation arrives via TRPO's surrogate objective.
candidate.definition: Technique (Precup, Sutton & Dasgupta, 2000): reweight trajectories from a behavior policy to evaluate a target policy.
candidate.source_title: Eligibility Traces for Off-Policy Policy Evaluation

member_names: Importance sampling for off-policy evaluation (Precup et al.)

candidate.name: DDPG (deep deterministic policy gradient)
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel off-policy lineage; not consumed by PPO.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Lillicrap et al., 2016): off-policy deterministic actor-critic for continuous control.
candidate.source_title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning
