raw_candidates.causal_claim: Microsoft's Xbox 360 graphics brief posed the unified-shader problem in shipped form a year before the G80: a console GPU requirement, designed with ATI over about two years, that made dynamic load balancing across one shader array a product requirement.
raw_candidates.definition: Microsoft's 2003-era design requirement for its second console's graphics chip, executed by ATI as Xenos - the commission that first made a unified shader array a shipping product.
raw_candidates.name: Xbox 360 graphics design brief (Microsoft)
raw_candidates.source_title: Microsoft & ATI unveil Xbox 360 GPU (2005 reportage)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: Inside NVIDIA, the design brief that produced the G80 was posed around 2002: over the four-year design, the observation that people were increasingly using graphics hardware for non-graphics work was turned into an explicit requirement - a direct computing mode rather than graphics in disguise (Kirk's retrospective account).
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's internal G80 design requirement, as later described by chief scientist David Kirk: the chip was designed over roughly four years with general-purpose use as a stated goal.
raw_candidates.name: NVIDIA's GPGPU design requirement (the four-year G80 brief)
raw_candidates.source_title: Nvidia Takes Fresh Tack In PC Graphics (CRN, Nov 2006)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The diagnosis the unified array answers: in split pipelines, vertex and pixel units idle whenever a scene's load is unbalanced, so peak throughput is unreachable in principle - an inefficiency named in architecture analyses of the DX9 generation and in NVIDIA's own retrospective ('Outstanding performance with a unified shader design' is the brief's answer to it).
raw_candidates.definition: The analysed structural defect of separate vertex/pixel pipelines - static partitioning wastes whichever array the current workload does not need - documented in mid-2000s architecture analyses and retrospectives.
raw_candidates.name: Split-pipeline load-imbalance diagnosis
raw_candidates.source_title: NVIDIA Tesla: A Unified Graphics and Computing Architecture (Lindholm et al., IEEE Micro 2008)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The early GPGPU literature diagnosed exactly what the G80's compute hardware removes: no scatter, no integer operations, no shared memory or inter-thread communication, and programs forced to masquerade as rendering - the limitation list (Purcell et al. 2002 and successors) that the Tesla architecture's design answers point by point.
raw_candidates.definition: The 2002-2004 analyses of programmable graphics hardware as a computer (Purcell et al.'s ray-tracing work; Thompson et al.'s framework analysis) cataloguing the graphics API's limits for general computation.
raw_candidates.name: Early GPGPU limitation analyses
raw_candidates.source_title: The Evolution of GPU Computing (Steve Scott, SC12)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The scalar-efficiency argument is the diagnosis behind the G80's most distinctive choice: vec4 shader units waste most of their width on the scalar-heavy instruction mixes of real shaders, so a scalar unit at a higher clock beats a wider vector unit - the argument the Tesla design adopted against both its own predecessors and Xenos's 5-wide vectors.
raw_candidates.definition: The utilisation analysis of vector shader units under real instruction mixes, used in the Tesla architecture's rationale for scalar stream processors (Lindholm et al. 2008).
raw_candidates.name: Vector-unit underutilisation diagnosis (the scalar argument)
raw_candidates.source_title: Tesla (microarchitecture) (Wikipedia)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The R580 was the incumbent the G80 displaced at launch: ATI's 48-pixel-shader split design held the high end through 2006, and the G80's reviews define its leap against it.
raw_candidates.definition: ATI's January 2006 flagship (Radeon X1900 XTX): 48 pixel shader units with a separate vertex array - the most powerful split-pipeline GPU ever shipped.
raw_candidates.name: Radeon X1900 XTX (R580)
raw_candidates.source_title: Radeon X1000 series (Wikipedia)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The G71 was NVIDIA's own incumbent flagship in the G80's launch year - the product the 8800 GTX replaced in the line and the split-design endpoint inside the company.

raw_candidates.name: GeForce 7900 GTX (G71)
raw_candidates.source_title: GeForce 7 series (Wikipedia)

raw_candidates.source_title: PhysX (Wikipedia)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The R400 is the negative space of the unified idea: ATI's own first attempt at a unified PC GPU was cancelled (its work reportedly fed the console design instead), showing the leap had been attempted and abandoned once before it shipped in Xenos and the G80.

raw_candidates.name: Self (programming language)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Self directly enabled JavaScript's leap by supplying its object model: Eich took prototype-based delegation - objects inheriting from other objects, with no classes - from Self as one of the design's three named pillars.
raw_candidates.source_title: SELF: The Power of Simplicity (Ungar & Smith, OOPSLA 1987)
raw_candidates.definition: Ungar and Smith's prototype-based object-oriented language (OOPSLA 1987; public releases from Stanford from 1990, then Sun Labs), in which objects are slot collections that inherit by delegating to prototypes rather than instantiating classes.

raw_candidates.name: Scheme
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Scheme directly enabled JavaScript's leap by supplying its function semantics: first-class functions, closures and lexical scoping are the Scheme core Eich kept under the Java-like syntax.
raw_candidates.source_title: Scheme: An Interpreter for Extended Lambda Calculus (Sussman & Steele, 1975)
raw_candidates.definition: Sussman and Steele's minimalist Lisp dialect (MIT AI Memo 349, 1975), the first Lisp with lexical scoping and first-class closures as the language's foundation.

raw_candidates.name: HyperTalk
raw_candidates.causal_claim: HyperTalk directly enabled JavaScript's leap by supplying the interaction model: scripts written by non-programmers, attached to visible page objects and fired by events, which the browser language re-created for HTML documents.
raw_candidates.source_title: JavaScript: The First 20 Years (HOPL)
raw_candidates.definition: The scripting language of Apple's HyperCard (1987, by Dan Winkler), in which end users attached English-like event-handler scripts to cards and buttons.

raw_candidates.name: AWK
raw_candidates.causal_claim: AWK directly enabled JavaScript's leap as one of Eich's cited influences: its associative arrays and pattern-action text processing fed the new language's object-as-map and string handling for page data.
raw_candidates.source_title: JavaScript (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: Aho, Weinberger and Kernighan's Unix text-processing language (Bell Labs, 1977), built on associative arrays and pattern-action rules.

raw_candidates.name: Smalltalk-80
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Smalltalk-80 directly enabled JavaScript's leap by establishing the message-passing object model and live-object culture that Self simplified and Eich drew on.
raw_candidates.source_title: JavaScript: The First 20 Years (HOPL)
raw_candidates.definition: Xerox PARC's object-oriented language and environment (publicly released 1980), in which everything is an object and computation is message passing.

raw_candidates.name: Java (programming language)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Java directly enabled JavaScript's leap by supplying the syntax skin and marketing frame management mandated: the new language had to 'look like Java' while remaining a lightweight scripting companion.
raw_candidates.source_title: JavaScript (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: Sun Microsystems' class-based language, publicly launched in May 1995 with the HotJava browser and the applet model of downloadable code.

raw_candidates.name: Scheme
raw_candidates.causal_claim: JavaScript is the Scheme-embedding plan altered: Eich was hired to put Scheme in the browser, and the shipped language is that plan recombined - Scheme's semantics retained, its surface replaced under the look-like-Java mandate.
raw_candidates.source_title: Brendan Eich (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: Sussman and Steele's minimalist Lisp dialect (MIT AI Memo 349, 1975), the first Lisp with lexical scoping and first-class closures as the language's foundation.

raw_candidates.name: Self (programming language)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: JavaScript is Self's object model modified for the browser: Self's uniform slot and delegation machinery simplified into constructor functions plus a prototype property, small enough to implement in ten days.
raw_candidates.source_title: SELF: The Power of Simplicity (Ungar & Smith, OOPSLA 1987)
raw_candidates.definition: Ungar and Smith's prototype-based object-oriented language (OOPSLA 1987; public releases from Stanford from 1990, then Sun Labs), in which objects are slot collections that inherit by delegating to prototypes rather than instantiating classes.

raw_candidates.name: HyperTalk
raw_candidates.causal_claim: JavaScript is HyperTalk's card-scripting ancestor modified: the same event-handler scripts for non-programmers, moved from HyperCard stacks to HTML pages and given a C-like surface.
raw_candidates.source_title: JavaScript: The First 20 Years (HOPL)
raw_candidates.definition: The scripting language of Apple's HyperCard (1987, by Dan Winkler), in which end users attached English-like event-handler scripts to cards and buttons.

raw_candidates.name: HTML forms (in NCSA Mosaic)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: HTML forms posed the problem JavaScript answers: once pages could collect input (Mosaic, 1993), validating and reacting to that input without a server round-trip became the browser's missing capability - form validation was Mocha's canonical first use.
raw_candidates.source_title: 1993: CGI Scripts and Early Server-Side Web Programming (Cybercultural)
raw_candidates.definition: The fill-in form elements implemented in NCSA Mosaic (1993) and later standardized in HTML 2.0, which let pages submit user input to servers.

raw_candidates.name: Visual Basic
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Visual Basic posed the role JavaScript fills: a component-scripting language for non-specialists alongside a professional systems language - Netscape's Java-for-components / Mocha-for-scripters split was explicitly analogized to the C++ / Visual Basic pairing on Windows.
raw_candidates.source_title: History of JavaScript: From Netscape to ECMAScript (Code Carbon)
raw_candidates.definition: Microsoft's visual component-programming system (1991) that made application scripting by non-professional programmers a mass practice on Windows.

raw_candidates.name: HyperCard
raw_candidates.causal_claim: HyperCard posed the problem at mass scale: millions of non-programmers authoring interactive, scripted documents - the demand a browser scripting language had to meet for the web's documents.
raw_candidates.source_title: JavaScript: The First 20 Years (HOPL)
raw_candidates.definition: Apple's hypermedia authoring system (1987, Bill Atkinson), which put scripted interactive stacks in the hands of end users.

raw_candidates.name: ViolaWWW
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ViolaWWW posed and prototyped the problem: the first browser with embedded scriptable objects and page applets (1992) showed what page scripting was for, three years before the mass-market browser adopted it.
raw_candidates.source_title: ViolaWWW (Wikipedia)
raw_candidates.definition: Pei-Yuan Wei's Unix browser (March 1992), the first to embed scriptable objects and applets in web pages, built on his Viola object toolkit at UC Berkeley's XCF.

raw_candidates.name: Ousterhout's two-language doctrine
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Ousterhout's doctrine diagnosed the obstruction JavaScript answers: applications need two languages - a systems language for components and a scripting language for gluing - articulated in his Tcl book (1994); Netscape's Java-plus-Mocha strategy is that diagnosis applied to the browser.
raw_candidates.source_title: History of Tcl (Ousterhout)
raw_candidates.definition: John Ousterhout's argument, developed from Tcl (1988) and stated in 'Tcl and the Tk Toolkit' (1994), that software splits into system programming languages and scripting/glue languages with different design optima.

raw_candidates.name: Netscape's assessment that Java was unsuited to page authors

candidate.definition: Ritchie and Thompson's systems language (Bell Labs, 1972), the implementation language of the browser and the ancestor of the C-family syntax JavaScript wears.

raw_candidates.name: Elman recurrent network
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's architecture is the Elman network trained as a language model: a simple recurrent network whose hidden layer is copied to context units and fed back, so the state summarizes an unbounded history - the component the 2010 model incorporates wholesale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finding Structure in Time (Elman, 1990)
raw_candidates.definition: Jeffrey Elman's simple recurrent network (Cognitive Science, 1990): a feedforward network with a context layer copying the hidden state, giving the network a trainable memory of the recent past; its tasks were next-item prediction tasks, and it explicitly develops Jordan's 1986 proposal.

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation through time
raw_candidates.causal_claim: BPTT is the training procedure the parent incorporates: the 2010 model is trained by unfolding the recurrent network through time and applying backpropagation - Werbos's 1990 formalization is the standard account the field trains by.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation Through Time (D2L)
raw_candidates.definition: Werbos's procedure (Proceedings of the IEEE, 1990) for training recurrent networks: unfold the network through time and apply backpropagation through the unfolded copies.

raw_candidates.name: Backpropagation (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Backpropagation is the learning rule inside every weight update of the parent; the 2010 model's training is backpropagation specialized through time.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation Through Time (D2L)
raw_candidates.definition: The 1986 Nature paper's generalized delta rule - gradient descent on network error by chain-rule propagation - the learning algorithm of the connectionist era.

raw_candidates.name: Class-based n-gram models (Brown et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's output layer incorporates Brown clustering's factorization: words are grouped into classes and the model predicts class-then-word, the class-based decomposition the 2010 architecture uses to keep its output layer tractable.
raw_candidates.source_title: Class-Based n-gram Models of Natural Language (Brown et al., 1992)
raw_candidates.definition: Brown, Della Pietra, deSouza, Lai and Mercer's IBM method (Computational Linguistics 18(4), 1992): words clustered into classes by mutual information so that n-gram probabilities factor through the classes.

raw_candidates.name: Jordan network
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Jordan network is the other founding recurrent design - outputs fed back as context - which Elman's 1990 paper explicitly develops from; the parent's recurrence concept descends from this pair.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finding Structure in Time (Elman, 1990)
raw_candidates.definition: Michael Jordan's recurrent architecture (1986) feeding the network's previous outputs back as context inputs - the proposal Elman's hidden-state recurrence explicitly develops.

raw_candidates.name: Neural probabilistic language model (Bengio et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent is the feedforward neural LM modified by recurrence: Bengio et al. replaced n-gram counting with learned word embeddings and a neural probability function over a fixed window; Mikolov's move is to make the context the network's own recurrent state.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Probabilistic Language Models - explainer
raw_candidates.definition: Bengio, Ducharme, Vincent and Jauvin's model (JMLR, 2003): words embedded in a continuous vector space, a feedforward network estimating the next word's probability from a fixed-length window - the founding neural language model.

raw_candidates.name: Continuous space language models (Schwenk)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schwenk's continuous-space LM is the direct ancestor in the speech-recognition line: the architecture (projection layer plus feedforward network) that the Brno group extended, and the comparison point the 2010 paper's own slides distinguish their feedforward setup from.
raw_candidates.source_title: Continuous Space Language Models and related work (Schwenk, MT Marathon 2010 / PBML 93)
raw_candidates.definition: Holger Schwenk's continuous space language model (Computer Speech & Language 21(3), 2007): a neural LM engineered for large-vocabulary speech recognition, whose projection-layer architecture became the field's reference design.

raw_candidates.name: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model (Morin & Bengio)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Morin and Bengio's hierarchical decomposition of the output vocabulary is the ancestor the 2010 paper cites (its reference [11]) for making neural LM output layers tractable - the problem the parent instead answers with class factorization.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent Neural Network Based Language Model (Mikolov et al., Interspeech 2010)
raw_candidates.definition: Morin and Bengio's 2005 model arranging the vocabulary in a binary tree so next-word probability is a product of decisions along a path, cutting the output layer's cost.

raw_candidates.name: Shannon's prediction and entropy of printed English
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shannon posed the problem the parent works on: predicting the next symbol of English text, with entropy as its measure - the 1951 guessing-game paper defines language modeling as a task.
raw_candidates.source_title: Prediction and Entropy of Printed English (Shannon, 1951)
raw_candidates.definition: Shannon's 1951 Bell System Technical Journal paper: the guessing-game experiment measuring how predictable the next letter of English is, bounding the entropy of printed English at roughly 0.6-1.3 bits per letter with 100 letters of context.

raw_candidates.name: DARPA CSR task definition (WSJ benchmark)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The CSR corpus design (Paul & Baker, 1992) posed the shared task: large-vocabulary continuous speech recognition on Wall Street Journal text, with fixed training data and NIST-administered benchmark tests - the arena the parent's word-error-rate claims are made in.
raw_candidates.source_title: ACL Data Collection Initiative / WSJ CSR corpus
raw_candidates.definition: The design (Paul & Baker, 1992) of the Wall Street Journal-based CSR corpus and its benchmark tests: a general-purpose, large-vocabulary, high-perplexity recognition task with shared data and centrally administered scoring.

raw_candidates.name: The curse of dimensionality diagnosis (Bengio et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 2003 paper's motivating diagnosis - discrete word histories make n-gram estimation collapse under data sparseness, because the number of possible contexts grows exponentially while observations do not - is the obstruction statement the whole neural-LM line, the parent included, is written against.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural Probabilistic Language Models - explainer
raw_candidates.definition: The diagnosis stated in Bengio et al. (2003): language modeling suffers a curse of dimensionality - a word sequence's probability must generalize across an exponential space of histories from finite data - which continuous word representations were proposed to cure.

raw_candidates.name: Bengio, Simard & Frasconi on learning long-term dependencies
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 1994 analysis diagnosed why recurrent training is hard - gradient descent struggles to learn long-term dependencies - the standing obstruction the parent's simple architecture and training regime had to live with.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation Through Time (D2L)
raw_candidates.definition: Bengio, Simard and Frasconi's 1994 analysis (IEEE Trans. Neural Networks) of the difficulty of learning long-term dependencies with gradient descent in recurrent networks.

raw_candidates.name: Hochreiter's 1991 diploma thesis analysis of vanishing and exploding gradients (Untersuchungen zu dynamischen neuronalen Netzen)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Hochreiter's 1991 diagnosis of vanishing and exploding gradients is the obstruction statement for all recurrent training; the parent's answer is pragmatic (simple architecture, truncated training) rather than the gated answer his own later work gave.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation Through Time (D2L)
raw_candidates.definition: Sepp Hochreiter's 1991 diploma thesis (TU Munich) identifying the vanishing/exploding gradient problem in recurrent networks - the diagnosis the LSTM design answers.

raw_candidates.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney is the incumbent the parent defines itself against: the parent paper's named baseline (KN5) and its interpolation partner - the strongest classical estimator, whose perplexity the recurrent model roughly halves.
raw_candidates.source_title: Improved Backing-Off for M-Gram Language Modeling (Kneser & Ney, 1995)
raw_candidates.definition: Kneser and Ney's smoothing (ICASSP 1995): absolute discounting plus a continuation-probability lower-order distribution - the strongest classical n-gram estimator.

raw_candidates.name: Katz backoff
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Katz backoff is the classical architecture the parent's mixtures replace: fall back to shorter contexts when longer ones are unobserved - the design the KN5 baseline itself builds on.
raw_candidates.source_title: Speech and Language Processing, Kneser-Ney appendix (Jurafsky & Martin)
raw_candidates.definition: Slava Katz's backoff scheme (1987): when a longer context is unobserved, fall back to shorter contexts with discounted probabilities.

raw_candidates.name: Stupid backoff and web-scale n-gram counts (Brants et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Brants et al. is the scale-first rival: enormous count tables with a deliberately simple backoff, which the field's survey literature records as the web-scale tendency - the alternative the parent's compact recurrent model answers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Continuous Space Language Models and related work (Schwenk, MT Marathon 2010 / PBML 93)
raw_candidates.definition: Brants et al.'s 2007 demonstration that enormous count tables (Google's Web 1T 5-grams) with a deliberately simple backoff scheme beat sophisticated smoothing at web scale.

raw_candidates.name: Good-Turing estimation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Good-Turing is the root of the incumbent's machinery: the estimate that unseen events' probability mass equals the proportion of events seen exactly once underlies every smoothing method the parent competes with.
raw_candidates.source_title: Empirical Estimates of Parameter Distributions (Chen thesis, incl. Good-Turing)
raw_candidates.definition: I.J. Good's elaboration (1953) of Turing's wartime estimator: the probability of unseen events is estimated from the count of events seen exactly once - the root of all smoothing.

raw_candidates.name: Deleted interpolation (Jelinek & Mercer)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Deleted interpolation is the incumbent's combination recipe: mixing n-gram estimates of different orders with estimated weights - the form the parent's own RNN-plus-KN mixtures inherit.
raw_candidates.source_title: Perplexity (AI Research Center glossary)
raw_candidates.definition: Jelinek and Mercer's deleted interpolation (1980): combining n-gram estimates of different orders with data-estimated weights, from IBM's speech recognition program.

raw_candidates.name: Long short-term memory (LSTM)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The LSTM is the road not taken inside the parent's own design space: the gated recurrent architecture existed for thirteen years, and the 2010 paper's claim is precisely that the SIMPLE recurrent network - not the gated one - suffices for language modeling at scale.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation Through Time (D2L)
raw_candidates.definition: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's gated recurrent architecture (1997) preserving gradient flow over long spans with a constant error carousel - the era's engineered answer to recurrent training difficulty.

raw_candidates.name: Bidirectional recurrent neural networks
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The bidirectional RNN is the sibling recurrent design not used: reading the sequence in both directions, inapplicable to left-to-right prediction - its exclusion defines the parent's causal design choice.
raw_candidates.source_title: Backpropagation Through Time (D2L)
raw_candidates.definition: Schuster and Paliwal's bidirectional recurrent network (1997), running one recurrent layer forward and one backward over the sequence.

raw_candidates.name: Discriminative language models for ASR (Roark et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Discriminative LMs are the alternative paradigm in the parent's own comparison table (its slide deck tabulates a discriminative-LM row): globally normalized models trained to discriminate correct transcripts, which did not become the parent's generative approach.
raw_candidates.source_title: Recurrent Neural Network Based Language Model - slide deck (Mikolov)
raw_candidates.definition: Roark, Saraclar and Collins's discriminative language models (2004): globally normalized models trained to discriminate correct transcripts - the alternative paradigm to generative language modeling.

raw_candidates.name: Wall Street Journal corpus / DARPA CSR
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The WSJ CSR corpus is the data the parent consumes: its training subsets (6.4M words) and its WSJ'92/'93 evaluation sets are the paper's primary experiments, rescored as 100-best lists.
raw_candidates.source_title: ACL Data Collection Initiative / WSJ CSR corpus
raw_candidates.definition: The CSR corpus built on Wall Street Journal text (designed by Paul & Baker, 1992; collected at MIT-LCS, SRI and TI): 47M words of text and hundreds of hours of read speech, with the WSJ'92 and WSJ'93 evaluation sets.

raw_candidates.name: Distributed representations (Hinton, McClelland & Rumelhart)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's first component is imported whole from this chapter: a concept - here, a word - is represented not by a symbol but by a pattern of activity over many units, so similarity becomes proximity of vectors; the 2003 model learns exactly such a representation for each word.
raw_candidates.source_title: Geoffrey Hinton - Curriculum Vitae (publications list)
raw_candidates.definition: The Parallel Distributed Processing volume 1 chapter (1986) stating the connectionist representation doctrine: concepts as patterns of activation distributed over many units, similar concepts as nearby patterns.

raw_candidates.name: Learning distributed representations of concepts (Hinton)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The learning half of the doctrine: this paper showed distributed representations can be LEARNED by a network from examples rather than hand-designed - the parent learns its word vectors by training, following this demonstration.
raw_candidates.source_title: Geoffrey E. Hinton's Publications: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.definition: Hinton's 1986 Cognitive Science Society paper showing a network can learn distributed representations of concepts, reprinted in the PDP literature.

raw_candidates.name: Perceptron (Rosenblatt)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's architecture descends from the perceptron line: layered adaptive units trained from examples; the multi-layer network computing the parent's probability function is this design's descendant.
raw_candidates.source_title: Geoffrey E. Hinton's Publications: Backpropagation
raw_candidates.definition: Frank Rosenblatt's perceptron (1958): a trainable layered network of threshold units - the ancestor artifact of every multi-layer network, the parent's included.

raw_candidates.name: Modeling high-dimensional discrete data with multi-layer neural networks (Bengio & Bengio)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's own section 1.2 names this the prior demonstration: neural networks can model joint distributions of high-dimensional discrete variables by factorizing them into conditionals estimated by a multi-layer network - the 2003 paper applies exactly this recipe to word sequences.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio, Ducharme & Vincent, NIPS 2000)
raw_candidates.definition: Yoshua and Samy Bengio's NIPS 12 paper (2000): an autoregressive multi-layer network modeling joint distributions over high-dimensional discrete variables; cited by the parent (with its journal companion) as its references [2]/[3].

raw_candidates.name: Taking on the curse of dimensionality in joint distributions using neural networks (S. Bengio & Y. Bengio)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The companion statement of the group's program: the curse in joint distributions is the named enemy and neural factorization the proposed weapon - the framing the parent inherits verbatim for language modeling.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio, Ducharme & Vincent, NIPS 2000)
raw_candidates.definition: Samy and Yoshua Bengio's IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks paper (11(3):550-557, 2000) arguing neural networks can take on the curse of dimensionality in joint distributions.

raw_candidates.name: Sequential neural text compression (Schmidhuber & Heil)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's section 1.2 acknowledges this line as related work: neural networks had already been used autoregressively on text (at character level, for compression) - a prior existence proof that a neural net can model text sequences probabilistically.
raw_candidates.source_title: Neural language models - the Schmidhuber priority case (retrospective survey)
raw_candidates.definition: Schmidhuber and Heil's neural text-compression work (NIPS 1994; IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks 1996): an autoregressive neural model predicting the next character, later pressed as a priority claim against the parent.

raw_candidates.name: Natural language processing with modular PDP models (Miikkulainen & Dyer)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: An early demonstration that distributed representations inside neural networks could process language structure (stories, case roles) - part of the prior neural-language record behind the parent's 'the idea is not new' acknowledgment.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model - An Explainer
raw_candidates.definition: Risto Miikkulainen and Michael Dyer's modular connectionist NLP work (book, 1991): networks with distributed representations processing sentences and stories.

raw_candidates.name: Maximum entropy language modeling (Rosenfeld)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The strongest non-neural generalization program of the era: maximum-entropy models integrated heterogeneous features (triggers, class information) into one exponential model - the alternative answer to sparsity against which the parent's learned-representation answer is positioned.
raw_candidates.source_title: Brief History of Language Modeling - from counting to attention
raw_candidates.definition: Ronald Rosenfeld's maximum-entropy language modeling program (from 1994-96): a unified exponential model combining n-gram counts with long-distance features.

raw_candidates.name: Prediction and entropy of printed English (Shannon)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Shannon posed the problem the parent works on: predict the next symbol of English and measure its entropy - the founding task definition of language modeling and the source of its measure.
raw_candidates.source_title: Brief History of Language Modeling - from counting to attention
raw_candidates.definition: Shannon's 1951 guessing-game experiments bounding the entropy of printed English - the founding statement of next-symbol prediction as a measurable task.

raw_candidates.name: Continuous speech recognition by statistical methods (Jelinek)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Jelinek's IBM program posed statistical language modeling as an engineering task inside speech recognition - the arena, and the trigram tradition, in which the parent's claims are made and measured.
raw_candidates.source_title: Brief History of Language Modeling - from counting to attention
raw_candidates.definition: Frederick Jelinek's 1976 IEEE paper founding the IBM statistical approach to speech recognition, in which the language model is a statistical component estimated from text.

raw_candidates.name: Curse of dimensionality (Bellman)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The diagnosis gets its hearing here (routed from RNNLM's expansion, session 12): the parent's abstract and first section name the curse of dimensionality as the intrinsic difficulty of its problem and define the contribution as fighting it; the term and the exponential-growth diagnosis are Bellman's coinage.
raw_candidates.source_title: Curse of dimensionality (Bellman's coinage)
raw_candidates.definition: Richard Bellman's coinage (Dynamic Programming, 1957; phrasing popularized in Adaptive Control Processes, 1961): the exponential growth of volume and state space with dimension that defeats tabular methods.

raw_candidates.name: Good-Turing estimation
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Good and Turing's estimate specified the unseen-events obstruction quantitatively - how much probability mass belongs to events never observed - the precise statistical form of the sparsity problem inside n-gram estimation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Brief History of Language Modeling - from counting to attention
raw_candidates.definition: The 1953 estimator (Turing's wartime method, published by I. J. Good) assigning probability mass to unseen events from the count of events seen exactly once - the statistical core of smoothing.

raw_candidates.name: Katz back-off
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The incumbent machinery the parent's introduction positions itself against: back-off trigram models (Katz, 1987) are named in the paper as the traditional approach, which generalizes only by concatenating very short sequences seen in training.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio et al., JMLR 3, 2003)
raw_candidates.definition: Slava Katz's 1987 back-off estimator: use the longest context with a reliable count, discounted, and fall back to shorter contexts - the standard trigram machinery of the era.

raw_candidates.name: Deleted interpolation (Jelinek & Mercer)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Consumed, not merely compared: the parent's headline numbers are mixtures of the neural model with an interpolated trigram - remove deleted interpolation and the 252-perplexity headline result does not exist in its reported form.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio et al., JMLR 3, 2003)
raw_candidates.definition: Jelinek and Mercer's 1980 smoothing method: blend n-gram estimates of several orders with weights fitted on held-out data - the mixture partner inside the parent's best reported results.

raw_candidates.name: Class-based n-gram models (Brown et al.)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The strongest incumbent in the parent's own table: the Brown-corpus headline is measured against the class-based back-off model with 500 classes (perplexity 312) - the counting tradition's own attempt to share strength across similar words.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio et al., JMLR 3, 2003)
raw_candidates.definition: Brown, Della Pietra, deSouza, Lai and Mercer's method (Computational Linguistics, 1992): words clustered into classes so n-gram probabilities factor through the classes, sharing counts among similar words.

raw_candidates.name: A bit of progress in language modeling (Goodman)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The counting tradition's high-water mark, cited by the parent: Goodman showed how far combining many n-gram tricks goes - the combined state of the art the neural approach had to beat on its own terms.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio et al., JMLR 3, 2003)
raw_candidates.definition: Joshua Goodman's 2001 synthesis of n-gram improvements (caching, clustering, skipping and more), cited by the parent as the counting approach's best combined form.

raw_candidates.name: Empirical study of smoothing techniques (Chen & Goodman)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The study that standardized which smoothing counts as state of the art - the baseline discipline the parent's comparison tables follow when they report modified Kneser-Ney numbers.
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio et al., JMLR 3, 2003)
raw_candidates.definition: Stanley Chen and Joshua Goodman's 1999 empirical comparison establishing the ranking of smoothing methods the field, and the parent's tables, use.

raw_candidates.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The strongest single incumbent the parent is measured against: on AP News the best n-gram in the parent's table is the 5-gram Kneser-Ney back-off model (perplexity 117) - the number the neural model's 109 is reported against. (Already a node in this graph, admitted at RNNLM's expansion.)
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio et al., JMLR 3, 2003)
raw_candidates.definition: Kneser and Ney's smoothing (1995): back-off weights driven by the number of distinct contexts a word appears in - the strongest counting estimator of the era.

raw_candidates.name: Elman recurrent network
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The road not taken, present in the parent's own design space: the probability function could have been a recurrent network over an unbounded history; the parent instead fixes a window of word vectors and uses a feedforward network - the design is defined against the recurrent alternative. (Already a node in this graph.)
raw_candidates.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model (Bengio, Ducharme & Vincent, NIPS 2000)
raw_candidates.definition: Jeffrey Elman's simple recurrent network (1990): a feedforward network with a context layer copying the hidden state, giving a trainable memory of the past.

raw_candidates.name: Latent semantic analysis (Deerwester et al.)

raw_candidates.name: Serial-order recurrent network (Jordan, 1986)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The direct ancestor, modified - in the paper's own abstract: 'The current report develops a proposal along these lines first described by Jordan (1986) which involves the use of recurrent links in order to provide networks with a dynamic memory.' Jordan's network (the paper's Figure 1) feeds OUTPUT patterns back through state/plan units; Elman's modification copies the HIDDEN-unit pattern back as context units, so the memory is the network's own learned internal representation rather than its behavior.
raw_candidates.source_title: Serial Order: A Parallel Distributed Processing Approach (Jordan, 1986; ICS Report 8604, UCSD Institute for Cognitive Science)
raw_candidates.definition: Jordan's serial-order network (ICS Report 8604, UCSD, 1986): a recurrent network for producing sequences, in which plan units and feedback from the output layer ('state units') give the network a context for the next element - the first PDP proposal for dynamic memory through recurrence.

raw_candidates.name: Time-delay neural network (Waibel et al., 1989)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The strongest form of the incumbent approach the paper argues against: the parent cites Waibel et al. (1987, ATR TR-I-0006 - the report version of the TDNN) among the time-delay designs in which time is laid out spatially over tapped delay lines, the representation strategy the recurrent proposal replaces.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finding Structure in Time (Elman, 1990)
raw_candidates.definition: Time-delay neural network (Waibel et al., 1989; ATR report 1987): a feedforward network whose units receive inputs over a window of time delays, learning shift-invariant temporal features (phoneme recognition) - time represented as space.

raw_candidates.name: Concentrating partial information in a recurrent network (Tank & Hopfield, 1987)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: One of the recurrent proposals the paper's Section 2 surveys (Tank & Hopfield, 1987): recurrent dynamics used to accumulate partial information over time - part of the small 1986-88 recurrent literature the parent situates itself in, though the parent modifies Jordan's design, not this one.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finding Structure in Time (Elman, 1990)
raw_candidates.definition: Tank & Hopfield (1987): a recurrent (Hopfield-style) network that concentrates partial, time-arriving information into a collective decision - recurrence as analog accumulation.

raw_candidates.name: Recurrent backpropagation (Pineda, 1988)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cited in the paper's Section 2 survey of recurrent proposals: Pineda's (1988) algorithm for training recurrent networks - the road the parent conspicuously does not take, since its recurrent connections are fixed at 1.0 and untrained.
raw_candidates.source_title: Finding Structure in Time (Elman, 1990)
raw_candidates.definition: Recurrent backpropagation (Pineda, 1988): a generalization of backpropagation that computes gradients for recurrent networks by solving for the fixed point of the network's dynamics.

card.definition: Ziv & Lempel's 1978 dictionary compressor: parses the input into phrases not seen before, stores them in an explicit dictionary, and encodes phrases as dictionary indices - the founding explicit-dictionary method from which LZW descends.

card.name: Lempel-Ziv-Welch compression (Welch, 1984)
card.definition: Welch's 1984 refinement of LZ78 (IEEE Computer): an adaptive dictionary compressor that needs no separate dictionary transmission because encoder and decoder build the same phrase dictionary in lockstep; the dominant dictionary compressor of the early 1990s (Unix compress, GIF).

raw_candidates.definition: Rao's 1945 Fisher-information Riemannian metric on a parametric family: the metric with respect to which the report's two connections are defined as a dual pair.
raw_candidates.justification: Duality of connections is duality WITH RESPECT TO the Fisher metric g; METR 82-7's structure is (g, nabla, nabla*) - the metric is a constitutive component named in the construction itself.
raw_candidates.name: Fisher-Rao metric (Rao, 1945)

raw_candidates.definition: Chentsov's 1972 monograph: the invariance framework for statistical geometry and the one-parameter family of alpha-connections from which the report's dual pair (the +alpha and -alpha connections) is selected.
raw_candidates.justification: The report's duality theorem is a theorem ABOUT Chentsov's alpha-connections: nabla^(alpha) and nabla^(-alpha) are dual w.r.t. the Fisher metric, and flatness of one is flatness of the other - the construction presupposes and reworks his family.
raw_candidates.name: Statistical Decision Rules and Optimal Inference (Chentsov, 1972)

raw_candidates.definition: Efron's 1975 statistical curvature: the loss-of-information measure for curved exponential families - admitted at the sibling Amari 1982 journal paper and at the 1985 monograph; proposed here to test whether this report's machinery consumes it.
raw_candidates.justification: Edge-scoping test: the sibling 1982 journal paper (curved exponential families) is Efron's home ground; METR 82-7's machinery is connections and duality on smooth families generally - whether curvature enters it must be judged on this parent's record, not inherited.
raw_candidates.name: Statistical curvature (Efron, 1975)

raw_candidates.definition: Csiszar's 1967 f-divergence paper (Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 2, 299-318): the general class of convex-function divergences between distributions - the reserved hearing: mediated via this report at both the 1998 and 1985 expansions, judged here on the report's own record.
raw_candidates.justification: THE RESERVED HEARING. Sessions 21-22 recorded Csiszar 1967 as mediated via Amari & Nagaoka 1982 at two other parents; this expansion is where that mediation inverts and the candidate is judged directly.
raw_candidates.name: Information-type measures of difference of probability distributions (Csiszar, 1967)

raw_candidates.definition: Bregman's 1967 relaxation-method paper, origin of the Bregman divergence: the divergence generated by a convex function and its Legendre dual - the form the dually flat canonical divergence later proved to take.
raw_candidates.justification: The dually flat canonical divergence is of Bregman type (Legendre structure); whether the 1982 report itself consumed Bregman's 1967 construction or only the classical Legendre transform must be judged on the report's record.
raw_candidates.name: Bregman divergence (Bregman, 1967)

raw_candidates.definition: The 1951 Kullback-Leibler divergence paper: the directed information measure that the dually flat canonical divergence reduces to on exponential families.
raw_candidates.justification: At the 1985 monograph KL was mediated via Chentsov; here its channel into the 1982 report itself is tested - the report's divergence is constructed from dual potentials, and the KL identification belongs to the divergence theory developed around it.
raw_candidates.name: On Information and Sufficiency (Kullback & Leibler, 1951)

raw_candidates.definition: Barndorff-Nielsen's 1978 monograph: the algebraic theory of exponential families, the incumbent treatment the geometric re-foundation defined itself against.

raw_candidates.note: The ancestor artifact of ANOVA-in-experiments, decomposed out of the analysis-machinery line.

raw_candidates.name: Legendre, Nouvelles methodes pour la determination des orbites des cometes (1805)
raw_candidates.definition: Legendre's 1805 monograph on comet orbits, whose nine-page appendix 'Sur la methode des moindres quarres' (pp. 72-75) is the first publication of the method of least squares: an algebraic fitting procedure ('of all the principles that can be proposed... none more general, more exact, or easier to apply than... rendering the sum of the squares of the errors a minimum'), offered with no probabilistic justification.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's section 186 presents least squares - the recipe Legendre printed in 1805 - now re-founded as a corollary of the error law, under Gauss's counter-claim of use since 1795 ('principium nostrum, quo iam inde ab anno 1795 usi sumus'). The hearing at the source: does the 1809 derivation consume the 1805 publication, or does it engage it only as a rival to be answered?

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The normal curve enters mathematics through De Moivre's binomial approximation; the question at this parent is whether Gauss's 1809 derivation consumes that approximation tradition or derives the curve independently, from the arithmetic-mean postulate of section 177, with no reference to the binomial limit.

Trans. 49, 82-93; read 1755): the first mathematical treatment of observational error as a distributed quantity - discrete error distributions (uniform and triangular chances) and the derived distribution of the mean of several observations, proving the mean is more likely near the truth than a single observation.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Simpson made 'error' a random variable with a distribution - the conceptual component the parent's section 177 presupposes when it asks for the functional form of the error density phi. Whether that component reaches Gauss through a document, or only through the practice tradition, is the hearing.

raw_candidates.definition: Laplace's 1774 memoir founding inverse probability: the probability of causes given events, the principle of indifference, and his first law of error (the double-exponential density), with the median as its most probable value; his 1781 memoir on probabilities extended the treatment to the combination of observations.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Laplace's pre-1810 error memoirs are the parallel probabilistic tradition available to the parent: the question is whether Gauss's derivation consumes any of it. The 1809 text uses neither inverse probability nor a limit argument - it derives the density from a postulate about the estimator - so the channel, if any, must be documented, not presumed.

raw_candidates.name: Boscovich, fitting of meridian arcs by absolute deviations (1755)
raw_candidates.definition: Boscovich's fitting method (c. 1755-57, for the measured meridian arcs): choose the line satisfying two conditions - the signed deviations sum to zero, and the sum of their absolute values is as small as possible - solved geometrically; Laplace replaced the geometry with an algorithm in 1789.

raw_candidates.definition: Tobias Mayer's 1750 memoir on the Moon's libration: 27 equations of condition from observations, combined by sorting them into three groups and averaging within groups - the practical ancestor of systematic combination, used to extract three unknowns from redundant discordant data.

raw_candidates.name: Cotes, Aestimatio errorum in mixta mathesi (1722)
raw_candidates.definition: Roger Cotes's posthumous tract (Harmonia Mensurarum, 1722): observations of one quantity, made with different instruments, are to be combined as weights placed at their positions - the weighted mean is their centre of gravity, and that point 'is the most probable site of the object' (Dico punctum z fore locum obiecti maxime probabilem).
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cotes first stated combination as an estimation problem - observations with weights, one most probable value - the problem form the parent answers with a probability law instead of a statics analogy.

raw_candidates.name: Piazzi's Ceres observations and the orbit-recovery problem (1801)
raw_candidates.definition: Giuseppe Piazzi's January 1801 observations of the new planet Ceres from Palermo: a short observed arc before the object was lost in the Sun's glare, posing the problem of determining a full conic orbit - and its future positions - from a few discordant observations.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The posed problem of the parent: Theoria Motus is the book of the Ceres recovery - determine an orbit from few, error-bearing observations. The demand that a handful of discordant observations yield one orbit is what forced a theory of observational error into an orbit-determination treatise.

raw_candidates.name: Daniel Bernoulli, Diiudicatio maxime probabilis plurium observationum discrepantium (1778)
raw_candidates.definition: Daniel Bernoulli's 1778 memoir (Acta Helvetica / Novi Commentarii Petropolitanae): 'of all the innumerable ways of dealing with errors of observations one should choose the one that has the highest degree of probability for the complex of observations as a whole' - the first statement of the maximum-likelihood principle, executed under an assumed semicircular error law, against the unexamined use of the arithmetic mean.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Bernoulli posed the parent's exact question - which single value is most probable, given an assumed law of error - thirty years before section 177 answered it by deriving the law from the mean postulate instead of assuming one. The argumentative form is the candidate's claim; the junction into Gauss's text is the hearing.

candidate.name: RenderMan Shading Language (Hanrahan & Lawson, 1990)
candidate.definition: The shading language of Pixar's RenderMan, published as Hanrahan & Lawson, 'A Language for Shading and Lighting Calculations' (SIGGRAPH 1990): a C-like procedural language in which surface, light, displacement and volume shaders are written once and executed by the renderer, with a standard library of graphics primitives (noise, transforms, illuminance loops). The parent paper: 'The most common shading language in use today is the RenderMan Shading Language, which provides for movie production-quality procedural shading effects for software batch-rendering systems.'
candidate.causal_claim: THE DEFERRED HEARING (carried since the early sessions). The parent takes over the candidate's design: its language is modelled on RenderMan SL's shader kinds and procedural model - the parent's own paper frames shading languages as descending from Cook through this language, and its surface and light shaders are the candidate's, re-founded on computation frequencies for hardware. The channel is personal as well as textual: Pat Hanrahan co-authored both the 1990 language paper and the parent.
candidate.source_title: Hanrahan & Lawson, SIGGRAPH 1990; Proudfoot, Mark, Tzvetkov & Hanrahan, A Real-Time Procedural Shading System for Programmable Graphics Hardware, Proc. SIGGRAPH 2001 (introduction and related work); Mark, Stanford RTSL SIGGRAPH 2001 course notes (April 18, 2001), graphics.stanford.edu/courses and the RTSL project page (graphics.stanford.edu/papers/rtsl/)

candidate.name: Cook, Shade Trees (1984)
candidate.definition: Robert L. Cook's 'Shade Trees' (SIGGRAPH 1984): shading described as a tree of procedural nodes evaluated per visible point - the founding formulation of programmable procedural shading, from which, in the parent paper's own words, 'shading languages developed'.
candidate.causal_claim: The parent's introduction names Cook's shade trees as the origin of shading languages. The hearing: whether that descent reaches the parent directly, or arrives embodied in RenderMan SL - the language that implemented the shade-tree idea as a textual language and the one the parent actually models itself on.
candidate.source_title: Proudfoot, Mark, Tzvetkov & Hanrahan, A Real-Time Procedural Shading System for Programmable Graphics Hardware, Proc. SIGGRAPH 2001 (introduction: 'Shading languages developed from the work of Cook...')

candidate.name: PixelFlow and pfman, a RenderMan-like language on custom hardware (Olano & Lastra, 1998)

The parent paper cites it directly: 'Olano and Lastra describe pfman, a RenderMan-like language for the PixelFlow system that is compiled to PixelFlow's SIMD processing arrays.'
candidate.causal_claim: The parent's own verification record concedes the Q1 pressure: PixelFlow had a RenderMan-like language on hardware first. The hearing at this parent: is pfman a consumed predecessor or a parallel system the parent compares itself against - the parent's leap being retargetability across commodity machines, pfman's being bound to one custom machine?

raw_candidates.definition: Robert L. Cook's 'Shade Trees' (SIGGRAPH 1984): shading described as a tree of procedural nodes evaluated per visible point, with the conceptually independent tasks of light source specification, surface reflectance and atmospheric effects separated - the founding formulation of programmable procedural shading, and the origin of the surface/light/atmosphere shader types RenderMan retains.

The parent paper's introduction: 'Cook developed a model which separated the conceptually independent tasks of light source specification, surface reflectance, and atmospheric effects' - and the abstract states the new language is 'based on previous work of Cook and Perlin' and 'incorporates features of both'. The hearing: whether the shade-tree formulation is consumed and reworked by the parent (as a textual language with shader kinds), or whether an intermediate carries it.

raw_candidates.name: Perlin, An Image Synthesizer (1985)
raw_candidates.definition: Ken Perlin's 'An Image Synthesizer' (SIGGRAPH 1985): a pixel-stream shading language with conditional and looping constructs, function and procedure definitions, and a full set of arithmetic and logical operators, together with the procedural noise and turbulence functions that became the standard library vocabulary of procedural shading.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: THE DIRECT HEARING (mediated via SL's library at RTSL, session 41). The parent paper's introduction: 'Perlin's image synthesizer carried this idea further by providing a full language including conditional and looping constructs, function and procedure definitions' - and the abstract: the new language 'incorporates features of both Cook's and Perlin's systems'. The hearing: whether Perlin's full-language form is the ancestor the parent modified (Cook supplied the shader-type separation; Perlin supplied the language), judged on the paper's own text.

raw_candidates.name: REYES rendering architecture (Cook, Carpenter & Catmull, 1987)
raw_candidates.definition: The REYES image rendering architecture (Cook, Carpenter & Catmull, SIGGRAPH 1987), built at Lucasfilm's Computer Division and carried to Pixar: primitives are diced into micropolygon grids, shaded as whole grids, then sampled - the architecture Pixar's renderer implemented and the one the RenderMan Interface was designed around.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: THE DIRECT HEARING (defined-against at RTSL, session 41 - a different relation there). At the parent the relation is design-target: the language was built at Pixar as the shading component of the REYES renderer; the interface it lives in 'was designed around' REYES, whose semantics (shading whole micropolygon grids before visibility, ShadingRate) the language's execution model presupposes - shaders run per grid point, with derivatives and texture filtering cheap because grids are shaded at once. The hearing: consumed target architecture, judged on the 1990 paper's design and implementation record.
raw_candidates.source_title: ACM Turing Award profile of Pat Hanrahan: 'Hanrahan's team built RenderMan on top of a system previously developed by Catmull along with Loren Carpenter and Rob Cook called REYES'; RenderMan Interface Specification schematic: 'REYES is where RenderMan started... the architecture the RenderMan Interface Specification was designed around... it shaped the spec's semantics, including ShadingRate, the shading-before-visibility order'

raw_candidates.name: RenderMan Interface Specification (Pixar, 1988)
raw_candidates.definition: Pixar's RenderMan Interface Specification, first published 1988 (v3.0; 3.1 in 1989): the standard interface between modelers and photorealistic renderers - the Ri procedural API, the RIB bytestream format, and the first specification of the shading language itself. Pat Hanrahan was its main architect.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: THE SESSION'S ASSIGNED DISCRIMINATION TEST (mediation by containment at RTSL, session 41). The spec's v3.0 'set out the core API, RIB and the Shading Language' - so the candidate CONTAINS the parent's design in its first specified form, two years before the parent paper. The hearing: does the 1990 language consume the spec's framework (the interface discipline, the global-state interface the paper says it 'clearly specified'), or is the spec the language's container and first publication form - the same design act by the same architect (Hanrahan led both), in which case containment is not ancestry?

Version 3.0 (1988) set out the core API, RIB and the Shading Language'; ACM Hanrahan profile: 'Hanrahan's principal contributions were the RenderMan Interface Specification (RISpec) and its Shading Language'

This was published in The RenderMan Companion by Steve Upstill in 1989, with more technical detail in Hanrahan and Lawson's 1990 SIGGRAPH paper.' raw_candidates.name: Whitted, An improved illumination model for shaded display (1980)
raw_candidates.definition: Turner Whitted's 1980 recursive ray-tracing illumination model, in which - as the parent paper's introduction records - Whitted proposed that the rendering system have a collection of built-in shaders accessible via a shader dispatch table: the earliest posed form of extensible shading inside a renderer.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent paper's introduction names Whitted's dispatch-table proposal in its ancestry survey. The hearing: a posed possibility (extensibility via a table of BUILT-IN shaders) is not the parent's mechanism (a user-writable LANGUAGE); anticipation of the problem's shape, judged against the paper's own framing, which passes from Whitted to Cook's model as the operative step.

raw_candidates.definition: Cook & Torrance's physically-based specular reflectance model (SIGGRAPH 1981 / TOG 1982): the microfacet BRDF that became standard content for shading systems' libraries and example surface shaders.

raw_candidates.name: Blinn, Models of light reflection for computer synthesized pictures (1977)
raw_candidates.definition: James Blinn's 1977 half-vector specular model and associated reflection models: with Phong's 1975 model, the default local illumination content that renderers hard-coded before shading languages, and that shading libraries thereafter supplied as built-in surface shaders.

raw_candidates.definition: Darwyn Peachey's 'Solid texturing of complex surfaces' (SIGGRAPH 1985): procedural three-dimensional texture functions evaluated in object space - with Perlin's synthesizer, the founding statement of procedural solid texturing as a practice.

raw_candidates.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
raw_candidates.definition: Brown et al. (2020): a 175B autoregressive language model whose few-shot prompting made zero-shot and few-shot task performance a public, measurable property of a pretrained model.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: THE BASE-MODEL HEARING, CORRECTED. The session brief framed this on the Codex pattern ('the base model FLAN fine-tunes'), but the parent paper's own text names a different base: 'We take a pretrained language model of 137B parameters' - LaMDA-PT, a Google-internal decoder-only model. GPT-3's documented channels into the parent are (a) the comparison incumbent the headline result is scored against (FLAN surpasses zero-shot GPT-3 on 20 of 25 datasets), (b) the origin of the few-shot prompting practice the parent positions instruction tuning against, and (c) the public existence proof of the 100B+ decoder-LM class. Whether any of these is consumption of the artifact - or whether the artifact channel is mediated via LaMDA-PT - is the hearing.
raw_candidates.source_title: Brown et al., 'Language Models Are Few-Shot Learners', NeurIPS 2020; Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

raw_candidates.name: T5 (text-to-text transfer transformer)
raw_candidates.definition: Raffel et al. (2019): a single encoder-decoder transformer trained with a unified text-to-text format on C4 plus a supervised multi-task mixture, every task rendered as text in and text out.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The unified text-to-text format and the at-scale supervised multi-task mixture are inside the parent's design: FLAN renders every task as natural-language text in and text out, and its training object is a multi-task mixture in exactly T5's sense, re-aimed from seen tasks to held-out task clusters. The hearing: format-and-recipe presupposition (the Cook-at-REYES shape) versus a component the leap merely contains.
raw_candidates.source_title: Raffel et al., 'Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer', arXiv:1910.10683 (2019); Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

raw_candidates.name: Transformer architecture
raw_candidates.definition: Vaswani et al. (2017): the self-attention sequence architecture underlying the parent's base model.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The architecture of LaMDA-PT, the parent's base. Expected mediation via the base model: the parent adds no architecture, so the channel runs through whatever artifact carries the architecture into the parent.
raw_candidates.source_title: Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

raw_candidates.name: LaMDA-PT pretrained language model (137B)
raw_candidates.definition: Google's 137B decoder-only transformer language model, pretrained on web documents, dialog data and Wikipedia; the actual base model the FLAN paper instruction-tunes. Its standalone describing publication is the LaMDA paper (Thoppilan et al., arXiv:2201.08239, Jan 2022).
raw_candidates.causal_claim: THE ACTUAL BASE - FILED FOR THE RECORD, EXPECTED DATE-DROPPED. Consumption by construction: the parent's weights are this model's weights after instruction tuning (the Codex/GPT-3 shape). But the artifact is an unpublished internal model: dated by its describing publication (Jan 2022) it postdates the parent; dated by the parent paper's own description of it (Sep 2021) it is the parent's own year. Under the run's dating discipline (unpublished artifacts are dated by the paper that describes them - the Codex corpus precedent) both datings are inexpressible at year granularity. Filed so the drop is on the record, never re-dated.
raw_candidates.source_title: Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

raw_candidates.name: UnifiedQA
raw_candidates.definition: Khashabi et al. (2020): a single T5/BART-based model unified across QA datasets and formats, demonstrating cross-format generalization from multi-dataset QA training.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The unified-format component: one model, many datasets, format as the only task signal. The hearing: whether FLAN's instruction format consumes UnifiedQA's demonstrated unification, or whether UnifiedQA is a format-bound relative (QA only) whose channel runs through the multi-task lineage.
raw_candidates.source_title: Khashabi et al., 'UnifiedQA: Crossing Format Boundaries With a Single QA System', EMNLP Findings 2020

raw_candidates.name: BERT
raw_candidates.definition: Devlin et al. (2018): bidirectional transformer pretraining whose per-task fine-tuning became the default transfer paradigm of 2019-2021.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The pretrain-then-finetune paradigm the parent inherits in form (finetune a pretrained model) and defines itself against in aim (one model per task versus one model for unseen tasks). FLAN's introduction positions instruction tuning between per-task finetuning 'as with BERT and T5' and GPT-3-style prompting. The hearing: paradigm ancestor, defined-against incumbent, or neither - its bidirectional mechanism is not in the parent's decoder-only base.
raw_candidates.source_title: Devlin et al., 'BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding', arXiv:1810.04805 (2018); Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

raw_candidates.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
raw_candidates.definition: Brown et al. (2020), as above.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cross-filing, ancestor-modified side: the parent's method is a modification of the GPT-3 usage pattern - where GPT-3 elicits task behaviour by prompting a frozen model, FLAN bakes task specification into finetuning. The paper's ablations run this comparison directly (zero-shot and few-shot GPT-3 as the baselines instruction tuning must beat).
raw_candidates.source_title: Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

raw_candidates.name: T5 (text-to-text transfer transformer)
raw_candidates.definition: Raffel et al. (2019), as above.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cross-filing, the ancestor-modified claim in its strongest form: FLAN is T5's multi-task finetuning with three modifications - task prefixes replaced by natural-language instructions, evaluation re-aimed at held-out task clusters, and the base scaled from an 11B encoder-decoder to a 137B decoder-only model. T0 (2021, date-dropped) is the same modification performed on T5 itself, which is evidence the modification was in the air - and that its carrier into this parent is the T5 formulation, not T0.
raw_candidates.source_title: Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

raw_candidates.name: The Natural Language Decathlon (decaNLP)
raw_candidates.definition: McCann et al. (2018): ten NLP tasks cast uniformly as question answering over a context, trained jointly in one multitask question answering network (MQAN) with no task-specific modules.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The earliest at-scale ancestor of the parent's form: one model, many tasks, the task specified in natural language (a question) rather than by architecture. FLAN's modifications: instructions instead of questions, a pretrained 137B LM instead of a bespoke BiLSTM network, and held-out-task generalization as the explicit objective (decaNLP's zero-shot transfer to unseen tasks was weak). The hearing: direct ancestor, or mediated via T5, whose text-to-text format generalizes decaNLP's QA format?
raw_candidates.source_title: McCann et al., 'The Natural Language Decathlon: Multitask Learning as Question Answering', arXiv:1806.08730 (2018)

candidate.definition: McCann et al. (2018): ten NLP tasks cast uniformly as question answering over a context, trained jointly in one multitask question answering network (MQAN) with no task-specific modules.
candidate.causal_claim: The earliest at-scale ancestor of the parent's form: one model, many tasks, the task specified in natural language (a question) rather than by architecture. FLAN's modifications: instructions instead of questions, a pretrained 137B LM instead of a bespoke BiLSTM network, and held-out-task generalization as the explicit objective (decaNLP's zero-shot transfer to unseen tasks was weak). The hearing: direct ancestor, or mediated via T5, whose text-to-text format generalizes decaNLP's QA format?
candidate.source_title: McCann et al., 'The Natural Language Decathlon: Multitask Learning as Question Answering', arXiv:1806.08730 (2018)

candidate.name: MT-DNN
candidate.definition: Liu et al. (2019): multi-task deep neural networks for natural language understanding - a shared BERT encoder finetuned jointly on the GLUE task mixture with task-specific heads.
candidate.causal_claim: The multi-task finetuning ancestor in its encoder-era form: joint finetuning on a task mixture as the route to generalization. The hearing: whether its channel into the parent runs through T5 (which generalized the shared-mixture idea to text-to-text generative form) - mediation expected.
candidate.source_title: Liu et al., 'Multi-Task Deep Neural Networks for Natural Language Understanding', ACL 2019

candidate.name: GPT-2
candidate.definition: Radford et al. (2019): 'Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners' - the paper that first claimed a pretrained LM performs tasks zero-shot (reading comprehension, translation, summarization) without task supervision.
candidate.causal_claim: The zero-shot ambition's origin document in the LM line: FLAN's objective (zero-shot performance on unseen tasks) is the claim GPT-2's paper staked and GPT-3's paper operationalized. Expected mediation via GPT-3, the operative carrier of the claim at the parent's scale.
candidate.source_title: Wei et al., 'Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners', arXiv:2109.01652 (Sep 2021)

candidate.name: The Turking Test (Efrat & Levy, 2020)
candidate.definition: Efrat & Levy (2020): a benchmark testing whether language models understand natural-language instructions, finding that contemporary LMs largely fail to follow the instructions they are given.
candidate.causal_claim: The diagnosis in named form: models do not understand instructions. The hearing under the Hochreiter condition: a diagnosis answered is not consumed unless the parent's documents derive from it - FLAN's remedy (train on instructions) answers the diagnosis, but whether the channel is this document or the general 2020-21 recognition is the question.
candidate.source_title: Efrat & Levy, 'The Turking Test: Can Language Models Understand Instructions?', arXiv:2010.11982 (2020)

candidate.name: Prompt engineering practice
candidate.definition: The 2020-21 practitioner practice of eliciting task behaviour from frozen large LMs by hand-crafted prompts and few-shot exemplars, centred on the GPT-3 API.
candidate.causal_claim: The incumbent practice the parent displaces for task specification: hand-crafted prompts, brittle to wording (the parent's ablations show instruction tuning's gains are largest exactly where prompting is most fragile). candidate.name: LaMDA-PT pretrained language model (137B)
candidate.definition: Google's 137B decoder-only transformer language model, pretrained on web documents, dialog data and Wikipedia; the actual base model the FLAN paper instruction-tunes. Its standalone describing publication is the LaMDA paper (Thoppilan et al., arXiv:2201.08239, Jan 2022).
candidate.causal_claim: THE ACTUAL BASE - FILED FOR THE RECORD, EXPECTED DATE-DROPPED. Consumption by construction: the parent's weights are this model's weights after instruction tuning (the Codex/GPT-3 shape). But the artifact is an unpublished internal model: dated by its describing publication (Jan 2022) it postdates the parent; dated by the parent paper's own description of it (Sep 2021) it is the parent's own year. Under the run's dating discipline (unpublished artifacts are dated by the paper that describes them - the Codex corpus precedent) both datings are inexpressible at year granularity. Filed so the drop is on the record, never re-dated.

candidate.name: Natural Instructions (Mishra et al., 2021)

candidate.causal_claim: FILED FOR THE RECORD, EXPECTED DATE-DROPPED (same year as the parent; April precedes September at month granularity, inexpressible). The problem-posed document in its purest form: 'a long-standing challenge in AI is to build a model that learns a new task by understanding the human-readable instructions that define it' - and its models (BART-based) gained 19% on unseen tasks from instructions while remaining far behind task-specific models. The hearing the bound prevents: whether the parent consumes this formulation or independently instantiates it (FLAN's templates are author-written, not crowdsourced; the formulations are parallel). At ChatGPT (session 44) this artifact was recorded as an academic formulation never consumed; that record is edge-scoped to ChatGPT and does not decide this hearing.

raw_candidates.name: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR)
raw_candidates.relation: the parent's retriever, initialized from DPR and its index
raw_candidates.why: The parent paper: 'The retriever (Dense Passage Retriever [26], henceforth DPR) provides latent documents conditioned on the input'. Same year as the parent - expected date-drop; the components hearing is recorded in drop form.

raw_candidates.name: ORQA: Latent Retrieval for Weakly Supervised Open Domain Question Answering
raw_candidates.relation: the latent-retrieval formulation ancestor; the parent follows Lee et al. for the corpus convention
raw_candidates.why: The parent: 'Following Lee et al. [31] and Karpukhin et al. [26], we use the December 2018 dump'; the introduction names ORQA as one of the two recently introduced retrieval-augmented models it generalizes (extractive reader -> generative generator).

raw_candidates.name: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
raw_candidates.relation: the coeval retrieval-augmented pretraining line named in the parent's introduction
raw_candidates.why: Named in the parent's introduction alongside ORQA. Same year (Feb 2020) - expected date-drop; multiples evidence for the formulation's ripeness.

raw_candidates.name: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training
raw_candidates.relation: the parent's generator, used in every headline result
raw_candidates.why: The parent: 'the seq2seq model (BART [32]) then conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output'. The generator-component hearing.

raw_candidates.name: DrQA: Reading Wikipedia to Answer Open-Domain Questions

raw_candidates.name: ASDiv (Miao et al., 2020)
raw_candidates.definition: ASDiv (Miao, Liang & Su, ACL 2020): a 2,305-problem English math word problem corpus built for diversity - wide lexicon usage and problem-type coverage, annotated with problem type and grade level, with a lexicon-usage-diversity metric for corpora.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's Sec.2 design principles incorporate ASDiv's corpus criteria as components: high diversity and high quality are stated as GSM8K's own first two principles, and Sec.3.1 says of ASDiv 'We share those design principles in the creation of GSM8K.' The hearing: incorporated criteria (this filing) versus the ancestor-modified relation (filed at L2).
raw_candidates.source_title: Miao, Liang & Su, 'A Diverse Corpus for Evaluating and Developing English Math Word Problem Solvers', ACL 2020; Cobbe et al., 'Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems', arXiv:2110.14168 (Oct 2021)

raw_candidates.name: AQuA-RAT (Ling et al., 2017)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: The natural-language-solution component: AQuA-RAT is the lineage's first at-scale carrier of the format the parent adopts as a design principle ('Natural Language Solutions', Sec.2). The parent's text simultaneously defines itself against AQuA-RAT's execution ('a high degree of problem templatization and poor quality control of the natural language solutions') - the hearing is whether the format component is consumed-and-redone or merely defined-against.

raw_candidates.name: In-context learning

raw_candidates.causal_claim: A production component named in Appendix A: the seed questions given to GSM8K's problem writers were 'automatically generated from a few-shot prompted 175B GPT-3 model' - few-shot prompting is the mechanism by which the seed stream was produced. Expected mediation via the GPT-3 artifact that was prompted; filed so the mediation is on the record rather than buried in GPT-3's evaluation.
raw_candidates.source_title: Cobbe et al., 'Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems', arXiv:2110.14168 (Oct 2021)

The parent's 16GB at 720 GB/s is HBM2's first GPU implementation.

The incorporated component par excellence: the parent's leap IS substantially this component productized - its stored leap names '16GB of HBM2 at 720 GB/s through a silicon-interposer package' first. The month order is documented (JEDEC Jan 2016 -> Samsung production Jan 2016 -> P100 Apr 2016) and is inexpressible at year granularity; the drop, when it comes, is the calendar's, not the gate's, and this filing puts the component's claim and the month order in the scout record. Its predecessor HBM (2013) is filed at L2 with the mediation this drop will force.
