raw_candidates.name: CoWoS silicon-interposer packaging (TSMC)
raw_candidates.definition: CoWoS (Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate), TSMC's 2.5D packaging platform: logic and memory dies mounted side by side on a silicon interposer whose dense wiring carries the wide memory interface. First commercial use 2011 in the Xilinx Virtex-7 2000T FPGA (first shipments 25 Oct 2011); TSMC's retrospective dates the platform's introduction to 2012 - the ambiguity is recorded, the earlier documented product date is used.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The packaging component the parent's memory system is physically built with: GP100's HBM2 stacks reach the die only through the interposer CoWoS provides - a 4096-bit interface cannot be routed through a conventional package substrate. The parent's press release lists 'CoWoS with HBM2' as one of its five breakthroughs. The CUDA-pattern hearing applies: a SPECIFIC enabling step (this packaging platform productized since 2011) versus generic infrastructure.
raw_candidates.source_title: TSMC CoWoS records; Xilinx Virtex-7 2000T shipment record (2011); NVIDIA press release, 'NVIDIA Launches Tesla P100' (GTC, 5 Apr 2016)

raw_candidates.name: HBM2 high-bandwidth memory
raw_candidates.definition: HBM2 (JEDEC JESD235A, adopted Jan 2016; Samsung mass production announced 19 Jan 2016): the second-generation stacked DRAM standard - four stacks on the GPU package, 4096-bit interface, the memory technology the parent implements at 16 GB and 900 GB/s.

The whitepaper's HBM2 section: 'Tesla P100 was the world's first GPU architecture to support HBM2. Tesla V100 uses a faster and more efficient HBM2 implementation ... a new generation HBM2 memory from Samsung, and a new generation memory controller in Volta, provides 1.5x delivered memory bandwidth versus Pascal GP100.' The mediation attack to run in verification: the same section defers details to the Pascal whitepaper - does the channel run through P100's prior integration? The discrimination to argue: the artifact consumed is the standard + Samsung's stacks, which P100 also consumed; a fellow consumer is not a carrier (the components discriminations), and GV100's controller is new. The counterfactual: without the 2016 standard and production stacks, the parent's 900 GB/s memory design does not exist; GDDR5X was the defined-against alternative actually shipping.

raw_candidates.definition: NVLink (announced GTC 25 Mar 2014, NVIDIA with IBM): a point-to-point GPU interconnect protocol and link, designed for 5-12x PCIe bandwidth, cache-coherent connection to IBM POWER CPUs, first integrated into Pascal-generation GPUs. (Existing node - canonical name used.)

The hearing: the 2014 artifact retained and extended (ancestor-modified at one remove - the parent implements generation 2 of THIS artifact), versus the objection that what the parent consumes is NVLink 2.0, its own component. The own-version discipline governs versions of the PARENT; NVLink is a separable artifact with its own node, date and co-developer, and generation-2 is its continuation, not the parent's earlier version of itself. Counterfactual: without the 2014 NVLink programme there is no NVLink 2.0 in Volta - the DGX-1 hybrid cube mesh and the Power9 coherence story both presuppose the link's existence as a technology line.

candidate.causal_claim: The own-formation filing (the proto-Reyes shape): a roadmap announcement is the parent's programme describing its future self; it contains no mechanism the parent consumes, and the run's own-version discipline refuses a parent's earlier self-descriptions as predecessors. Filed so the refusal is on the record - and because the 2013 date matters to the CORAL hearing (the programme predates the procurement that later named it).
candidate.source_title: NVIDIA GTC 2013 keynote roadmap (Mar 2013)

candidate.name: CORAL Summit and Sierra procurement
candidate.definition: The DOE CORAL procurement (awards announced 14 Nov 2014): $325M to IBM with NVIDIA and Mellanox for the Summit (ORNL) and Sierra (LLNL) supercomputers, plus ~$100M FastForward 2 R&D - the awards explicitly naming 'the IBM Power Architecture, NVIDIA's Volta GPU and Mellanox's interconnect technologies' as the systems' basis.
candidate.causal_claim: THE POSED-PROBLEM / INSTITUTIONAL HEARING. A specific, dated, funded document names the parent - 'NVIDIA's Volta GPU' - two and a half years before it shipped, as the accelerator of two leadership systems whose requirements (node performance, POWER9 coherence, memory bandwidth) the parent was then designed against; the whitepaper's IBM passages document the resulting system line ('working with IBM to build even higher performance servers using Tesla V100 accelerators and Power 9 CPUs connected with NVLink'). Against admission: the Volta programme predates CORAL (roadmap, Mar 2013), so CORAL did not originate the parent; and no V100 design document cites CORAL requirements as derivations (the Hochreiter condition in institutional form). The hearing: posed-and-paid problem as ancestry (the OpenPOWER shape - a vehicle without which the leap does not happen in that form), or the demand context that shaped the parent's system targets while its chip-level leap (Tensor Cores) answers a different problem (deep learning scale). Argued in full in evaluation.
candidate.source_title: DOE CORAL award announcement (14 Nov 2014); NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture' whitepaper WP-08608-001_v1.1 (Aug 2017)

candidate.name: Deep Speech 2 large-scale speech recognition
candidate.definition: Baidu's Deep Speech 2 (Amodei et al., Dec 2015): end-to-end deep learning speech recognition for English and Mandarin, trained at scale on multi-GPU systems - the era's demonstration that frontier model quality had become a function of training scale.
candidate.causal_claim: The workload-side posing: DS2 is the document class that made 'train bigger networks, faster' the field's operative demand in the parent's design window - the Tensor Core section's own framing ('the complexity and size of neural networks have continued to grow ... demand even higher performance and faster training times') is this demand in the vendor's words, without citation. The hearing: demand document as posed problem (Lashley shape requires adoption in the child's documents - the framing echo is thematic, not a derivation), or era demand, the AlexNet-at-P100 shape one level closer. Filed with its L22 cross-filing; argued fresh.
candidate.source_title: Amodei et al., 'Deep Speech 2', arXiv:1512.02595 (Dec 2015)

candidate.name: Deep learning with limited numerical precision (Gupta et al.)
candidate.definition: Gupta, Agrawal, Gopalakrishnan & Narayanan, 'Deep Learning with Limited Numerical Precision' (ICML 2015): the demonstration that 16-bit fixed-point arithmetic with stochastic rounding can train deep networks without accuracy loss - the paper that dissolved the assumed FP32-precision requirement.
candidate.causal_claim: THE MIXED-PRECISION HEARING the brief assigns. The Tensor Core's arithmetic contract (FP16 inputs, FP32 accumulation) presupposes a fact the field did not have before 2015: reduced-precision training works. Gupta et al. is the canonical document that established it (with stochastic rounding as the mechanism that made the lowest precisions viable). Against consumption: the whitepaper cites no external literature at all; the tensor core's mechanism (a 4x4 MMA unit) is not Gupta's mechanism (stochastic rounding in software arithmetic); and NVIDIA's own FP16 datapath (GP100, 2016) is the proximate in-house carrier - which would mediate this channel via the P100 node if the P100 link is admitted. The hearing: problem-formulation ancestry (the precision obstruction diagnosed and removed, Lashley/Hochreiter tests), versus an era result whose channel into the silicon runs through the vendor's own prior product. Fail-closed partial is the expected honest grade; anything stronger must be earned on documents that do not exist in the whitepaper.
candidate.source_title: Gupta et al., ICML 2015

member_names: Deep learning with limited numerical precision (Gupta et al.)
Deep learning with limited numerical precision (Gupta et al.)

candidate.name: Training deep neural networks with low precision multiplications (Courbariaux et al.)
candidate.definition: Courbariaux, Bengio & David, 'Training Deep Neural Networks with Low Precision Multiplications' (ICLR 2015 workshop): multiply-accumulate in reduced precision during training, with full-precision accumulation - the arithmetic shape the Tensor Core later hardens.
candidate.causal_claim: The second document of the 2015 precision stratum, filed so the stratum is heard whole: its formulation (low-precision multiplies, high-precision accumulate) is verbally the Tensor Core's contract. Against: it is a multiple of Gupta et al. within the same season (the two papers are the stratum's parallel carriers), no channel into NVIDIA's design documents exists for either, and a verbal match between a software formulation and a hardware contract is shape, not consumption (the Jenkin-at-Typical-laws discrimination). Expected: refused as the stratum's second carrier, with Gupta's record carrying the hearing.
candidate.source_title: Courbariaux, Bengio & David, ICLR 2015 workshop

member_names: Training deep neural networks with low precision multiplications (Courbariaux et al.)

candidate.name: Baidu DeepBench
candidate.definition: Baidu's DeepBench (released Sep 2016): the first vendor-neutral benchmark of the low-level operations deep learning training spends its time on - GEMM, convolutions, recurrent ops, communication - across hardware.
candidate.causal_claim: Cross-filed from L17 as the diagnosis filing: DeepBench made the operations mix of training a measured public quantity in the parent's design window - the measurement stratum that says training time is GEMM-and-bandwidth time, which is the parent's design centre. Against: no NVIDIA design document derives from it (it is Baidu's artifact, and NVIDIA's own measurements needed no permission), and at P100 it was date-dropped as coeval; here it predates the parent and gets its hearing: measurement/diagnosis answered, not consumed (the Hochreiter condition), expected fail-closed partial.
candidate.source_title: Baidu DeepBench release (Sep 2016)

candidate.name: Google TPU v1
candidate.definition: Google's Tensor Processing Unit v1 (in production from 2015; publicly disclosed May 2016; ISCA paper Apr 2017): a datacenter inference ASIC built around a 256x256 systolic matrix multiply unit - the first shipped proof that dedicated matrix-multiply silicon beats general processors at neural network arithmetic.
candidate.causal_claim: The rival-silicon hearing, in two directions. As multiples evidence: the dedicated matrix unit was ripe - Google shipped one before the parent was announced, which caps the Tensor Core's necessity (the parent's own stored verification already records the TPU family as its Q3 multiple). As ancestor: NO channel is documented - Volta was in design from ~2014, TPU v1's details were public only from May 2016 (and its ISCA paper weeks before the parent's announcement), it is an INFERENCE part (INT8, no training), and the tensor core's form (a warp-level 4x4 MMA inside a programmable SM) is not the systolic form. Defined-against / multiple, not consumed. Filed also at L19 as the import-stratum carrier.
candidate.source_title: Jouppi et al., 'In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit', ISCA 2017; Google TPU disclosure (May 2016)

candidate.name: GDDR5X memory
candidate.definition: Micron's GDDR5X (2016): the fastest GDDR generation - the memory NVIDIA's own consumer flagship (GTX 1080) shipped with, and the incumbent alternative the parent's HBM2 choice defines itself against.
candidate.causal_claim: The defined-against memory incumbent: the parent's HBM2 section opens by contrasting its subsystem with 'traditional GDDR5 memory designs', and GDDR5X was the live, shipping, cheaper alternative in the parent's own product house. A choice's rejected branch is not its ancestor (the GDDR5-at-P100 shape, consistent). Filed so the memory stratum's negative space is complete beside the admitted HBM2.
candidate.source_title: Micron GDDR5X announcements (2016); NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture' whitepaper WP-08608-001_v1.1 (Aug 2017)

candidate.name: Intel Xeon Phi Knights Landing
candidate.definition: Intel's Xeon Phi 'Knights Landing' (shipped 2016): a 72-core many-core HPC processor with on-package MCDRAM high-bandwidth memory - the CPU camp's competing answer to accelerator-class bandwidth.
candidate.causal_claim: The rival HPC incumbent: KNL is the alternative 2016 answer to the same problem (feed many arithmetic units with stacked/on-package bandwidth), from the camp that had refused NVIDIA its fabric licence a few years earlier. No channel into the parent's design exists or is claimed; its role is the defined-against stratum and multiples context (the bandwidth-first accelerator was a contested, multi-vendor move in 2016). Expected refusal.
candidate.source_title: Intel Knights Landing launch materials (2016)

candidate.name: TSMC 16nm FinFET Plus process (16FF+)
candidate.definition: TSMC's 16nm FinFET Plus process (16FF+) (2015): the foundry process generation GP100 was manufactured on - the platform of which the parent's 12FFN is a customised refinement. (Existing node - canonical name used.)
candidate.causal_claim: The mediation filing: the parent's whitepaper names its process as 12FFN, and launch coverage describes 12FFN as 'a refinement of TSMC's 16nm FinFET technology customized for NVIDIA' - so the 2015 platform reaches the parent only through its 2017 derivative, which the year bound drops. The cited-final-link rule assigns ancestry to the artifact the parent's documents name; that artifact is inexpressible, so the honest record is MEDIATED VIA TSMC 12nm FFN (2017, date-dropped) - the HBM-at-P100-via-HBM2 shape, one generation on. 16FF+'s own admission (at P100, where it was consumed directly and named in the documents) is untouched.
candidate.source_title: NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture' whitepaper WP-08608-001_v1.1 (Aug 2017); HPCWire, Volta launch coverage (10 May 2017)

candidate.name: CUDA GPU computing
candidate.definition: NVIDIA's CUDA platform (2007): the programming model and toolchain that made NVIDIA GPUs programmable for general computation. (Existing node - canonical name used.)
candidate.causal_claim: The presupposition hearing, argued fresh at this parent as the rules require: at P100 and at NVLink CUDA was refused edge-scoped (it ran identically on the products the parents replaced; the product LINE's presupposition). At V100 the same shape holds - CUDA 9's warp-level matrix operations EXPOSE the Tensor Cores, but an exposure layer written for the hardware attends the leap rather than enabling it, and the platform's decade-old base cannot discriminate a 2017 leap from the 2016 product it also served unchanged in kind. Expected refusal, edge-scoped, with the WMMA point recorded.
candidate.source_title: NVIDIA CUDA launch materials (2007); NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture' whitepaper WP-08608-001_v1.1 (Aug 2017)

candidate.name: cuDNN deep neural network library
candidate.definition: NVIDIA's cuDNN (2014): the GPU-accelerated primitives library for deep neural networks - the library through which frameworks call the parent's Tensor Cores (the whitepaper: 'cuBLAS and cuDNN libraries have been updated to provide new library interfaces to make use of Tensor Cores').
candidate.causal_claim: The direction hearing (the cuDNN-at-P100 shape, argued fresh): cuDNN's Volta support was written FOR the parent - the whitepaper's own sentence has the libraries 'updated' to use the new hardware, which is the descendant direction (the HF-Transformers-at-RAG shape). The counter-consideration: a tensor-core GPU whose libraries could not call the cores would be a diminished leap, so the library stratum is a genuine enabling condition of the leap's USE - but enabling conditions supplied by the parent's own launch train are the programme's software half, not predecessors. Expected refusal on direction.
candidate.source_title: NVIDIA cuDNN launch materials (2014); NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture' whitepaper WP-08608-001_v1.1 (Aug 2017)

candidate.name: NVIDIA TensorRT inference optimizer
candidate.definition: NVIDIA's TensorRT (announced as GIE in 2015; TensorRT from 2016): the inference optimiser/runtime that compiles trained networks for deployment on NVIDIA GPUs - the software half of the parent's inference claims (6x inference TFLOPS).
candidate.causal_claim: The inference-side tooling filing: TensorRT predates the parent and its Volta version was, like cuDNN's, written for the new hardware. The parent's leap as stored is a TRAINING leap ('mixed-precision training at cluster scale'), and its inference half rides the same silicon; the tooling neither contains a parent mechanism nor predates the design decisions it serves. Expected refusal - descendant-facing tooling of the same product programme.
candidate.source_title: NVIDIA TensorRT announcements (2016)

candidate.name: PCI Express 3.0
candidate.definition: PCI Express 3.0 (PCI-SIG, Nov 2010): the third generation of the PCIe standard - the host interface the parent retains (its board 'provides NVLink and PCIe 3.0 connectivity').
candidate.causal_claim: Filed fresh at this parent as an ordinary candidate (it was refused at NVLink, a different parent - the refusal does not transfer, the hearing does): the parent RETAINS PCIe 3.0 as its host attach in most systems, so coexistence is documented in the parent's own board description. Against: a retained host interface is the substrate the product ships in, unchanged from the prior generation - it discriminates nothing about the leap (the parent's PCIe form is its baseline form). Expected refusal as coexistence substrate, argued fresh.
candidate.source_title: PCI-SIG, PCI Express Base Specification 3.0 (2010); NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture' whitepaper WP-08608-001_v1.1 (Aug 2017)

candidate.name: IEEE 754 half-precision format (FP16)
candidate.definition: The IEEE 754-2008 half-precision binary16 format: the 16-bit floating-point representation (1 sign, 5 exponent, 10 mantissa bits) that is the Tensor Core's input format and Pascal/Volta's FP16 arithmetic type.
candidate.causal_claim: Re-filed at a new parent as an ordinary candidate (fail-closed partial at P100 under the specification-as-notation discrimination). At V100 the format's role deepens - it is no longer just a rate on a spec sheet but the input type of the parent's defining unit - and the hearing should be run again on that fact: does being the defining unit's DATA TYPE make the format a mechanism of the leap, or is it still presupposed vocabulary (the hardware implements the format; the format document is never what the design consumes - the design consumes arithmetic behaviour, multiply carried by every FP16 implementation since 2008)? Expected: fail-closed partial again, with the deepening recorded - consistency argued, not assumed.

candidate.name: Systolic array architecture (Kung & Leiserson)
candidate.definition: Kung & Leiserson's systolic arrays (1978): the architecture concept of a regular grid of simple processing elements rhythmically passing data between neighbours - the classical form of the matrix-multiply machine, ancestor in concept to every matrix unit since.
candidate.causal_claim: The deep-origin filing, made because the tensor-core enablement question is incomplete without it: the matrix unit's CONCEPT is 1978 systolic. Against admission, decisively: the parent's Tensor Core is not a systolic array in form (it is a warp-synchronous 4x4 MMA unit inside a programmable SM), the gap is four decades, and whatever of the concept reached 2017 arrived through the era's matrix-unit practice - its proximate carrier at this parent is the TPU v1 record (itself refused as a multiple). Expected: refused as a mediated/distant fundamental - the scout files it so the gate, not silence, draws the line, and the mediation is recorded via TPU v1.
candidate.source_title: Kung & Leiserson, 'Systolic Arrays (for VLSI)' (1978)

candidate.name: Microsoft Catapult FPGA acceleration
candidate.definition: Microsoft's Catapult (ISCA 2014): FPGAs wired into every server of a datacenter fabric to accelerate ranking, networking and (later) neural inference - the reconfigurable-hardware camp's proof that dedicated acceleration silicon belongs in the fleet.
candidate.causal_claim: The second rival-silicon filing: Catapult (with TPU) marks the mid-2010s moment when every hyperscaler concluded general processors were not enough - the ripeness stratum for dedicated matrix silicon. No mechanism of Catapult (FPGA fabrics, its interconnect) is in the parent, and no channel is documented. Expected refusal as multiples/era evidence, completing the L19 stratum.
candidate.source_title: Putnam et al., 'A Reconfigurable Fabric for Accelerating Large-Scale Datacenter Services', ISCA 2014

candidate.name: OpenPOWER Foundation
candidate.definition: The OpenPOWER Foundation (formed 6 Aug 2013; founders IBM, Google, Mellanox, NVIDIA, Tyan): the consortium through which IBM opened the POWER architecture for licensing and co-development. (Existing node - canonical name used.)
candidate.causal_claim: The convergence filing: the parent's whitepaper documents the POWER9+NVLink system line ('working with IBM to build even higher performance servers using Tesla V100 accelerators and Power 9 CPUs connected with NVLink') - the same opened-architecture vehicle admitted at NVLink in this session. At THIS parent the channel runs through the parent's own interconnect subsystem: the vehicle's contribution to V100 (the POWER9 pairing) reaches the chip only via the NVLink artifact that implements the pairing. Expected: MEDIATED VIA NVLink interconnect - recorded so the convergence is explicit and the edge is not double-counted at both parents.
candidate.source_title: OpenPOWER Foundation founding announcement (6 Aug 2013); NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture' whitepaper WP-08608-001_v1.1 (Aug 2017)

raw_candidates.name: Through-silicon via (TSV) manufacturing technology (IBM, 2007)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's April 2007 announcement took TSVs from laboratory to manufacturing line: vertical connections etched through thinned silicon wafers and filled with metal, sample chips in H2 2007 and production planned for 2008, after 'more than a decade of pioneering research'.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: TSV manufacturing directly enabled CoWoS's leap by supplying the vertical feed-throughs that carry signals and power from the interposer's wiring layers down to the package substrate: without a production TSV process, a silicon interposer is a wiring sheet with no way off itself.
raw_candidates.source_title: IBM, 'IBM Extends Moore's Law to the Third Dimension' (TSV manufacturing announcement, 12 Apr 2007)

raw_candidates.name: C4NP fine-pitch micro-bump solder interconnect (IBM, 2008)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's C4NP (Controlled Collapse Chip Connection - New Process) mold-transfer solder bumping, extended in 2008 to micro-bumps for 3D packaging, with 50 um-pitch bumping of 300 mm wafers demonstrated.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Fine-pitch micro-bumping directly enabled CoWoS's leap by providing the tens-of-micrometres-pitch joints that attach dies to the interposer across thousands of connections per die pair - the parent's 'chip-on-wafer' step is a micro-bump assembly.
raw_candidates.source_title: Perfecto, Shih et al., 'C4NP - solder bumps for flip chip and microbumps for 3D' (IBM extended abstract, GBC 2008)

raw_candidates.name: C4 controlled-collapse flip-chip connection (IBM, 1962)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's controlled-collapse chip connection: solder bumps on the chip face joined simultaneously to a carrier by reflow, reduced to practice in summer 1962 and later extended from the chip edge to the full area array (bump counts growing from 3 to 7,018 per chip over 40 years).
raw_candidates.causal_claim: C4 directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the originating form of the area-array solder joint the interposer's micro-bumps miniaturize; the evaluator must test whether the channel runs through C4NP rather than directly - the mediation question is the hearing.
raw_candidates.source_title: Paul A. Totta, 'Forty Years of Flip Chips with Solder Bumps' (retrospective abstract)

raw_candidates.name: IBM silicon carrier packaging (Knickerbocker et al., 2005)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's silicon-carrier system-on-package technology (CICC 2005; IBM J. Res. Dev. 49(4), 2005): multiple chips on a silicon carrier containing through-silicon vias, 50 um fine-pitch interconnection, >16x standard chip I/O and 20-100x the wiring density of traditional organic and ceramic packaging; mini-multichip modules integrating heterogeneous dies into a single 'virtual chip'.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The silicon carrier directly enabled CoWoS's leap as its single direct precursor: CoWoS is this architecture - chips on a TSV-bearing silicon carrier used as a wiring medium - productized as a foundry platform with a named first customer and a production line.
raw_candidates.source_title: Knickerbocker et al., 'Three dimensional silicon integration using fine pitch interconnection, silicon processing and silicon carrier packaging technology' (CICC 2005); IBM J. Res. Dev. 49(4), 2005

raw_candidates.name: IBM glass-ceramic multi-chip module (POWER4 'Regatta' MCM, 2001)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's high-performance glass-ceramic multichip module carrying four POWER4 chips, each attached through 7,018 flip-chip solder connections, with 1.7 million internal copper vias in co-sintered glass-ceramic (IBM J. Res. Dev. 46(6), 2002).
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The glass-ceramic MCM directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the incumbent multi-die carrier whose wiring-density ceiling the silicon interposer broke: the ancestor whose carrier material - ceramic at ~200 um pad pitch - CoWoS replaced with lithographically wired silicon.
raw_candidates.source_title: Knickerbocker et al., 'An advanced multichip module (MCM)' - POWER4 Regatta glass-ceramic MCM (IBM J. Res. Dev. 46(6), 2002)

raw_candidates.name: Xilinx Stacked Silicon Interconnect technology (2010)
raw_candidates.definition: Xilinx's SSI, announced 26 Oct 2010: multiple FPGA dies on a passive silicon interposer fabricated with TSMC technology, more than 10,000 routing connections between adjacent dies, 100x the die-to-die connectivity bandwidth-per-watt of board-level integration; first shipped in the Virtex-7 2000T on 25 Oct 2011.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: SSI directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the co-developed first application in which the platform was proven: 'five years of Xilinx research and development coupled with industry leading technology from TSMC', with TSMC's R&D chief describing the TSV-and-interposer approach in the same release. Whether SSI is the parent's ancestor, its first instance, or the parent itself under a customer name is the hearing.
raw_candidates.source_title: Xilinx, 'Xilinx Stacked Silicon Interconnect Extends FPGA Technology' (PR Newswire, 26 Oct 2010); Xilinx, 'Xilinx Ships World's Highest Capacity FPGA' - Virtex-7 2000T first shipments (PR Newswire via EDN, 25 Oct 2011)

raw_candidates.name: Rent's rule (Landman & Russo, 1971)
raw_candidates.definition: The empirical power law T = t*B^p relating a logic module's terminal count to its block count, observed in E. F. Rent's 1960 IBM internal memoranda and published by Landman & Russo (IEEE Trans. Computers C-20(12):1469-1479, Dec 1971), with Rent exponent 0.57-0.75.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Rent's rule directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the founding quantitative statement of the problem the parent answers: terminal demand grows inexorably with logic size while a package's pins cannot, so the interface must eventually move into a wiring medium of lithographic density.
raw_candidates.source_title: Landman & Russo, 'On a Pin Versus Block Relationship for Partitions of Logic Graphs', IEEE Trans. Computers C-20(12), Dec 1971

raw_candidates.name: ITRS 'More than Moore' integration agenda (2005)
raw_candidates.definition: The concept introduced in the 2005 edition of the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors: value increasingly comes from heterogeneous functional integration ('More than Moore') rather than from transistor scaling ('More Moore') alone.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: 'More than Moore' directly enabled CoWoS's leap by posing, at roadmap level, the problem the parent answers - system performance through integration of separately manufactured components - six years before the foundry platform that answered it.
raw_candidates.source_title: Graef et al., 'Positioning More Than Moore Characterization Needs and Methods Within the 2011 ITRS' (concept introduced in the 2005 ITRS edition)

raw_candidates.name: Memory wall (Wulf & McKee, 1995)
raw_candidates.definition: Wulf & McKee's 'Hitting the Memory Wall' (ACM SIGARCH Computer Architecture News 23(1):20-24, Mar 1995): processor performance improving ~60%/yr against DRAM speed ~7%/yr implies systems become wholly memory-bound.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The memory-wall diagnosis directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the named obstruction the parent's wide on-package interface answers; the evaluator must apply the Hochreiter condition - whether any CoWoS-side document derives from this diagnosis (the same candidate was refused at P100 and at NVLink on exactly that test).
raw_candidates.source_title: Wulf & McKee, 'Hitting the Memory Wall: Implications of the Obvious', ACM SIGARCH Computer Architecture News 23(1):20-24, Mar 1995

raw_candidates.name: Rent-based wire-length distribution theory (Donath, 1979)
raw_candidates.definition: W. E. Donath's Rent-based analysis of placement and average interconnection lengths (1979), turning Rent's rule into a predictive stochastic theory of wiring demand within and between logic blocks.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Donath's theory directly enabled CoWoS's leap by converting the pin problem into a computable wiring-demand distribution - the design-side instrument that states how much wiring a partition needs, and hence when a package substrate's wiring runs out.
raw_candidates.source_title: Donath's Rent-based wire-length distribution theory (1979), as surveyed in the SLIP literature on Rent's rule and interconnect prediction

raw_candidates.name: Wire-bonded stacked-die memory package (Akita Elpida 20-die MCP, 2007)
raw_candidates.definition: Akita Elpida's 2007 demonstration of 20 stacked dies inside a 1.4 mm package using wafer thinning, thin-wafer handling and low-loop wire bonding - the high-water mark of edge-wired die stacking.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The wire-bonded stack directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the incumbent it is defined against: stacking by edge wires caps connections at the die perimeter, which is precisely the constraint the interposer's area-array wiring removes.
raw_candidates.source_title: Semiconductor Digest, 'Packaging Beat: Industry leaders vie for memory-stacking bragging rights' (June 2007)

raw_candidates.name: Samsung wafer-level stack package (WSP) TSV NAND (2006)
raw_candidates.definition: Samsung's April 2006 wafer-level processed stack package: laser-drilled, copper-filled through-silicon vias stacking NAND flash dies vertically, announced for mass production from 2007.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Samsung's WSP directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the first production TSV stack - proof that TSV stacking ships - whose vertical, single-function form CoWoS's lateral, heterogeneous interposer form is defined against and extends.
raw_candidates.source_title: Phil Garrou, IFTLE 95, '3DIC - Time Flies When You're Having Fun' (Semiconductor Digest, Apr 2012)

raw_candidates.name: GDDR5 board-level memory interface (2008)
raw_candidates.definition: GDDR5, the fifth-generation graphics DRAM interface commercialized in 2008: 32-bit-per-chip channels routed across the package substrate and circuit board between a GPU and discrete memory chips.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: GDDR5 directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the defined-against incumbent memory interface: a few hundred board-routed bits is the prior state the parent's wide on-package interface displaces (refused in the defined-against role at P100 and at V100; argued fresh here, where the parent's own stored bottleneck names the substrate-routing limit).
raw_candidates.source_title: Anton Shilov, 'AMD started to work on HBM technology nearly a decade ago' (KitGuru, 2015; GDDR5 commercialized 2008)

raw_candidates.name: IBM thermal conduction module (TCM, 1981)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's thermal conduction module for the 3081 processor generation: up to roughly a hundred chips flip-chip mounted on a multilayer ceramic substrate with piston cooling - the mainframe era's high-density multichip module.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The TCM directly enabled CoWoS's leap through the failure record: ceramic multichip modules delivered wiring density at mainframe prices and never crossed into volume markets, teaching the field that the carrier's wiring medium must itself be a volume manufacturing process, not a bespoke ceramic.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fried et al., 'A VLSI Bipolar Metallization Design with Three-Level Wiring and Area Array Solder Connections' (IBM J. Res. Dev. 26(3), 1982; 3081 thermal conduction module technology)

raw_candidates.name: Intel TSV 3D-integration programme (Rattner IDF demonstration, 2005)
raw_candidates.definition: Intel's spring-2005 IDF presentation of stacked dies and wafers using through-silicon vias 'showing promise in meeting the memory bandwidth challenge' - a programme that produced demonstrations but no commercial TSV product in the following decade.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Intel's stalled programme directly enabled CoWoS's leap as adjacent negative space: the largest chipmaker's failure to commercialize TSV stacking left the production-platform step to a foundry-FPGA pair to take.
raw_candidates.source_title: Phil Garrou, IFTLE 95, '3DIC - Time Flies When You're Having Fun' (Semiconductor Digest, Apr 2012)

raw_candidates.name: Through-silicon via (TSV) manufacturing technology (IBM, 2007)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's April 2007 announcement took TSVs from laboratory to manufacturing line: vertical connections etched through thinned silicon wafers and filled with metal, sample chips in H2 2007 and production planned for 2008, after 'more than a decade of pioneering research'.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: As the wielded recipe, TSV fabrication - deep etch, insulation, copper fill, wafer thinning, via reveal - is the manufacturing process the CoWoS line runs; cross-filed under the recipe lens per the scout's cross-lens rule (duplicate of the L1 filing).
raw_candidates.source_title: IBM, 'IBM Extends Moore's Law to the Third Dimension' (TSV manufacturing announcement, 12 Apr 2007)

raw_candidates.name: Thin-wafer handling and wafer thinning process (Akita Elpida, 2007)
raw_candidates.definition: The wafer-thinning, thin-wafer handling and die-handling technology Akita Elpida cited in 2007 as the enabling craft of its 20-die stack: grinding and handling silicon at tens-of-micrometres thickness without breakage.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Thin-wafer handling directly enabled CoWoS's leap because an interposer is a thinned wafer: TSVs can only be revealed, and the carrier made package-thin, if wafers are routinely thinned and handled at production yield.
raw_candidates.source_title: Semiconductor Digest, 'Packaging Beat: Industry leaders vie for memory-stacking bragging rights' (June 2007)

raw_candidates.name: Deep reactive-ion etching (Bosch process, 1996)
raw_candidates.definition: The Bosch process (Laermer & Schilp, patented 1993-1996): alternating etch and passivation plasma cycles producing deep, near-vertical silicon trenches and holes - the standard etch for TSVs and MEMS structures.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: DRIE directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the equipment-side process that cuts the interposer's vias: high-aspect-ratio vertical holes in silicon are a plasma-etch artifact before they are a packaging feature.
raw_candidates.source_title: '3-D Integration and Through-Silicon Vias in MEMS and Microsensors', J. Micromech. Microeng./JMEMS review (2015)

raw_candidates.name: Rent's rule (Landman & Russo, 1971)
raw_candidates.definition: The empirical power law T = t*B^p relating a logic module's terminal count to its block count, observed in E. F. Rent's 1960 IBM internal memoranda and published by Landman & Russo (IEEE Trans. Computers C-20(12):1469-1479, Dec 1971), with Rent exponent 0.57-0.75.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: As the measurement model, Rent's rule is the metric that registered the wiring-demand growth the parent answers - the number every packaging generation is scored against; cross-filed under the metrics lens per the scout's cross-lens rule (duplicate of the L4 filing).
raw_candidates.source_title: Landman & Russo, 'On a Pin Versus Block Relationship for Partitions of Logic Graphs', IEEE Trans. Computers C-20(12), Dec 1971

raw_candidates.name: eWLB fan-out wafer-level packaging (Infineon, 2007)
raw_candidates.definition: Infineon's embedded wafer-level ball grid array, introduced fall 2007: dies embedded in a reconstituted wafer with thin-film redistribution wiring fanning out beyond the die footprint; licensed to ASE, STMicroelectronics and STATS ChipPAC; volume commercialization 2009/2010.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: eWLB directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the cross-field import: it proved redistribution wiring at wafer level could carry a production package's interconnect, transferring front-end-style thin-film wiring into the packaging field the parent works in.
raw_candidates.source_title: Semiconductor Digest, 'Fan-out wafer level packaging set to expand' (eWLB introduced by Infineon fall 2007; volume 2009/2010)

raw_candidates.name: MEMS through-silicon via foundry practice (Silex Microsystems, 2005)
raw_candidates.definition: Silex Microsystems, the first MEMS foundry to offer through-silicon via foundry services (polysilicon and single-crystalline TSV variants), carrying the via craft as a purchasable service in the microsystems field by the mid-2000s.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: MEMS TSV practice directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the donor field's carried craft: via formation, sidewall insulation and thin-wafer handling existed as a foundry service in MEMS while the IC-packaging field still treated TSVs as research.
raw_candidates.source_title: '3-D Integration and Through-Silicon Vias in MEMS and Microsensors', J. Micromech. Microeng./JMEMS review (2015)

raw_candidates.causal_claim: As the cross-field import, the silicon carrier is front-end silicon processing - lithography, thin films, wafer fabrication - transferred wholesale into packaging; cross-filed under the import lens per the scout's cross-lens rule (duplicate of the L2 filing).
raw_candidates.source_title: Knickerbocker et al., 'Three dimensional silicon integration using fine pitch interconnection, silicon processing and silicon carrier packaging technology' (CICC 2005); IBM J. Res. Dev. 49(4), 2005

raw_candidates.name: Shang-yi Chiang returns to TSMC to lead the packaging programme (2009)
raw_candidates.definition: Shang-yi Chiang, TSMC's former R&D senior vice president, returned to TSMC in 2009 at Morris Chang's invitation and started its advanced-packaging R&D programme (reported at roughly US$100M with a team of more than 400 engineers), from which CoWoS emerged; Chiang is the TSMC voice quoted on TSV and silicon-interposer technology in Xilinx's October 2010 SSI announcement.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Chiang's return directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the creator-lineage carrier: the person who had run the foundry's R&D was brought back to build the packaging programme, and he personally fronted the interposer technology to its first customer in the SSI announcement.
raw_candidates.source_title: Granite Firm, 'TSMC Advanced Packaging Evolution History' (2025) - secondary history; Xilinx, 'Xilinx Stacked Silicon Interconnect Extends FPGA Technology' (PR Newswire, 26 Oct 2010)

raw_candidates.name: TSMC Integrated Interconnect & Packaging programme (IIPD, 2008)
raw_candidates.definition: TSMC's Integrated Interconnect and Packaging Technology Integration Department, established 2008, and the funded advanced-packaging programme built under it from 2009 - the organizational vehicle that developed CoWoS.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The IIPD programme directly enabled CoWoS's leap as its institutional vehicle; the evaluator must apply the self-carriage test - the parent is this institution's own artifact (the Pixar-at-SL shape) - against the OpenPOWER-at-NVLink discrimination, where the admitted vehicle was external to the parent.
raw_candidates.source_title: Granite Firm, 'TSMC Advanced Packaging Evolution History' (2025) - secondary history

raw_candidates.name: ASET TSV consortium (1999)
raw_candidates.definition: The Association of Super Advanced Electronics Technologies consortium (Fujitsu, Toshiba, NEC, Oki, Renesas and others), formed in 1999 to study direct connection of chips by through-silicon vias as a pre-competitive programme.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: ASET directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the institutional ripening of TSV: a decade of consortium process work across the Japanese industry is part of what a foundry platform in 2011 could stand on.
raw_candidates.source_title: Phil Garrou, IFTLE 95, '3DIC - Time Flies When You're Having Fun' (Semiconductor Digest, Apr 2012)

raw_candidates.name: NEDO TSV development grant programme (Elpida, 2004)
raw_candidates.definition: The Japanese NEDO grant programme under which Elpida began TSV development in 2004, leading to its Cu-TSV multi-layer DRAM - development completed August 2009, sample shipments scheduled before the end of 2009, on a dedicated Hiroshima TSV line.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The NEDO programme directly enabled CoWoS's leap by funding the memory-side TSV production craft that made stacked DRAM a manufacturable component - the class of component the interposer exists to wire.
raw_candidates.source_title: Elpida Memory, 'Elpida Completes Development of Cu-TSV Multi-Layer 8-Gigabit DRAM' (31 Aug 2009)

raw_candidates.name: Xilinx-TSMC SSI co-development partnership (2010)
raw_candidates.definition: The Xilinx-TSMC collaboration behind SSI - 'five years of Xilinx research and development coupled with industry leading technology from TSMC', with assembly suppliers - announced 26 Oct 2010.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The partnership directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the junction vehicle: platform and first customer were co-developed, so the channel may be carried by this vehicle or by the SSI artifact itself; the evaluator must not count both (the NVLink partnership discrimination).
raw_candidates.source_title: Xilinx, 'Xilinx Stacked Silicon Interconnect Extends FPGA Technology' (PR Newswire, 26 Oct 2010)

raw_candidates.name: 28-nanometre reticle-limit and yield economics (2010)
raw_candidates.definition: The cost condition at the 28 nm generation: defect-free monolithic dies at the reticle limit could not supply the logic capacity leading designs demanded, making multi-die assembly the only route to beyond-Moore capacity in that generation - the SSI announcement's own framing ('capacities that otherwise wouldn't be possible in an FPGA for at least another process generation').
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The 28 nm economics directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the timeliness condition: the platform's first customer needed twice the largest feasible monolithic FPGA in that process generation, or the product did not exist.
raw_candidates.source_title: EE Times, 'Stacked and Loaded: Xilinx SSI, 28-Gbps I/O yield amazing FPGAs' (Xcell Journal cover story, Q1 2011)

candidate.name: C4NP fine-pitch micro-bump solder interconnect (IBM, 2008)
candidate.definition: IBM's C4NP (Controlled Collapse Chip Connection - New Process) mold-transfer solder bumping, extended in 2008 to micro-bumps for 3D packaging, with 50 um-pitch bumping of 300 mm wafers demonstrated.
candidate.causal_claim: Fine-pitch micro-bumping directly enabled CoWoS's leap by providing the tens-of-micrometres-pitch joints that attach dies to the interposer across thousands of connections per die pair - the parent's 'chip-on-wafer' step is a micro-bump assembly.
candidate.source_title: Perfecto, Shih et al., 'C4NP - solder bumps for flip chip and microbumps for 3D' (IBM extended abstract, GBC 2008)

candidate.name: C4 controlled-collapse flip-chip connection (IBM, 1962)
candidate.definition: IBM's controlled-collapse chip connection: solder bumps on the chip face joined simultaneously to a carrier by reflow, reduced to practice in summer 1962 and later extended from the chip edge to the full area array (bump counts growing from 3 to 7,018 per chip over 40 years).
candidate.causal_claim: C4 directly enabled CoWoS's leap as the originating form of the area-array solder joint the interposer's micro-bumps miniaturize; the evaluator must test whether the channel runs through C4NP rather than directly - the mediation question is the hearing.
candidate.source_title: Paul A. Totta, 'Forty Years of Flip Chips with Solder Bumps' (retrospective abstract)

candidate.name: Reactive ion etching (Hosokawa, Matsuzaki & Asamaki, 1974)
candidate.definition: The founding report of reactive ion etching - RF sputter-etching by fluoro-chloro-hydrocarbon gases (Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. candidate.name: Cryogenic deep silicon etching (Tachi et al., Hitachi, 1988)
candidate.definition: Tachi's team at Hitachi etched silicon in SF6 with the wafer held between -130 and -100 C (Appl. Phys. candidate.causal_claim: Filed as the direct precursor-rival the parent modified away from: cryogenic etching reached the same deep vertical geometry first, by freezing the wafer; the parent reaches it by time-multiplexing at room temperature. The parent's documents do not cite it - the two-family split is the literature's, and the hearing is on the defined-against / multiples record.

candidate.name: Single-step mixed-gas SF6/fluorocarbon etching - the 'mixed process' (c. 1988)
candidate.definition: The incumbent practice of running an etchant gas and a polymer-forming fluorocarbon simultaneously in one plasma, which Laermer & Urban describe as inefficient and difficult to control: fluorine radicals and polymer-forming monomers extinguish each other pairwise by gas-phase recombination, so rate and wall protection fight inside the same step - and the parent's own patent background describes the same failure (polymer formers in the etch plasma worsen selectivity and protect the walls non-uniformly).

candidate.name: Silicon as a mechanical material (Petersen, 1982)
candidate.definition: Petersen's review (Proc. IEEE 70(5):420-457, 1982) founded silicon micromechanics as a field: silicon as a high-precision mechanical material, its etch-based fabrication techniques, and the device programme - pressure sensors, print heads, alignment assemblies - that needed batch-fabricated mechanical structures integrated with electronics.
candidate.causal_claim: Petersen posed MEMS as a field and named etch-based micromachining as its fabrication basis; the parent's problem - deep, arbitrary, vertical structures for sensors, at production rate and selectivity - is Petersen's programme arrived at its etch bottleneck.
candidate.source_title: Petersen, 'Silicon as a mechanical material', Proc. IEEE 70(5):420-457 (1982)

candidate.name: Anisotropic wet etching of silicon in KOH/EDP (c. 1978)
candidate.definition: The incumbent silicon-structuring technology of the MEMS era: orientation-dependent wet etching in KOH or ethylenediamine-pyrocatechol, whose sidewalls are the crystal's slow (111) planes - precise and batch-capable, but geometry-dictated, mask-hungry at convex corners, and unwelcome in a CMOS fab (alkali contamination).

raw_candidates.name: C4 controlled-collapse chip connection (Miller, 1969)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's controlled-collapse chip connection: the flip-chip solder joint whose collapse is limited by glass dams defining the solderable area, published by Miller (IBM J. Res. Dev. 13(3), May 1969) with companion reliability and geometry papers in the same issue; the practice descends from IBM's summer-1962 reduction to practice of the glass-passivated solder-bump flip chip (3 bumps per chip, copper-ball standoff), and placing bumps over active device area is what created the area array.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The parent's headline is fine-pitch high-I/O chip interconnection (50 um pitch, >16x a standard chip's I/O) - an area-array solder-bump attach, which is C4's invention carried to its density limit; the carrier's reason to exist is to be the substrate that attach lands on. Filed as the practice-instantiation hearing: a practice with a unique founding artifact, judged on the parent's own documents.

raw_candidates.name: RFC 2396, Uniform Resource Identifiers: Generic Syntax (Berners-Lee, Fielding & Masinter, 1998)
raw_candidates.definition: The IETF standards-track generic syntax for URIs: 'A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a compact string of characters for identifying an abstract or physical resource' - defining absolute and relative URI references (including fragment identifiers) as one scheme-independent grammar that 'revises and replaces the generic definitions in RFC 1738 and RFC 1808'. raw_candidates.name: RFC 1738, Uniform Resource Locators (URL) (Berners-Lee, Masinter & McCahill, 1994)
raw_candidates.definition: The original URL specification: a uniform syntax for locating resources by scheme (http, ftp, gopher, ...), each scheme registering its own name space under a common grammar. The first artifact of the universally-managed identifier space the parent later borrows for namespace names - but a locator specification, superseded as the generic form by RFC 2396, whose abstract states it 'revises and replaces the generic definitions in RFC 1738 and RFC 1808'.

raw_candidates.name: Common Lisp package system (Steele, Common Lisp the Language, 1984)
raw_candidates.definition: The canonical programming-language namespace mechanism: 'One problem with earlier Lisp systems is the use of a single name space for all symbols. In large Lisp systems, with modules written by many different programmers, accidental name collisions become a serious problem. Common Lisp addresses this problem through the package system' - packages partition symbols, and a symbol in another package is referenced by a package qualifier, foo:bar. The parent's own January 1998 Note says its mechanism is 'based on the use of qualified names, similar to those long used in programming languages' - the tradition is acknowledged generically in the parent's documents; no specific language system is cited or consumed by the Recommendation.

raw_candidates.name: Colloidal-silica chemical-mechanical polishing of silicon wafers (Walsh & Herzog, Monsanto, 1965)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Walsh & Herzog practice directly enabled CMP's leap by supplying the working process the parent morphed from: Fury (2009) records that in the IBM wafer-facility development environment 'the chemical-mechanical polishing of silicon wafers morphed into the chemical-mechanical planarization process known today simply as CMP' - submicron silica abrasive in alkaline slurry on a pad, the parent's own mechanism, transferred from bare wafers to patterned device wafers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fury, Milestones in a Quarter Century of CMP, ECS Trans. 19(7) (2009); Lai, Mechanics, Mechanisms, and Modeling of the Chemical Mechanical Polishing Process, MIT PhD thesis (2001), sec. 1.3
raw_candidates.definition: Monsanto's chemical-mechanical polishing process for bare silicon wafers (Walsh & Herzog, patented 1965; polished wafers sold from late 1962): submicron silicon-dioxide abrasive in an alkaline slurry, cutting wafer finishing time from about 1.5 hours to about 5 minutes while leaving a damage-free, scratch-free surface.

raw_candidates.name: Colloidal-silica chemical-mechanical polishing of silicon wafers (Walsh & Herzog, Monsanto, 1965)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: As a wielded recipe: the slurry-and-pad finishing recipe run daily in wafer production is the procedure the 1983 East Fishkill experiments re-aimed at deposited films on device wafers.
raw_candidates.source_title: Lai, Mechanics, Mechanisms, and Modeling of the Chemical Mechanical Polishing Process, MIT PhD thesis (2001), sec. 1.3
raw_candidates.definition: Monsanto's chemical-mechanical polishing process for bare silicon wafers (Walsh & Herzog, patented 1965; polished wafers sold from late 1962): submicron silicon-dioxide abrasive in an alkaline slurry, cutting wafer finishing time from about 1.5 hours to about 5 minutes while leaving a damage-free, scratch-free surface.

raw_candidates.name: Preston's law of polishing (F. W. Preston, 1927)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Preston's law directly enabled CMP's leap by supplying the rate law (removal rate proportional to pressure times relative velocity) under which any pad-and-slurry polishing process is designed and controlled - the quantitative model CMP's process models cite from the glass-polishing literature.
raw_candidates.source_title: Preston, The theory and design of plate glass polishing machines, J. Soc. Glass Technol. 11 (1927) 214; Borucki et al., A Theory of Friction for CMP, ECS J. Solid State Sci. Technol. 14 (2025) ('the seminal theoretical paper for CMP')
raw_candidates.definition: F. W. Preston's 1927 empirical law of glass polishing: the material removal rate is proportional to the applied pressure and the relative sliding velocity (RR = Kp x P x V), with the Preston coefficient absorbing pad, abrasive and chemistry - the founding quantitative model of polishing, later adopted wholesale by CMP process modeling.

raw_candidates.name: Preston's law of polishing (F. W. Preston, 1927)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: As the metric that registers polishing: Preston's coefficient is the number by which a polishing process's removal behaviour is measured and compared.
raw_candidates.source_title: Preston, J. Soc. Glass Technol. 11 (1927) 214
raw_candidates.definition: F. W. Preston's 1927 empirical law of glass polishing: the material removal rate is proportional to the applied pressure and the relative sliding velocity (RR = Kp x P x V), with the Preston coefficient absorbing pad, abrasive and chemistry - the founding quantitative model of polishing, later adopted wholesale by CMP process modeling.

raw_candidates.name: Pitch-lap polishing of optical glass (the optics craft tradition)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The optics craft directly enabled CMP's leap by supplying the donor-field practice - a compliant lap charged with fine abrasive, worked against glass until figure and finish converge - whose pad, abrasive and dwell logic semiconductor polishing inherited.
raw_candidates.source_title: Preston, J. Soc. Glass Technol. 11 (1927); Twyman-era optical workshop practice as surveyed in CMP histories
raw_candidates.definition: The optical workshop's pitch-lap polishing craft: a pitch lap, charged with abrasive (later cerium oxide), worked against glass with controlled stroke and dwell to produce precision optical surfaces - the donor-field practice from which scientific polishing, and ultimately wafer polishing, descends.

raw_candidates.name: Cerium oxide optical polishing abrasive
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Cerium oxide directly enabled CMP's leap by proving a chemically active abrasive - one that attacks the workpiece surface chemically as it abrades - the chem-mech coupling at the parent's core.
raw_candidates.source_title: Optical polishing literature on ceria as a chemically active glass abrasive (surveyed in CMP slurry histories)
raw_candidates.definition: Cerium oxide (ceria), the optical industry's polishing abrasive from the mid-twentieth century: a rare-earth oxide whose polishing action on glass is partly chemical (surface hydrolysis and complexing), not purely abrasive - the donor-field demonstration that an abrasive can be chemically active.

raw_candidates.name: Fuller & Allison polishing etchant for III-V semiconductors (1962)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The Fuller & Allison etchant directly enabled CMP's leap by demonstrating, inside semiconductor work itself, that coupling a chemical etchant to mechanical polishing yields rapid, planar, damage-free semiconductor surfaces - the chem-mech combination the parent generalises.
raw_candidates.source_title: Fuller & Allison, A Polishing Etchant for III-V Semiconductors, J. Electrochem. Soc. 109 (1962) 880 (as catalogued in US Pat. 3,979,239 prior art)
raw_candidates.definition: Fuller & Allison's 1962 chemical-mechanical polishing etchant for III-V semiconductor crystals (halogen in organic solvent, used with mechanical polishing): rapid production of smooth, planar, damage-free GaAs/GaP surfaces by combined chemical attack and abrasion.

raw_candidates.name: Schmidt's first report of chemical-mechanical polishing (1962)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Schmidt's 1962 report is the first published report of the CMP approach in the slurry literature's own lineage survey - the documentary head of the practice the parent inherits.
raw_candidates.source_title: Morinaga, Origin and Innovations of CMP Slurry, ECS J. Solid State Sci. Technol. 13 (2024) 074006
raw_candidates.definition: The 1962 report by Schmidt identified by Morinaga (2024) as the first report on chemical-mechanical polishing: an early published demonstration, assessed by visual inspection, of combined chemical-mechanical surface finishing later validated by modern inspection.

raw_candidates.name: Loose-abrasive mechanical polishing of semiconductor wafers (1950s practice)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Mechanical wafer polishing directly enabled CMP's leap as the single direct precursor it modified: the parent is this practice with chemistry added - abrasive classification and mechanical finishing were the state of the art the chem-mech step altered.
raw_candidates.source_title: Morinaga, Origin and Innovations of CMP Slurry, ECS J. Solid State Sci. Technol. 13 (2024) 074006
raw_candidates.definition: The 1950s semiconductor wafer-finishing practice: purely mechanical polishing with classified alumina/zirconia abrasives, controlling particle size to limit damage - the direct ancestor practice that chemical-mechanical polishing modified by adding slurry chemistry.

raw_candidates.name: Chemical etch-polishing of silicon (etch-and-polish wafer finishing, c. 1960)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Etch-polishing directly enabled CMP's leap as the competing finishing route whose damage-removal logic (dissolve the damaged layer chemically) the parent fused with mechanical polishing into a single simultaneous step.
raw_candidates.source_title: Lai, Mechanics, Mechanisms, and Modeling of the Chemical Mechanical Polishing Process, MIT PhD thesis (2001), sec. 1.3
raw_candidates.definition: The wafer-finishing practice of removing the mechanically damaged surface layer by chemical etching after sawing and lapping: the chemical half of wafer finishing before the chemical and mechanical actions were combined in one polishing step.

raw_candidates.name: IBM cupric-salt chem-mech polishing improvement (Blake & Mendel, 1970)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: The IBM cupric-salt slurry work directly enabled CMP's leap as the firm's own intermediate step: a faster chem-mech silicon polish on conventional machines, inside the same company whose wafer facility produced the parent a decade later.
raw_candidates.source_title: Lai, Mechanics, Mechanisms, and Modeling of the Chemical Mechanical Polishing Process, MIT PhD thesis (2001), sec. 1.3 (citing Blake & Mendel, 1970)
raw_candidates.definition: IBM's c. 1970 improvement to chem-mech silicon polishing: a cupric-salt slurry giving higher throughput and a mirror-like finish on conventional polishing machines - an intra-IBM intermediate between Monsanto's process and the 1983 planarization experiments.

raw_candidates.name: Colloidal silica abrasive (commercial Syton/Ludox-class products)
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Colloidal silica directly enabled CMP's leap as the consumed material: submicron silica particles are the abrasive whose alkaline slurry performs the parent's removal.
raw_candidates.source_title: Morinaga, Origin and Innovations of CMP Slurry, ECS J. Solid State Sci. Technol. 13 (2024) 074006
raw_candidates.definition: Commercial colloidal silica: a stable dispersion of submicron amorphous silica particles, sold for polishing (Monsanto's Syton and DuPont's Ludox class of products) - the abrasive material semiconductor chem-mech polishing consumes.

raw_candidates.name: Phosphosilicate glass reflow planarization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Reflow planarization directly enabled CMP's leap as the incumbent it displaced: heating doped glass until it flows smooth was the standard smoothing step whose temperature and angle limits define the parent's leap by contrast.
raw_candidates.source_title: Semiconductor History Museum of Japan, Transition of flattening technique from reflow to etching back (2019)
raw_candidates.definition: Reflow planarization: depositing phosphosilicate/borophosphosilicate glass over topography and heating it (about 800-1100 C) until surface tension smooths the surface - the incumbent smoothing technique of the 1970s, limited by its thermal budget and poor smoothing of wide features.

raw_candidates.name: Spin-on glass planarization
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Spin-on glass directly enabled CMP's leap as the second incumbent: a spun-on liquid glass that pools in low areas and partially levels the surface, the partial-planarization state of the art against which the parent's global planarity is measured.
raw_candidates.source_title: PatSnap Eureka survey of spin-on glass dielectric planarization patents (1985-2007 landscape, foundations in etch-back concepts)
raw_candidates.definition: Spin-on glass (SOG) planarization: spin-coating a sol-gel silica precursor that flows into recesses, then curing it to a glassy film - a partial, local planarization technique used with etchback in the multilevel-interconnect era.

candidate.name: RFC 2141, URN Syntax (1997)

raw_candidates.name: Huygens, De Ratiociniis in Ludo Aleae (1657)
raw_candidates.definition: The first printed treatise on probability (1657, in van Schooten's Exercitationum Mathematicarum): expectation defined and computed as the fair price of a game (Prop. III), the problem of points solved for two and more players, dice propositions, and five problems left unsolved at the end - the textbook the Ars's Part I reprints with annotations.
raw_candidates.causal_claim: Huygens, De Ratiociniis (1657) directly enabled the Ars Conjectandi's leap by being its desk book and skeleton: Part I of the Ars is an annotated reprint of this tract (Bernoulli's notes run to four times the original), its central concept - expectation - is the one Bernoulli generalises, its closing five problems are the ones he solves, and the binomial distribution is first derived inside these annotations.

candidate.causal_claim: Named in the parent's own vendor record: the Altera/TSMC release (Jun 2004) says Nexsys 90nm Stratix II silicon features 'Applied Materials' production-qualified Black Diamond low-k dielectric films', and TSMC's 90nm release specifies low-k k = 2.9 or lower. Against directness: TSMC selected and qualified the film at the 0.13um generation (its own release, Jan 2001), and the film is one substitutable material inside the stack - the component discrimination and the 0.13um channel are both live.
candidate.source_title: EE Times, Applied outlines roadmap in 'low-k era' of chip making (4 Feb 2004)

candidate.name: 300 mm wafer production transition (2001)
candidate.definition: The industry's move from 200mm to 300mm wafers: SEMI-standardized wafer and factory interfaces, and the first high-volume 300mm fabs (TSMC Fab 12 among them, 2001) - roughly 2.25x the die area per wafer.
candidate.causal_claim: TSMC's 90nm release headlines '12-inch wafer production as standard' for the generation; but TSMC's 300mm production began at the 0.13um generation (Fab 12, Oct 2001), so the transition's enabling step for this parent was taken one generation earlier - a mediation candidate via the 0.13um carrier.
candidate.source_title: TSMC press release, Nexsys 90nm volume production (29 Dec 2004)

candidate.name: TSMC 0.18 µm copper process generation (2000)
candidate.definition: TSMC's 0.18-micron generation with two-layer copper interconnect (2000) - the first copper offered by a pure-play foundry, with FSG dielectric.
candidate.causal_claim: The copper line's first TSMC step; its content reaches the parent through the 0.15um and 0.13um generations, so a mediation via the 0.13um carrier is the expected record.
candidate.source_title: TSMC press release, Black Diamond selection for 0.13um copper (18 Jan 2001)

candidate.name: Intel 90 nm process generation (P1262, 2003)
candidate.definition: Intel's 90nm generation: 50nm-gate transistors, the industry's first production strained silicon, seven layers of copper, a new low-k dielectric, 300mm only - announced Aug 2002, in volume production 2003 (Prescott).
candidate.causal_claim: The era's headline parallel: a multiple for the parent's Q3 (already recorded in kind in the parent's verification via IBM's line) and the defined-against incumbent for the transistor step - Intel's documents claim the strained-silicon first; TSMC's documents claim no strained silicon at all. Multiples are verification evidence, not ancestors.
candidate.source_title: Intel press release, 90nm process unveiling (13 Aug 2002)

candidate.name: IBM 90 nm process line (2003)
candidate.definition: IBM's 90nm CMOS line on partially depleted SOI - the line that fabricated the Cell processor and partnered on the Xbox 360 Xenos eDRAM.
candidate.causal_claim: The multiple already named in the parent's own verification record ('IBM's 90 nm line fabricated the Cell and partnered on Xenos's eDRAM'); filed so the multiples evidence is on this expansion's record too. A rival's line is not a channel.
candidate.source_title: EDN, IEDM: Intel, IBM joust at 90-nm (Dec 2002)

candidate.name: Strained silicon channel engineering (2002)
candidate.definition: Enhancing carrier mobility by straining the transistor channel lattice (SiGe source/drain stressors and SiGe virtual substrates): Intel's production implementation at 90nm claimed 10-20% drive-current gain.
candidate.causal_claim: The era's headline transistor step - at a rival. For TSMC it is documented negative space: EE Times (Apr 2002) records TSMC 'investigating' strained silicon, SOI and high-k for future nodes, and no TSMC document claims it for the 90nm generation. Defined-against / not-adopted; judged on documents, firm-scoped.
candidate.source_title: Intel press release, 90nm process unveiling (13 Aug 2002)

candidate.name: Partially depleted SOI CMOS (IBM 90 nm line, 2002)
candidate.definition: IBM's 90nm transistor path: partially depleted silicon-on-insulator CMOS, presented at IEDM 2002 as IBM's answer at the node.
candidate.causal_claim: The node's other divergent path: IBM took SOI, Intel took strain, TSMC took neither - its 90nm is bulk CMOS. A parallel the parent is defined against by omission; no consumption channel exists.
candidate.source_title: EDN, IEDM: Intel, IBM joust at 90-nm (Dec 2002)

candidate.name: ITRS technology roadmap, 2001 edition (2001)
candidate.definition: The International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors' 2001 edition: the industry's consensus target tables, including the 90nm node's scheduled year and parameter targets.
candidate.causal_claim: A requirement specification: the roadmap posed the node's targets, but a specification is not a consumed mechanism (the standing discipline: IAM HMM, NTRS, ITRS refused at other parents) unless the child's text implements its clauses as its mechanism - TSMC's releases cite their own measured deltas against 0.13um, not roadmap clauses.
candidate.source_title: TSMC press release, Nexsys 90nm volume production (29 Dec 2004)

candidate.name: Bohr, Interconnect scaling - the real limiter to high performance ULSI (1995)
candidate.definition: Mark Bohr's IEDM 1995 analysis: with constant materials, interconnect RC delay degrades 2x per generation while gate delay improves - 'new conductor and dielectric materials... will be needed' - the named diagnosis of the interconnect bottleneck.
candidate.causal_claim: The diagnosis the copper/low-k complex answers. Under the Hochreiter condition a diagnosis is ancestry only if the parent's documents derive from it; TSMC's 90nm documents derive from its own 0.13um qualification record, and the diagnosis was answered at the damascene step a decade earlier. Filed so the L5 question is judged, not skipped.
candidate.source_title: Bohr, Interconnect Scaling - The Real Limiter to High Performance ULSI, IEDM 1995, pp. 241-244

candidate.name: Dennard constant-field scaling (1974)
candidate.definition: Dennard et al.'s scaling rules (IEEE JSSC, 1974): shrink dimensions and voltages together and delay, power density and energy per operation scale predictably - the theory every process generation of the era executed.
candidate.causal_claim: The presupposed theory of the parent's generation targets (35% speed, 60% power vs 0.13um are scaling-line claims); no TSMC document cites it, and it was refused at DELTA under the same discipline. Filed for the L10/L1 theory question.
candidate.source_title: Bohr, Interconnect Scaling - The Real Limiter to High Performance ULSI, IEDM 1995, pp. 241-244

candidate.name: 157 nm F2 lithography programme (abandoned 2003)
candidate.definition: The industry's planned post-193nm wavelength: F2 excimer lithography at 157nm, pursued through the late 1990s and abandoned around 2003 (Intel's withdrawal, July 2003) over CaF2 lens and pellicle failures.
candidate.causal_claim: Negative space: the era's failed next step. Its collapse redirected the industry to extending 193nm - but at this parent the 193nm line was already the production inheritance, and no TSMC document derives the 90nm generation from the 157nm failure.
candidate.source_title: Intel press release, 90nm process unveiling (13 Aug 2002)

candidate.name: Aluminum interconnect with SiO2 dielectric (incumbent BEOL, 1997)
candidate.definition: The pre-copper back-end: subtractively etched aluminum alloy lines in silicon dioxide - the incumbent stack whose RC delay and electromigration limits defined the interconnect problem.
candidate.causal_claim: The defined-against incumbent: the parent's BEOL is measured against it, but it was displaced at TSMC's 0.18-0.13um generations, not at 90nm; an incumbent the lineage already replaced is not this parent's enabler.
candidate.source_title: Bohr, Interconnect Scaling - The Real Limiter to High Performance ULSI, IEDM 1995, pp. 241-244

candidate.name: Ta/TaN copper barrier liner (1997)
candidate.definition: The tantalum/tantalum-nitride liner that keeps electroplated copper from diffusing into the dielectric - a necessary constituent of every damascene layer.
candidate.causal_claim: A component of the damascene complex, refused as a component at damascene's own expansion (the barrier-liner precedent); the same discrimination applies here, one level further down.
candidate.source_title: TSMC press release, Nexsys 90nm volume production (29 Dec 2004)

candidate.name: Copper electrochemical deposition (Novellus SABRE, 1998)
candidate.definition: Electrochemical plating of copper into damascene trenches (Novellus's SABRE tool, 1998; technology imported from the plating industry) - the deposition half of the damascene flow.
candidate.causal_claim: A component of the damascene flow (deposit, then polish back): consumed inside the parent's BEOL, but as a constituent of the mediated damascene candidate, not as a separable enabling step of this generation.
candidate.source_title: TSMC press release, Nexsys 90nm volume production (29 Dec 2004)

candidate.name: Optical proximity correction and phase-shift masks (2000)
candidate.definition: Resolution enhancement techniques for sub-wavelength printing: model-based OPC (mask shapes pre-distorted by EDA software) and phase-shift masks, in production use from the 130nm generation.
candidate.causal_claim: Named in the parent's own release ('scanning lithography with OPC and phase-shift masks'); but RET was the established recipe of the preceding generations, wielded through EDA tooling - a recipe component whose enabling step belongs to the lithography line, not to this generation.
candidate.source_title: TSMC press release, Nexsys 90nm volume production (29 Dec 2004)

candidate.name: 193 nm ArF lithography (2001)
candidate.definition: Argon-fluoride excimer step-and-scan lithography at 193nm: the wavelength that printed the critical layers of the 130nm and 90nm generations.
candidate.causal_claim: The parent's critical layers print at 193nm (its release says 'scanning lithography'; Intel's parallel release documents the 248+193nm mix at the node). candidate.name: ASML TWINSCAN ArF scanner (2001)

candidate.name: Applied Materials (supplier institution, 1998)
candidate.definition: The equipment and materials supplier whose Black Diamond film, BLOk barrier and Producer/Centura platforms sit inside the parent's BEOL.

candidate.name: Pure-play foundry model (TSMC, 1987)
candidate.definition: TSMC's founding form (1987): a merchant fab selling process capacity to fabless designers - the organizational invention the parent is an instance of.
candidate.causal_claim: The parent's own business form: era condition and self-carriage. The foundry model explains why a merchant 90nm generation exists at all, but it is the parent's maker's form, not a consumed enabler of the generation's technical step.
candidate.source_title: TSMC press release, Nexsys 90nm volume production (29 Dec 2004)

candidate.name: Morris Chang (1987)
candidate.definition: TSMC's founder: carried the pure-play foundry concept from his TI/GI career into TSMC's 1987 founding and led the company through the 0.13um-90nm generations.
candidate.causal_claim: A person as the lineage's continuity is formation: Chang carried the foundry concept, but no separable artifact of his is consumed by the 90nm generation's technical step; the institutional form is filed separately at L21/L22.

candidate.name: SEMI 300 mm wafer standards (1998)
candidate.definition: The SEMI standards fixing 300mm wafer dimensions, flatness, and factory interface (SEMI E-series/M-series, late 1990s) - the coordination layer of the wafer-size transition.
candidate.causal_claim: A specification behind the transition: the standard is the requirement's form; the production transition itself is filed under its own name and judged on the Fab 12 record.

candidate.name: TSMC process design kit and design collateral (0.13 µm, 2001)
candidate.definition: The design rules, models and libraries a foundry ships so customers can design into a generation - the interface layer of the Nexsys offering, established at the 0.13um generation.
candidate.causal_claim: The programmability-layer analogue for a process parent: the PDK makes the process usable by designers, but it is the generation's customer interface (a specification), not the enabling step of the generation itself; and its operative form here descends from the 0.13um collateral.
