candidate.causal_claim: Filed to log the foreclosure: DTSS is dated the parent's own year (1964) and is dropped by the same-year bound; its communication-files facility (1967) postdates the memo outright (filed separately under L3).
candidate.source_title: McIlroy, Communication files for interprocess IO in the Dartmouth Time-Sharing System

raw_candidates.name: Cook, Shade Trees (1984)
raw_candidates.definition: Cook's 1984 procedural shading model: surface appearance computed by a tree of procedures evaluated per point - the founding document of procedural shading, already in this graph as the RenderMan line's head.

raw_candidates.name: Perlin noise / procedural texture synthesis as the shader workload (1985)
raw_candidates.definition: Perlin's 1985 image-synthesizer work made procedural texture the canonical thing a shader computes - the workload class the parent's pixel stage exists to run at frame rate.

raw_candidates.name: The rendering equation (Kajiya, 1986)
raw_candidates.definition: Kajiya's 1986 integral formulation of image synthesis - the theory the shading computation approximates; the parent presupposes it without implementing it.

raw_candidates.name: REYES rendering architecture (Cook, Carpenter & Catmull, 1987)
raw_candidates.definition: Pixar's REYES architecture (1987): the render-time pipeline of the RenderMan system, whose shading stage the real-time line miniaturized - already in this graph.

raw_candidates.name: Stanford Real-Time Shading Language - RTSL (Proudfoot et al., 2001)
raw_candidates.definition: The Stanford real-time shading system (Proudfoot, Mark, Tzvetkov, Hanrahan, 2001): a RenderMan-like shading language compiled to single-chip GPUs - in this graph already, edged to HLSL at 6.0.

raw_candidates.name: Lastra, Molnar, Olano & Wang, Real-time Programmable Shading (I3D, 1995)
raw_candidates.definition: The UNC group's 1995 symposium paper: the first published design for programmable shading at interactive rates, from simulation of the PixelFlow machine - the PixelFlow paper's own cited predecessor.

raw_candidates.name: A shading language on graphics hardware: the PixelFlow shading system (Olano & Lastra, 1998)
raw_candidates.definition: Olano & Lastra (SIGGRAPH 1998): the first system to support a shading language in real time, on UNC's PixelFlow multicomputer; its language pfman is modelled on Pixar's RenderMan shading language. Bill Mark's Cg foreword names Olano's PixelFlow compiler as his own inspiration.

raw_candidates.name: Direct3D 8 / DirectX 8 shader model 1.x (2000)
raw_candidates.definition: DirectX 8 (November 2000): Direct3D gains programmable vertex shaders (vs_1_0/1_1) and pixel shaders (ps_1_0-1_4) at assembly level, on the device/capability-bits architecture - the parent's own prior version, whose conversion the D3D9 SDK documents.

raw_candidates.name: PixelFlow parallel graphics multicomputer (Molnar et al., 1992)
raw_candidates.definition: UNC's PixelFlow (SIGGRAPH 1992): a parallel multicomputer rendering by image composition - the machine built to make programmable shading run at frame rate, host of the pfman system.

raw_candidates.name: SGI RealityEngine graphics supercomputer (1992)
raw_candidates.definition: SGI's RealityEngine (1992): the high-end fixed-function pipeline as a room-sized product - the performance pole the PC line chased, with no user programmability at any stage.

raw_candidates.name: Microsoft Talisman tiled-rendering architecture (1996)
raw_candidates.definition: Microsoft's Talisman project (1996-98): a tiled/chunked rendering architecture and API effort inside Microsoft that never shipped as a product - the road Direct3D did not take, from the parent's own firm.

raw_candidates.name: Direct3D Immediate Mode / Reality Lab lineage (1996)
raw_candidates.definition: The original Direct3D (DirectX 2/3, 1996), built on RenderMorphics' Reality Lab engine Microsoft acquired in 1995: the API line's founding artifact, six versions behind the parent.

raw_candidates.name: 3dfx Glide API (1996)
raw_candidates.definition: 3dfx's Glide (with the Voodoo Graphics chip, 1995-96): the proprietary fixed-function API that defined PC 3D gaming in the late 1990s; 3dfx ceased support in Feb 2001 and filed for bankruptcy in Oct 2002, weeks before the parent shipped.

raw_candidates.name: OpenGL (Segal & Akeley specification, 1992)
raw_candidates.definition: SGI's OpenGL 1.0 (1992): the cross-platform state-machine graphics API, Direct3D's defined-against rival for a decade - the parent's stored prior_state names it ('OpenGL 1.x with vendor extensions').

raw_candidates.name: RenderMan Shading Language (Hanrahan & Lawson, 1990)
raw_candidates.definition: Pixar's RenderMan shading language (Hanrahan & Lawson, 1990): the offline shading language whose model every real-time language copied - already in this graph, edged to RTSL at 7.5.

raw_candidates.name: Hanrahan & Haeberli, Direct WYSIWYG painting and texturing on 3-D shapes (1990)
raw_candidates.definition: Hanrahan & Haeberli (SIGGRAPH 1990): interactive 3D painting on SGI hardware - the interactive-graphics culture of the laboratory whose shading line (Hanrahan) runs through RTSL to the parent's language.

raw_candidates.name: The OpenGL extension registry mechanism (vendor/EXT/ARB extensions)
raw_candidates.definition: OpenGL's extension architecture: new hardware features exposed as named extensions (vendor, EXT, then ARB) - the mechanism by which programmable stages first reached OpenGL applications, and the fragmentation the parent's capability-bits system answers.

raw_candidates.name: ARB vertex program extension (GL_ARB_vertex_program lineage, 2001)
raw_candidates.definition: The OpenGL ARB's assembly vertex-program extension work (ratified 2002 from 2001 drafts): the rival API's own programmable-stage mechanism, developed in parallel with the parent's shader models.

raw_candidates.name: John Carmack's .plan statements on API fragmentation and programmability (1996-97)
raw_candidates.definition: Carmack's public .plan files (1996-97) grading OpenGL against Direct3D and demanding programmable hardware: the era's most-read problem statement from its most influential game programmer - a diagnosis the platform vendors answered, not a mechanism any of them consumed.

raw_candidates.name: The Fahrenheit unification project (Microsoft-SGI, 1997)
raw_candidates.definition: The joint Microsoft-SGI Fahrenheit project (announced 17 Dec 1997): a common architecture evolving from Direct3D, DirectDraw and OpenGL - collapsed by 1999, only its XSG scene graph shipped (2000) and was discontinued. The unification problem it posed was answered by the parent unilaterally.

raw_candidates.name: Fixed-function pipeline exhaustion as documented in the GeForce 3 design (Lindholm et al., 2001)
raw_candidates.definition: Lindholm et al.'s GeForce 3 paper (2001): the hardware side's own statement that fixed-function lighting had run out - the vertex engine's private instruction set 'exposed to the application developer', coinciding with DirectX 8 and OpenGL's vertex extensions.

raw_candidates.name: ATI Radeon 8500 / pixel shader 1.4 line (2001)
raw_candidates.definition: ATI's Radeon 8500 (2001) carried pixel shader 1.4 - a more capable fragment model than NVIDIA's 1.3 - inside DirectX 8.1: the multiple that made the parent's unified 2.0 model a negotiation between two vendors' dialects.

raw_candidates.name: Cg, the NVIDIA-Microsoft shading language (2002)
raw_candidates.definition: NVIDIA's Cg (specification announced 13 June 2002; compiler 1.0 released 20 Dec 2002, the parent's own release window): designed in collaboration with Microsoft, whose implementation of the same language shipped as HLSL inside DirectX 9 - the parent's coeval twin, expected to be calendar-foreclosed.

raw_candidates.name: High-Level Shading Language (HLSL, 2002)
raw_candidates.definition: Microsoft's HLSL: the C-like shading language shipped as part of DirectX 9 (beta May 2002), designed with NVIDIA as the twin of Cg - in this graph already as a node (edged to the D3D10 effort at 6.5); at this parent it is both same-year and the parent's own component.

raw_candidates.name: Unified shader architecture (as later realized in Direct3D 10)

raw_candidates.name: General-purpose computation on GPUs (GPGPU, as a named practice)
raw_candidates.definition: The parent has no compute model: its shaders are bound to the graphics pipeline, and the GPGPU practice that grew on top of it (2002-04) is a use discovered against the API's grain - a descendant practice, filed for the negative space.

raw_candidates.name: A geometry-shader stage
raw_candidates.definition: The parent's pipeline has no geometry stage between vertex and rasterization - added only by its child. Filed as negative space; not an ancestor.

raw_candidates.name: Consumer 3D accelerator price collapse (Voodoo/RIVA/TNT line, 1996-99)
